This game was great, and I say 'was'. For every update released on TF2, I get more remorseful of having put money into it.
It's been nothing but downhill since. First the Gun Mettle Update which tried to imitate CS:GO's skin system (I mean, it was okay, I guess... but TF2 should be unique in it's own way, this seemed more like a way to gross more profit from it's consumers), then the "Meet your Match" update which, in my opinion, was what really made this game slip down a steep cliffside because it removed a lot of features from TF2 and replaced them with a more gimmicky "Esports" themed interface (which almost nobody asked for).
And now, the latest "Pyro Update" or also known as the "Jungle Inferno" update nailed the final peice into the coffin for me. I'm not counting the instability of the game's services (like the item server or matchmaker). It just doesn't appeal anymore.
The game feels 'broken'. The spirit of the game disappeared kind of broken. Gameplay seemed so much more enjoyable back then. Valve seeming to put life support on it, and it doesn't help that the community is hating everything Valve does to it (so ultimately this would confuse developers there).
The people not finding this review helpful proves my point on this, because this would mean a portion of the community seems satisfied with how TF2 is coming along and disagrees with how I feel about how TF2 is slowly dying in it's own foundation, and if you look at the forums right now there's evidence that people are complaining about the update (the attitude though is unecessary with the allcaps n' all...). The community cannot make up their mind (very mixed).
As long as this game remains free (as it will forever), it will have players, and it will die a slow painful death.
TL;DR
This poor game, I feel bad for it. Just put it out of its misery.

To start off, let me just say that TF2 is really fun. But.
This update, meet your match. Won't be reverted, it WILL NOT be reverted. This follows my experience in watching game devs, they believe it will work if they simply give it time.
There was a hell of a fun in TF2, but, in the end. It was a casual game the hid some competitve elements, however it was never designed, as a whole, to be competitve. One person *could* replace 3-4 if those people decided to conga at spawn and while you could say community servers now exist for that, no they don't. A community server will never replace a pub.
If you wanted a community server, you could search for it. If you wanted a pub, you could search for it and if you wanted matchmaker, you could search for it if the devs had done this update right.
What it attempts to do, is push TF2 into a competitve light. Newsflash Valve, the streaming section in TF2 was used by barely anyone and provided nothing but an annoyance. Matchmaker is a good idea, don't get me wrong, but it's also a horrible idea simple because it's replaced pub matches. You want to quit? 20 minute ban that goes up and up. Crap map? 20 minute wait. You want X gamemode only? nope, have to choose at least two gamemodes. If I wanted to matchmake in CTF or something, on such and such map, you bloody well better let me choose.
The upside is that after matchmaker has been out for a while, the problems in relation to skill ratio will weed themselves out. But if I just get home from work, want to screw around in a match with a map I can actually pick, one I can kill people in one minute, focus the objective the other and conga next to some friendly's the next, one I can offclass in without worrying about "point drain," then why is it that I have to go to someone elses server that is probbaly running something cancerous such as minecraft or alltalk just so I get squeakers♥♥♥♥♥♥talking one another.
I'm going to play the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of matchmaker, but I'm ♥♥♥♥ing angry that such a big slip up could be made. Pub's and "casual" could very easily both be run at the same time and you can't tell me they don't have enough money since servers cost something, MvM often has 40+ servers free of action even at peak hours in the AUS region, one of the most expensive regions.

True, they can. But I think those servers will be few and far. Not to mention the ads.

Why. Why did you change the age old formula that we all knew and loved?

Martin Luther King Jr. John Lennon. JFK. Team Fortress 2. What do all of these have in common? They've been murdered. Killed. Reduced to a lifeless corpse. King, Lennon and JFK were ended by assassins. Team Fortress 2 was killed by the newest update. Let me tell you how this beautiful, amazing game was killed.
Pros:
New taunts (The Carlton is my favorite.)
New guns for either the Pyro or Heavy.
Minmode
Cons:
You get penalized for leaving Casual mid-game. Yes. CASUAL. (I'll talk about that more later)
Custom HUDs are no longer usable.
The matchmaking takes 30 minutes or more (Hooboy, I'm gonna rant about this)
Teleporters are less expensive
They nerfed the Pyro. Hard. (DPS is terrible. He's barely a threat anymore. Not even the Phlog can save him)
Now. Let me tell you in detail how much of a dumb idea it is to make you wait if you leave mid game in casual. 1.) It's CASUAL. 2.) IT'S CASUAL. 3.) IT'S GODDAMN CASUAL. 4.) What if something happens to your internet? What if something abrupt and unexpected forces you to leave?
Matchmaking. The reason smurfing in CS:GO isn't as bad as it could be is because of one thing. The price tag. Every single time you want to make a smurf account, you have to pay for another copy of the game. But with TF2, it's free. So all you need to do to make a smurf account is to make another account, download the game, and buy the cheapest thing off of the Mann Co. Store. Plus, the whole skill based matchmaking is a terrible concept. You could have played this game for over 5000 hours, and still be meh. You could then go into the game, and be matched with people who have played similar hours, but these people are amazing at the game. "Oh, but to play competitive, you have to buy a ticket" No, you actually don't. All you have to do is link your phone number to Steam, and you're ready to go.
I started playing shortly before the MannConomy update, and it breaks my heart to not recommend TF2. Most of my friends on Steam are from TF2. Hell, one of my best friends that I'm seriously considering travelling overseas just to stay with for a few months, was met on TF2. But now that Valve is trying to compete with Overwatch, even though if they stayed the same, Overwatch would have died anyways, I have to click the thumbs down. Goodbye, Team Fortress 2. I loved you. I loved seeing you grow. But I have to let go.

Don't get me wrong, competitive matchmaking IS a great thing, but they forced casual play into something that is not casual at all. There is no team balance, which is bad. EDIT: There was a little update today, hot-fixing most of the issues with casual. There is no abandon penalty now, but teams remain unbalanced, because there is no auto balance either. 10-20 minute wait for a game to connect is a bug, and will be fixed in next patch. You can choose one game mode yet cannot choose maps you want to play. I hope community servers will get revived, now the game is less enjoyable than it was before this update, but the real problems are fixed and Valve listens, even when it does not reply. And that's good.

I mean, launch the game, hop into a server, enjoy and pub for about a bit, and that was it, yet it was pretty fun regardless.
With the new update, I can't be arsed to wait 10+ minutes just to join a casual game (which replaced pubs) only to find myself feeling frustrated as I can't play the maps I specifically want, the gamemodes I specifically enjoy nor enjoy a full game of payload, not having the game getting cut off just because the other team made it significantly further than ours in the previous round
At first glance, Overwatch felt like it's copying TF2, but it turns out the game plays so much differently with the use of abilities and ultimates, but right now, it feels like TF2 is copying Overwatch's competitive formula.
I don't really enjoy the formula in Overwatch, nor do I enjoy it in TF2
I'm hoping Valve brings back pubs, or at least bring improve the whole casual/ranked formula by making waiting times shorter, improving the gamemodes, allowing custom HUDS, etc, but for now I think I'm going to wait and see if things get better, if not worst

I have played this game for a lot of years. During that time I have met a lot of great people, and also quite a bunch of people who I wish I'd never meet.
Unfortunately, I've joined the scene quite late as I first started playing this in January 2011, a point where the game was still optimized and still fun. As years passed by I've seen the game go downhill more and more each update. The performance of the game was getting worse and the content Valve kept adding was not contributing to the game one single bit, if anything it just killed more and more frames on a lot of machines, no matter how powerful they are.
The latest update "Meet your Match" was the final straw for me. Them replacing pub servers with "Casual" servers, which are basically pubs with a competitive setting really didn't do it for me. Competitive could've kept this game alive if they implemented this years ago. If you ask me, they are way too late with doing this and I personally do not see a future for this game anymore.
If anyone would ask me, I would not recommend Team Fortress 2 to anyone. Even though I have never played Overwatch, I'd say that game holds a much greater future than TF2 would ever achieve.
EDIT: Well then, to my surprise they're actually doing something about this whole issue. Way to go, I guess?
EDIT 2: My opinion still stands. This game is nothing but a broken pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥
EDIT 3: I moved over to Overwatch, much better game than TF2. Get it now, seriously.

text:
Why. Why did you change the age old formula that we all knew and loved?
Issues:
1. Match making takes way too long compared to being able to manually select games.
2. Disabled the voting system in casual.
3. Unable to select specific game modes.
4. As soon as the game finished I was taken back to the mode select screen to wait another 5 minutes.
I just played an entirely one sided game, and there was no option to scramble teams for balance. Simply not fun or fair or even manageable anymore.

Martin Luther King Jr. John Lennon. JFK. Team Fortress 2. What do all of these have in common? They've been murdered. Killed. Reduced to a lifeless corpse. King, Lennon and JFK were ended by assassins. Team Fortress 2 was killed by the newest update. Let me tell you how this beautiful, amazing game was killed.
Pros:
New taunts (The Carlton is my favorite.)
New guns for either the Pyro or Heavy.
Minmode
Cons:
You get penalized for leaving Casual mid-game. Yes. CASUAL. (I'll talk about that more later)
Custom HUDs are no longer usable.
The matchmaking takes 30 minutes or more (Hooboy, I'm gonna rant about this)
Teleporters are less expensive
They nerfed the Pyro. Hard. (DPS is terrible. He's barely a threat anymore. Not even the Phlog can save him)
Now. Let me tell you in detail how much of a dumb idea it is to make you wait if you leave mid game in casual. 1.) It's CASUAL. 2.) IT'S CASUAL. 3.) IT'S GODDAMN CASUAL. 4.) What if something happens to your internet? What if something abrupt and unexpected forces you to leave?
Matchmaking. The reason smurfing in CS:GO isn't as bad as it could be is because of one thing. The price tag. Every single time you want to make a smurf account, you have to pay for another copy of the game. But with TF2, it's free. So all you need to do to make a smurf account is to make another account, download the game, and buy the cheapest thing off of the Mann Co. Store. Plus, the whole skill based matchmaking is a terrible concept. You could have played this game for over 5000 hours, and still be meh. You could then go into the game, and be matched with people who have played similar hours, but these people are amazing at the game. "Oh, but to play competitive, you have to buy a ticket" No, you actually don't. All you have to do is link your phone number to Steam, and you're ready to go.
I started playing shortly before the MannConomy update, and it breaks my heart to not recommend TF2. Most of my friends on Steam are from TF2. Hell, one of my best friends that I'm seriously considering travelling overseas just to stay with for a few months, was met on TF2. But now that Valve is trying to compete with Overwatch, even though if they stayed the same, Overwatch would have died anyways, I have to click the thumbs down. Goodbye, Team Fortress 2. I loved you. I loved seeing you grow. But I have to let go.

I mean, launch the game, hop into a server, enjoy and pub for about a bit, and that was it, yet it was pretty fun regardless.
With the new update, I can't be arsed to wait 10+ minutes just to join a casual game (which replaced pubs) only to find myself feeling frustrated as I can't play the maps I specifically want, the gamemodes I specifically enjoy nor enjoy a full game of payload, not having the game getting cut off just because the other team made it significantly further than ours in the previous round
At first glance, Overwatch felt like it's copying TF2, but it turns out the game plays so much differently with the use of abilities and ultimates, but right now, it feels like TF2 is copying Overwatch's competitive formula.
I don't really enjoy the formula in Overwatch, nor do I enjoy it in TF2
I'm hoping Valve brings back pubs, or at least bring improve the whole casual/ranked formula by making waiting times shorter, improving the gamemodes, allowing custom HUDS, etc, but for now I think I'm going to wait and see if things get better, if not worst
On an unrelated note, TF2 right now seems to be running absolutely terrible compared to the previous updates

Edit 5: After over 2 months Valve finally added in a "stay in the damn game I queued 5 minutes for" option. Sadly, the community has become very conditioned by the previous, garbage system into leaving the match as soon as it is over. Gone are the days that you could marathon a map.
I have played TF2 for close to 7 years. Over this time I have seen many improvements and many steps backwards. As of today, 7/8/16, Valve managed to kill some of the best portions of the game in order to try and compete with recent other games (Overwatch). Lets go over some  things.
-
Took them half a month to fix something that was previously in the game. "Valve time"
-
-
-
-
Queues are getting better, I've gotten into a few games with 5 minute waits. Good luck trying to queue into an obscure game type though...
-
-
It took 2 months to fix this. 2 months.
Would I recommend this game in its current state? No. It is not as accessible or fun as it used to be. Competitive should have been an addition, not a replacement for the existing structure. TF2 was never about winning, it was about fun, and much of that has been lost in this pseudo-competitive environment that was thrust upon us.
I adore TF2. It used to be a fun, absurd hat-based combat simulator. It no longer feels like that.
But hey, it's free...
Edit: Let's hope that I can continue to cross things off this list.
Edit 2: The issue remains that around 2 years ago, the Quickplay update killed off many community servers. Quickplay allowed new users to QUICKLY find a game on the map they desired and enjoy a no-hassle, vanilla experience. This new update has made finding a game a pain. It is clunky, and far from the "upgrade" that Valve toted. If you do not wish to play the "Casual" game mode, you must comb through piles of crap servers to try and find one without annoying adverts, plugins, and abusive mods. Good luck finding ones that aren't running stupid cp_Orange_x3 (I hate that map). Valve has made a blog post mentioning that they will change certain aspects, but until the issues are fixed, the vanilla experience is not as accessible to new players or enjoyable to long-time veterans.

[Disclaimer] This review is mostly unbiased so if something offends you about this review, don't complain. I am the person who says that Overwatch and TF2 can co-exist and I stand by that dammit!
As you can see I have plenty of hours in this game, and about 2x as many on my other 2 steam accounts, You may ask why I say I don't reccomend this game... After seeing this newest update with the competitive its changed my mind. Its not the competitive that I'm mad at, its unnessesary changes like the design on the jumpers its been on a downward spiral ever since EotL... anyways lets get into this.
[Pros]
Team Fortress 2 is a fairly easy game to pick up, and it has a high skill cap
-For instance; Rocket Jumping basics can be learned quickly, but it is hard to completely master it to be like STAR_ or Muselk
It has such amazing mechanics that everyone can enjoy and many people turned away from CoD and other fps games just because its so much fun.
-Most of the people in my friend list that play tf2 left their old fps games for this simplistic, pixar-like game
The classes can all be fun to play, and have various styles of play to suit pretty much everyone.
- No one can deny that fact
The soundtrack for the game is amazing!
I like how even if you don't know how to play the game very well, you can still do decent, and you can get ready help from others
-I will cover more of the community on the cons
I love how the characters have... well... charater, rather than it just being a generic blood bath point and click
[Cons]
Pyros require very little skill to pick up and play... I know its supposed to be for newer players, but all you have to do is walk forward and people die
-airblasting pyros are ok in my book...
There have been a lot of unnessary nerfs recently...
-For instance the previous dead ringer didn't really need a nerf, same with the iron bomber and loch n load.
They keep buffing the phlogistinator and never nerf it
-Foot pyro was created because of that weapon, it takes away your airblast in exchange for almost full crits and invulin at command... if you see this valve, NERF IT!
The community is becoming cancer because of 10 year old CoD kids, hackers, and overall elitist ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.
-That is just a brief description of the entirety of the toxic community there are still nice people though..
The game is getting kind of old because no new weapons, just hats and taunts, that in a few weeks everyone will forget about.. we need something new.
-Other than competitive, which is hacker-ridden *fyi*
There is no real compensation to playing medic, no one likes to play medic except a select few people like myself.
-Its a fun class, but no one knows how to use him correctly, they either charge forward or they pocket a heavy
Tying in with that previous note.. Medics need to heal more than just heavies and pyros... the only reason why people do it is because they don't want to take a chance of losing.
Also since the EotL update they have been nerfing everything except pyro and buffing it...
-Now with this update I'm even more♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥at valve... they buffed him and are thinking of buffing him again. Why can't they do both heavy and pyro, are they going on vacation or something, or are they on a schedule...

Would I recommend this game in its current state? No. It is not as accessible or fun as it used to be. Competitive should have been an addition, not a replacement for the existing structure. TF2 was never about winning, it was about fun, and much of that has been lost in this pseudo-competitive environment that was thrust upon us.
I adore TF2. It used to be a fun, absurd hat-based combat simulator. It no longer feels like that.
But hey, it's free...
Edit: Let's hope that I can continue to cross things off this list.
Edit 2: The issue remains that around 2 years ago, the Quickplay update killed off many community servers. Quickplay allowed new users to QUICKLY find a game on the map they desired and enjoy a no-hassle, vanilla experience. This new update has made finding a game a pain. It is clunky, and far from the "upgrade" that Valve toted. If you do not wish to play the "Casual" game mode, you must comb through piles of crap servers to try and find one without annoying adverts, plugins, and abusive mods. Good luck finding ones that aren't running stupid cp_Orange_x3 (I hate that map). Valve has made a blog post mentioning that they will change certain aspects, but until the issues are fixed, the vanilla experience is not as accessible to new players or enjoyable to long-time veterans.

Oh how the mighty have fallen.
TF2 was a game where I spent countless hours talking, playing, and generally have a fun time. About 99% of my friends on my friends list including my close and best friends were met through TF2. TF2 has charming characters with funny and interesting personalities. The backstory is funny and the story was interesting. I have fond memories of spending late nights slicing heads off as a Demoman on Nucleus or market gardening people as Soldier on Hightower. Every day I'd come home and play. The multitude of glitches such as the Halloween doomsday glitch where you could leave the map or the engineer crit glitch. This game was a mess and that was what I fell in love with, a mess, an organized mess. The game was fun even though it wasn’t very balanced with the pyro and the old reserve and all, but it was still fun.
The fun lasted a while and stayed strong, that was until the last few months or so. Within the last 6 months I saw this game turn from my most played game to one of my least played (well also the fact that Overwatch came out), and to me that is sad because it was one of my favorites. They killed the pyro class making the pyro twenty times less effective at his job and severely decreasing his dps. I remember when pyros were a threat, now they are the worst class in the game. But that is not what did it for me, I could handle the pyro being bad. This update was the star that broke the camel's back.
This update is the worst update in the history of this game and will remain that way till the day this game gets shutdown. Let’s start off with the interface. It sucks. It forces you to default hud. I do have to give it some credit, it does clean up the main menu a bit, but it removed the create server option so no more Tr_Walkway. Next matches have to be qued and you can no longer play on one you must choose 2 of the game modes and then it will choose your map. Really Valve? Plus ranked in “casual”. That’s another thing, casual gameplay was just pubs and there wasn’t anything serious about it just silly fun. Let’s go to gameplay now. Demo and Soldier are OP because for some reason valve increased blast radii. All the weapon changes are weird. Teleporters are insanely cheap to create. The game requires less skill. Items are now more pointless, and generally the whole game is a mess, but this time it’s a horrendous mess, not the mess of a game I fell in love with years ago. In the past I would have given the game a solid 9/10, but now with this update the game is more like a 3/10. Valve is making Call of Duty look like a cutting edge game.
Can valve fix TF2? Maybe, but the damage has already been done. I had the dream to do competitive TF2 and my friend had the dream to be on the same team as me, but I guess that is the end of that dream. Both he and I are thinking of quitting the game and cashing out, which the chances for me to do so are high. This game was amazing, and now? It is garbage.
It feels sad to leave the game I loved so much and put so much time into. Feels like I’m putting down an old pet. Valve doesn’t listen to their community at all and that is why they suck. If you are a fan of this game I hope you like the new TF2. Looks like I’m going to stick to Overwatch since this game is no longer enjoyable. If you are a new player and like it good for you, but I recommend to stay away from this game. As is has really been turned to rubbish

I remember when Team Fortress 2 went F2P, I'm glad it did as I wouldn't have (probably) got this great game, the community is pretty good, with lots of community servers with various community modes (stuff like Minigames). The Valve official modes range from Payload (Protecting and getting a cart to a point) to Pass Time (Think of something like Basketball but in the TF2 Universe!), With Matchmaking getting an overhaul in the upcoming Meet your Match update, which also adds a Competitive Mode which is similar to another of Valve's games "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive" where depending on how you play in the mode, you will earn a rank. Another mode in the game is Man Versus Machine (MVM for short), which is a six player wave based mode where you and your friends can team up against an army of Robots.
The game can be played in various ways as there are 9 Separate classes with many different playstyles, ranging from a Sniper to a Medic to a Spy. Each class is customizable with different clothing options (Hats etc.) and they can use many different weapons designed specifically for their class. There are 40+ maps in the game (actually too many to count) NOT including all the custom maps available for the game which gives a lot of replayability to Team Fortress 2. The only problem I have with the game is that a lot of people like playing only 1 map (2Fort/ctf_2fort) so if you don't really enjoy the map then you may dislike the game, I do play this map a lot as I really like the way the map is laid out and a lot of the servers were just 2Fort so I got used to the layout and probably know the map like the back of my hand.
My rating for the game would be a solid 9/10, Thanks Valve for making an incredibly enjoyable game!

I've had TF2 on 3 different accounts with a combined total of ~1500 hours. I have to say, recently the game has gotten real repetitive. Valve has taken a game that once had updates with completely new weapons, taunts, etc. made by the community and downgraded it into a similar feel to CS:GO (Dont get my words confused; CS:GO by itself is a good game.) What I mean is; the game has gotten to where skins, unusuals, aussies, etc. make the player and not the playstyle itself. When I go on public matches, many a time I'll see a bunch of players that seem like their w key is stuck down, as is there primary fire button. I've ran a server for quite a while, and the players that get on now a days seem to be clones of each other, like a scout with a F.A.N. and Sandman or a Pyro with the phlog, or a demo seemingly only using his sticky launcher. In short, the game needs some new ideas, new weapons, and some players teaching people a vast amount of playstyles. Until then, this game is headed into the ground. Thank you for your time.

Good fun, mein freund. Games have two teams: Red, and Blu (Blu is the actual name, yes), with nine classes: Scout, Soldier, Pyro, Demoman, Heavy, Engineer, Medic, Sniper, and Spy. The classes in that list are broken into three labels (three classes per label): Offense, defense, and support, in that order. There are basic tutorials in the game, and various Youtubers that make tutorials for different classes.
Something I like, and hate, is that if you're really good at a class, then you can wreck unorganized teams, i.e. most TF2 teams. Anyway, this is good fun, most servers and players are open to doing some really goofy things at any time.
So, yeah. It's free. You can just uninstall it if you don't like playing TF2. *No judgements, or anything*

I've had TF2 on 3 different accounts with a combined total of ~1500 hours. I have to say, recently the game has gotten real repetitive. Valve has taken a game that once had updates with completely new weapons, taunts, etc. made by the community and downgraded it into a similar feel to CS:GO (Dont get my words confused; CS:GO by itself is a good game.) What I mean is; the game has gotten to where skins, unusuals, aussies, etc. make the player and not the playstyle itself. When I go on public matches, many a time I'll see a bunch of players that seem like their w key is stuck down, as is there primary fire button. I've ran a server for quite a while, and the players that get on now a days seem to be clones of each other, like a scout with a F.A.N. and Sandman or a Pyro with the phlog, or a demo seemingly only using his sticky launcher. In short, the game needs some new ideas, new weapons, and some players teaching people a vast amount of playstyles. Until then, this game is headed into the ground. Thank you for your time.

Tf2 is my all tim favorite game I have ever played.  When i played this game on the Orange Box for Xbox 360 i was instantly hooked and bought it for the computer (it used to cost money). This game is very fun and you can play it for a while without getting bored, but it has gone downhill a little. Dont get me wrong I still love this game, but the community isnt the best and people call others noobs if you dont have hats. After looking at the comments for this game and seeing that people were saying this is a pay to win game, well im here to say that it is not! This game has a store where you can buy hats and guns with real money but you can find weapons from drops and hats dont buff you in the slightest. The only reason to spend a cent on this game is to upgrade to premium. When  you start this game you will start with a small, limited inventory of 50 spaces, Stock weapons, and access to all classes (no paying for classes in this game), the only upsides for premium is extra backpack space, and the small chance of finding a hat iin a drop instead of a weapon (even Free 2 plays can find any weapon from drops.
Even though i recommmend this gsme and it free, I still suggest buying something from the store to upgrade to premium (any thing you purchase in the store will give you premium, the cheepest item being the rocket/sticky jumper for 49 cents i think). In conclusion i totally recommend this game, it is a ton of fun and you can play it for hours at a time without getting bored!!

I've played TF2 for a long time - basically when Orange Box was still a thing.
In it's core, TF2 is a fantastic game. Great characters with unique personalities and roles. Furthermore, items can change the functionality and playability of your character adding more hours to game-play. If you pair that with lots of updates, community made maps, and different game types, you end up with a game that can be played endlessly.
. You can't really ask for much more in a FPS.
Initially my major complaint for this game was: no trading system. Well that changed, hooray for Valve!
Let's not celebrate too soon... the trading system, while great for people who actually use the trading system to improve playability (getting weapons they did not previously have), it has quickly spiralled into a pointless competition of showing-off the fanciest hats and items. In game purchases? Extremely rare hats that can cost up to thousands? My only question is
Thankfully these items that I would consider silly and pointless don't actually influence game play. Weapons are reasonably well balanced so there is little frustration in that regard. Having a strong, well organised team will still beat a team that simply has more items. So if you don't mind the flashy nonsense, TF2 is still definitely worth your time.

Team Fortress 2 is a team-based FPS that varies in different gamemodes like Medieval Mode (medieval weapons only), Capture the Flag (By flag, I mean the glowing briefcase), Payload (Push a bomb to a certain point)  and Capture (Capturing control points). Most people care more about hats and just playing deathmatch than playing the specific gamemode. Once I have been banned for capturing the objective on an official server. (Vote-banned) Team Fortress 2 is highly addicting since On an alternative account I had around 600+ hours and I would of had tons more if I didn't get VAC-banned. But the trading system is nice. And its also just really fun to play in general. There are tons of community servers, mods and gamemodes out there everywhere. It's also got a cartoonish art-design and has been out since the release in 2007. Over time you can randomly find items as drops like a weapon, hat, or tool item.
Team Fortress 2 has nine different classes to pick from including Scout, Soldier and Pyro (Offense) Demoman, Heavy and Engineer (Defense) then Medic, Sniper and Spy (Support).
Gameplay:
Scout: The fastest running speed in the game with a double jump to make you easily mobile with a scattergun, pistol and bat.
Soldier: Semi-slow movement speed with a rocket launcher, shotgun and shovel but soldier is more mobile than you think as you can rocket jump and have a specialised rocket launcher to rocket jump. (The Rocket Jumper)
Pyro: Pyro is a medium movement speed deadly pyromaniac with a flamethrower, shotgun (and flare gun) and fire axe. The Pyro has all different strategies like flare punching. The Pyro can also deflect projectiles making him a deadly class to challenge on the battlefield.
Demoman: Demoman is a slow-moving defense class that has a Grenade Launcher, Sticky Bomb Launcher and Bottle to destroy anyone thats come within range.
Heavy: Heavy is a super-slow moving class but super-devastating as he has a Minigun, Shotgun and his own fists to destroy anything that comes in his way.
Engineer: Engineer is a medium-movement speed class that has a Shotgun, Pistol, Wrench, Construction PDA and Demolition PDA. He can create a Sentry Gun, Dispenser and a Entrance and Exit teleporter which can all go up to each level increasing firepower, healing rate/metal generation rate and recharge rate. The wrench can be used to upgrade and repair buildings.
Medic: Medic is a underplayedclass since there is usually none or one on a team but he has a semi-fast movement speed with a Syringe Gun, Medi-Gun and Bonesaw do not underestimate them there are really good players as medic that can dominate you. The Medic also has an Übercharge which charges up over time as you heal a patient with the Medi-Gun and once it reaches 100% you can release the charge which will give a short period of time of invulnerability to you and the patient.
Sniper: Sniper is a medium-movement speed support character which usually stays around one spot or changes if it gets invaded. The Sniper has a Sniper Rifle, SMG and a Kukri.
Spy: Spy is my personal favourite. Spy has a Revolver, Sapper, Knife and Invis Watch. The spy can use the Knife to stab from behind for a 1-hit kill. And the Sapper is used to disable and destroy enemy Engineer buildings.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

This game used to be considered good. Now, I think its absolute GARBAGE. For one, this game is more unbalanced than ANY cod game ever. Let me give you some examples. Medics that can make people invincible, Rocket launchers that can one shot most classes, Sentry guns that have potential to kill any class in a matter of a second, sticky grenades that are practically meant for spawn camping, invisibility, disguising, one shot backstabs, ect. There will be many nerds out there that say "theres no such thing as an OP class, its just good players", but I can tell you that this could not be more of a lie. For one, lets look at the scout. He can run backwards, is ridiculously fast, and can run away from pretty much anything. His shotgun is pretty ridiculous. It does stupid damage. The scout is purely aim. Now lets look at the soldier. He can one shot any class with 175 health with a direct rocket. The fire rate is really high on it for a rocket launcher. That means that the soldier can just spam corners easily. Also he can rocket jump. That means that he can get anywhere, and get out of most situations. Not to mention that he has a melee weapon that can one 200 hp classes. The Demoman is pretty balanced and takes skill to use (unlike the soldier) though his secondary class form known as the Demoknight can be really op and lacks skill. Now lets look at the spy. While he takes skill to use, his backstabs are RIDICULOUS and are annoyingly buggy. The backstab while either lag, and not register, or you can jump at people and stab them in the face and it counts as a 'backstab' (which WILL annoy you at one point or another). Overwatch is a MUCH better solution. I know you might be attracted to this game because its F2P, but its absolute garbage and don't expect much out of it except BS, and a bunch of nerds saying thats its 'skill based' and 'balanced' because they want to make themselves look good. Not to mention the spawncampers.
EDIT: This game can be very fun at times, even though its unbalanced and "being good" is simply putting together item strategies, I have decided that it is still worth it.

Welcome to my Team Fortress 2 review.  After three years in development, hopefully it will have been worth the wait.
Despite, or perhaps because of, its age, this venerable classic of PC gaming is still a well-developed experience with a fantastic and thriving community, a timeless and entertaining graphical style, and last but not least, a player, class, and equipment balance that surpasses any other game in the industry.
Team Fortress 2 is a game that embodies that overused tagline - "minutes to learn, ages to master" or some variant of that.  I was engaged from the moment three years ago when I first ran around as Pyro on 2fort, and I'm still engaged as I rocketjump past a Kritz-boosted Heavy to take down his Medic in a coordinated strike.  It has such variety and such a level of community involvement and emergent gameplay, I don't doubt I could spend another three years and not conqueror even a quarter of the possibilities for enjoying the game.
The game and the community have had ups and downs, and the developers are far from perfect, but they pay enough attention to community feedback that rough edges are quickly whittled down to the exact par of the rest of the game.  In the end, the game and the fanbase are inextricably linked to a degree that few games other than Bethesda ever achieve.

Welcome to my Team Fortress 2 review.  After three years in development, hopefully it will have been worth the wait.
Despite, or perhaps because of, its age, this venerable classic of PC gaming is still a well-developed experience with a fantastic and thriving community, a timeless and entertaining graphical style, and last but not least, a player, class, and equipment balance that surpasses any other game in the industry.
Team Fortress 2 is a game that embodies that overused tagline - "minutes to learn, ages to master" or some variant of that.  I was engaged from the moment three years ago when I first ran around as Pyro on 2fort, and I'm still engaged as I rocketjump past a Kritz-boosted Heavy to take down his Medic in a coordinated strike.  It has such variety and such a level of community involvement and emergent gameplay, I don't doubt I could spend another three years and not conqueror even a quarter of the possibilities for enjoying the game.
The game and the community have had ups and downs, and the developers are far from perfect, but they pay enough attention to community feedback that rough edges are quickly whittled down to the exact par of the rest of the game.  In the end, the game and the fanbase are inextricably linked to a degree that few games other than Bethesda ever achieve.

Team Fortress 2 does have a lot of positive things going for it. Lots of servers, maps, items, game types, workshop, Co-op. Most of which I've barely scraped the surface. And the game does get frequent fixes and updates even though it's been around for quite a few years. Team Fortress 2 is an extremely solid 1st person arena shooter but not one revolving around deathmatch modes like most multiplayer shooters. It has more strategic modes like capture the flag and hold the point, along with a few more innovative ones. The game mechanics, sounds, and graphics ran well on my system, although overall it's starting to appear a little dated.
This game might just not be for me. It might be great for you, though, especially if you are into old school arena shooters.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I pose an interesting philisophical quandry with this review. The paradoxical question is as such:
How is it that this game, this wonderful, creative, clever, in-depth, psychotic, child-scarring game that the developers have clearly poured so much love and effort into can manage to be so boring sometimes?
I don't get it, I honestly don't. It's got fun and varied gameplay, hysterical characters, an "easy to learn, hard to master" skill curve, and an endless roster of weird♥♥♥♥♥furry multiplayer servers that will have you on the floor with laughter or trauma, and yet every time I open up this game and start to play, I find myself getting distracted, sighing a lot, and generally wishing I had a bus window to look forlornly out of as I listen to some sad guitar music on a Walkman. A WALKMAN.
This will not do.
So WHY, I must ask. Why can I no longer enjoy this game for what it is? A simple, mindless shooter with a bloody, cartoony can of paint over it, which is all a disguise for the dark, insane microtransaction culture that takes place under the surface.
I'll tell you why.

I pose an interesting philisophical quandry with this review. The paradoxical question is as such:
How is it that this game, this wonderful, creative, clever, in-depth, psychotic, child-scarring game that the developers have clearly poured so much love and effort into can manage to be so boring sometimes?
I don't get it, I honestly don't. It's got fun and varied gameplay, hysterical characters, an "easy to learn, hard to master" skill curve, and an endless roster of weird♥♥♥♥♥furry multiplayer servers that will have you on the floor with laughter or trauma, and yet every time I open up this game and start to play, I find myself getting distracted, sighing a lot, and generally wishing I had a bus window to look forlornly out of as I listen to some sad guitar music on a Walkman. A WALKMAN.
This will not do.
So WHY, I must ask. Why can I no longer enjoy this game for what it is? A simple, mindless shooter with a bloody, cartoony can of paint over it, which is all a disguise for the dark, insane microtransaction culture that takes place under the surface.
I'll tell you why.

Alright. Where to begin..
A few years ago I came across TF2. I saw so many videos about this game without knowing what this game was actually about. So I decided to create a Steam Account, to download TF2 and to check it out myself.
I immediately fell in love with this game. It was fun, I enjoyed it for hours every single day and it actually is the reason why I had to retake one class in school because I was addicted. It was a painful hit but I decided to keep playing.
Many years later, I put so much tears, bucks and effort into this game to become better at it, make my classes look fancier and to make new friends. And also, a few friends I met in-game are still my friends today. Which is a big PLUS. Because you could just join servers like the Orange servers and meet new people. And also in Casual. You joined a game, if it sucked you would just leave and if it was fun you could stay for hours.
BUT not too long ago, Valve decided to take that holy experience away and changed Casual mode completely.
No more leaving and joining like we knew it. It was gone and so was the fun I had with this game. It may sound pathetic, but in my eyes this game once was a masterpiece and it became a part of my life.
Dear Valve, I know you won't change anything. But if anyone from the Valve staff reads this, which I highly doubt, keep in mind that you didn't only lose me as a player with your major game changes, but also many others.
It's definitely not a bad game. But I'm sure that some people out there, like me, agree that this is nothing like the old TF2 feeling anymore.

Team Fortress 2, the game with 9 classes that are unique and creative.
The classes are as follows:
1. Scout - Fast class that can double jump. Does small damage to other classes but in the end it adds up and the opponent is dead.
2. Sniper - A class that is better standing back, headshotting people and making them mad. This class can be used upclose but its smarter to play farther back.
3. Soldier - A slow, annoying (to others) class that gets a rocket launcher. Very fun to annoy others with, and you also get to rocket jump!
4. Spy - A fun, strategic class that requires a lot of strategy to play with as there are several components that spys need to have to be good.
5. Pyro - An easy to get good at class, the pyro has a flamethrower! Who wouldn't want to use it? And even if you die, you still burned your enemy and inflicted tons of damage, so thats good!
6. Heavy - A tanky, slow class with the most health in the game. This class uses a minigun which can be used to exterminate other classes that get in the heavies way.
7. Medic - A class that doesn't attack a lot, the medic does what he should, which is heal. He is a support who can also deal some good damage.
8. Engineer - This class is a fun to play with class who trolls people but putting down a sentry to obliterate his opponents, dispenser to heal/give ammo to team, and teleporters to teleport his team anywhere in the map.
9. Demoman - The demoman is a class with a grenade launcher. This class has a similar rocket jump, but instead of a rocket jump, it is a sticky jump with sticky grenades.
Overall, this game is very unique to other 1st person shooters. The classes all have a unique personality and all of the classes work differently than the others. Have fun playing!

Well what can I say about Team Fortress 2 that hasn't been said already?
I first played this game on my old Steam account back in 2008, when I bought the Orange Box, I remeber looking at the artwork and thinking "what is this weird cartoon game about, I'll give it a try". Well after 1500 hours of gameplay (this account and my older one) I can say that this is perhaps my favourite multiplayer FPS ever.
I have never got bored with this game, the gameplay and gunplay is immensely satisfying and never becomes stale or boring. The class variety is perfect with a class for every role and skillset.
If you have excellent aim and twitch gameplay skills then there's the scout who does large damage with his scattergun up close, but has a low health pool meaning you need to be good at dodging and getting in then backing out of a fight quickly. His run speed the fastest of all the classes and his double jump ability help with this.
If you don't have the best aim but have good map sense and game sense try the spy, he can cloak for a short time to get behind the enemy lines, then disguise himself as one of the enemy team and get instant kill backstabs.
All of the 9 classes on offer are very well balanced and each offers a unique style of gunplay that makes them all fun to play.
Valve perhaps made their best decision when they decided to switch from a realistic style of graphics to the shaded cartoon style way back in 2007. It has allowed the appearance of this game to age very well over the years and still looks half decent today.
The community is good with this game and thanks to valves VAC system, cheaters are rare and easily voted off a server when they do show up.
Now that this game is free to play there's no excuse not to download it and start playing now :)

Well what can I say about Team Fortress 2 that hasn't been said already?
I first played this game on my old Steam account back in 2008, when I bought the Orange Box, I remeber looking at the artwork and thinking "what is this weird cartoon game about, I'll give it a try". Well after 1500 hours of gameplay (this account and my older one) I can say that this is perhaps my favourite multiplayer FPS ever.
I have never got bored with this game, the gameplay and gunplay is immensely satisfying and never becomes stale or boring. The class variety is perfect with a class for every role and skillset.
If you have excellent aim and twitch gameplay skills then there's the scout who does large damage with his scattergun up close, but has a low health pool meaning you need to be good at dodging and getting in then backing out of a fight quickly. His run speed the fastest of all the classes and his double jump ability help with this.
If you don't have the best aim but have good map sense and game sense try the spy, he can cloak for a short time to get behind the enemy lines, then disguise himself as one of the enemy team and get instant kill backstabs.
All of the 9 classes on offer are very well balanced and each offers a unique style of gunplay that makes them all fun to play.
Valve perhaps made their best decision when they decided to switch from a realistic style of graphics to the shaded cartoon style way back in 2007. It has allowed the appearance of this game to age very well over the years and still looks half decent today.
The community is good with this game and thanks to valves VAC system, cheaters are rare and easily voted off a server when they do show up.
Now that this game is free to play there's no excuse not to download it and start playing now :)

Here is my review to the game :
This game is one of the best FPS Game ever or if i can say The First and Only War Themed Hat Simulator XD.But seriously you will never regret playing this game.Team Fortress 2 was released on 2007 but even though this is an old game the servers is still full or crowded.After 9 years of development,this game is worth the wait XD
What makes me love this game :
-The cartoonish art style and graphic
-The 9 different class to play
-The taunts,hats,skins and costumes XD
-The team work
-The modes of the game
-The trade and community
-and many more!
Playing Team Fortress 2 is different than any other FPS game.You MUST cooperate with other players in order to defeat the enemy team.There is 9 different classes with different weapons and purposes.If there is too many players using 1 of 9 classes the team will lose.So in order to balance the team and winning,one MUST use the class that the team needed and cooperate with other classes to defeat the enemy.This is Team Fortress 2 not Solo Deathmatch 2.This is what makes Team Fortress 2 different and fun to play.
Graphic : 8/10 (cartoonish art syle is good)
Gameplay : 10/10
Story : 8/10 (the story only exist in the comics and trailers)
Enjoyment : 10/10
Overall : 9

I have been playing this game since the Orange Box was released. It has certainly changed over the years. I enjoy seeing it doing so well in this world where most games live fast and die young. The best part of the game is the art style. Unfortunately, the art style has degraded over the years with the advent of cosmetics and weapons. The game does still manage to stand out as unique, but the distinct style has been obscured by everyone's favorite sombreros and pink manes. There is still plenty of fun to be had. The teamwork is indeed the main source of enjoyment. You feel great when you work together to out maneuver the enemy team. In a similar vain, there's a lot of opportunity for rage when you find yourself outclassed as you and all your gibus teammates get stomped by the unusuals. Give it a try, and for God's sake don't spend any money in it.

TF2 Is Great.
If you have been living under a rock your whole life, allow me to explain why.
TF2 is an old game, but it still has a great community and still looks and plays very well. Imagine something almost like a slower-paced Quake in terms of gameplay. When it came out, TF2 was and still is the DeFacto Game for all Arena-based FPS's, a game you can goof off in and generally have a good time, with a competative scene for those who want it. It might not be as competative as CS:GO, it might not be as fast as Overwatch, but it still holds alot of fun and it is a game you will consistantly come back to for a good time. Yes, there is a money store, and there are weapons, but you have the chance to randomly earn these weapons by playing the game, and everyting else is either donations to map makers, or cosmetics. The classes are all incredibly balanced and easy to use (Exception of Spy) and most cheap strategies can be mitigated by using a different class or changing tactics. Weapons are generally fine BUT, there are select weapons that people use because of THE META, or the fact that you can cheese strat with them (the dead ringer...Will not be an example as it is being changed.) There are also some....Questionable Changes like The Pretty boy's pocket pistol being a worse Blutsauger (more damage vulnerability on a gun you'd ONLY be using if you're hurt) or the Poor Mann's Phlog, the Cleaner's Carbine.
The final Verdict: Despite strange happneings with weapon balance, Play it, you will like it.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I've been playing Team Fortress 2 (TF2) almost four years now, it was my first game on Steam and started my passion for team-based shooters. I've seen the game evolve into great things, while some tweaks might not be as good. To simply everything, I'm going to list details in a pro/con list. Let's start
-Core gameplay is fun and inviting with nine playable classes and a multitude of weapons.
-Recieves regular updates to fix bugs and tweak gameplay, (However, there's more to it.)
-Fun team-based gameplay. Great game to play with friends.
-Community isn't toxic as other games like Counter Strike: Global Offensive (CS:GO,) or DOTA. You can find a lot of servers full of friendly players.
-You can tailor your classes to your liking through the use of cosmetic items.
-Community servers. While Valve's hosted servers are good and all, sometimes you just want a server to mess around on, good thing there are a lot of community servers that wouldn't mind you taking up a player slot.
-This game is Free to Play (F2P and recieves a lot of "pay to unlock" features such as cosmetics or taunts.
-Most updates that add in new features add in a huge amount of new hats.
-Did I mention hats? A good portion of this game's community focus on cosmetic changes of their classes or trading hats to earn money.
-While this game does recieve regular updates, every update seems to cause more issues or gets flak from the community. This game is not Valve's majory priority any more and often gets lazy fixes due to the lack of devs working on the game.
-Because this game is Free to Play, there are hackers, they often get kicked from servers because they're so obvious, (Valve has also been re-working features of their anti-cheat to catch hackers, and it's been working a lot better.)
-Community consists of a lot of younger players, while this does not bother me it does bother members of the community and people kick these younger players off of servers simply because of their voice.
This game has been a blast in the four years I've played it. While I know a lot of people think that the game isn't one of Valve's better games, it has a place in my heart as one of my first truly enjoyable experiences in gaming. Team Fortress 2 has a lot to offer, and I still haven't seen it all. I personally recommend that you download Team Fortress 2 and play it. It's been a blast of a game, and let's hope that it continues to stay that way in the future.

To be honest, I've had a BLAST with this game. Even if you don't spend any money, you can still get far up. There are a lot of good cosmetics and item combinations. This game has many classes to play as, with each having their own quirk and playstyle: there's something for everyone. Though people who play normal FPSes such as COD will probably not immediately understand TF2, as the concept and way to play is a lot different. There are also other things besides the normal fighting to make things more fun, like taunting and as mentioned before: cosmetics. There are a LOT of cosmetic items in TF2, some for all classes, some for specific ones, and I think this really brings some variety to the usual kill-every-enemy-you-see method of playing games. There's also an innovative item system which includes trading, combining items, limited space to store things (increases with a Premium account), etc.
Overall, I recommend TF2. If you usually play other shooters like CS:GO or COD, don't take it as the same thing and do some research to understand how it works. But after you get the hang of it, it's quite an amazing game.

This review, strangely enough, contains my point of view. My opinion so to speak. If you dont like it or disagree just hit that dislike button. If you have words of criticism however, I encourage you to write it all down.
[Review]
TF2, a brilliant game indeed. I had a lot of fun with it, I mean I got over 1000 hours in it after all. There must be something that kept me there for so many years. And it did. It was the game as a whole. While I could never take the game all that seriously, it was the main point as to why I loved it so much. Being a hoovy, a pyroshark or just a dumbass annoying scout that yells for the dispenser even after it's built and hits the engi with his pan. I am just that kind of player in TF2. I recently even went in with the thought of tryharding until I don't like it anymore. I go soldier, get into the enemy base, yell medic once and the enemy soldier stands infront of me and does the same. I went from tryhard mode to "I wanna have fun" mode. What followed was a voicecommand conversation of about 5 minutes until the teams got sick of it and killed us both. Which didn't stop us from becoming hoovies. God, I love this game.
And as much as I do love it, I also have to say this very little but also major fact. TF2 is on its deathbed. And before you hit that dislike button and rage at me for saying this: Hear me out. TF2 has been on its deathbed for years. I mean, hell, it's an old game. Look at when it came out. There are more players jumping off now because they have gotten into other things, as it goes normally. But they will also come back from time to time. Or they go and play Overwatch. Kinda like I did. But of course everything has a reason.
TF2 on its own is a great game. The concept, the gamemodes and the classes are fun to play. Some harder than others but, hey, that's the fun of it. And while the base of TF2 couldn't be greater, it's the devs and a small but dedicated part of the community which made and still make it a rather bad experience. So let us begin with my points.
"Ragers"
We all know, back in the day without casual and competitive, we had to play all on one server. Back then, their anger at hoovies who wouldn't play or spycrabs etc was understandable. Now with this update in place however the amount ragers got smaller, but the ones that stood their ground are so annoying and rather rude even though there is a perfect mode just for them to play. Leave us, the silly hat people, in peace and you can play the game. Noone is going to stop you.
"The competitive update"
With the update many things have changed. Community servers still exist, but they went from 100% to 20% in terms of the amount of them. Valve servers no longer exist and I know how much time I spent on them. More than on Skial, that's for sure. 'cause screw fast-respawn. Y'all are noobs, if you wanna play like that. Jokes aside, I have been let down with the update as a whole. The competitive aspect is rather disappointing and if you go in with a good team it's still not good enough as you are reminded of what pubstomping means when you are in your very first game. Or in other words: If you don't get 20 kills in one life as a scout, don't play competItive. It just isn't worth it.
But what about casual? The new "Valve Servers". Hit and miss kind of. I like the idea, but I hate having to wait to join one. It isn't all that bad, especially as you can actually just play as you would normally. Everyone is chill, not totally focused on winning and all is as casual as it can get. But I still don't like waiting. I don't like it in OW either for that matter! Skirmishes ftw!
And what about the rest of the community servers? Well, imagine a world in which most rotation servers are either empty at most times or gone. Imagine a world in which most servers are minigames or something else. Jumpservers, surf and more. Fast respawn, times 10 and so on and so forth. There still are good classic community servers. However you will be lucky to find one without a single little modification. Like Fast respawn. Who in the hell likes fast respawn?!
"MVM and the trader community"
Disclaimer: If you don't belong to these types of people, all is fine. I don't mean you or the community in general. But I feel like I should mention what I experienced myself.
In my time of playing MVM I met so many disgusting people. It ranges from pure tryhard who doesn't give a damn about the team to: "obey me or you will get kicked". And not to forget the lovely farmers. In my whole time playing MVM I think I had like 3 good matches and all of them were with friends.
As for the trading community? Well this might be just a small part of it but never have I ever been more insulted in my life. Those few months that started out well became just a grand annoyance in the end. It went from trading to selling and buying. Noone cared for having good well rounded trades. Everyone just wanted to make profit. And that surely isn't trading anymore. People tried to force me to give them certain items for others, tried to scam me and so much more. From mere insults in the chat to harrassment on my profile until I blocked and reported them. I went out of there as fast as I could and just kept on playing the game from there on out.
|-[Edit]-|
After the most recent experience, my opinion on the casual mode has changed quite a lot. You are better off finding community servers that work instead of playing casual mode. The casual experience has a huge toxicity problem and I am sad to say that just yesterday, it ruined many a game. I was told to kill myself/that the person wants to kill me just for having 9 kills as a trolldier no less while he had 50 as sniper. Another game chimed in just because I was merely typing instead of speaking over my mic calling me a ♥♥♥♥♥ and many other things. After it died down for 2 - 3 minutes, suddenly the second guy called a votekick on me which sadly worked out. On this day, I realised that the community of casual mode, NOT of TF2, is as bad as it can get.
|-[Edit End]-|
Anyhow, these are my overall thoughts on TF2. I love the game. It couldn't be more brilliant. But we have to see the facts: It is on its dying breath. It sure as hell refuses to die and I hope it lives for a good time but it is dying. And when it happens I will mourn the loss as everyone else who has ever played it. It brought me great times. So many great times. I don't want to miss any of it. But everything in life has a start and an end. And at some point TF2 will cease to exist as well.
So to all of you to still play TF2: Game on my friends and greet a hoovy for me if you were to find one. And please, protect my brothers from any harm as I am not able to anymore.

(This review is a rewrite of my old one, which was far less serious)
Team Fortress 2, even after over 8 years since its release, remains one of Steam's most played games. TF2 has exciting FPS gameplay, 9 classes that all feel different from one another, and it feels incredibly smooth to control your character and shoot people. Each class has unlockable weapons, which are (mostly) side-grades to the stock. The game has several bright, well-designed, and interesting maps to play on. This game still hasn't gotten old for me, because there's so much stuff to learn and do. Even after getting the hang of all the classes, you can still learn about things like sentry jumps, trimping, and entering the reference pose to screw with people. This is because so many people have played the game and discovered new mechanics over the years.
Team Fortress 2 also has an amazing free-to-play model. Every single map, weapon, class, and mechanic is available to everybody for free. All things you are required to invest money in are completely cosmetic, mostly hats and weapon reskins.
The TF2 community can be rather toxic at times. People often do things like spam memes and bully new players, even if they themselves are relatively new. Nice players are still playing this game though. I run into players who are good sports and display kind manners toward their opponents and new players.
Not everything is completely balanced in TF2, either. Some weapons and weapon combos can be unfair to fight against, but every once in a while Valve steps in and fixes these things. Speaking of which, Valve has been helping the game out a lot recently, with bug fixes, balance changes, a new competetive mode (not perfect but in the making), and cosmetic updates. I have a lot of hope for the future of TF2 and its community, and I invite anyone who wants to play a good shooter game to join us.

[Headsup]
This review, strangely enough, contains my point of view. My opinion so to speak. If you dont like it or disagree just hit that dislike button. If you have words of criticism however, I encourage you to write it all down.
[Review]
TF2, a brilliant game indeed. I had a lot of fun with it, I mean I got over 1000 hours in it after all. There must be something that kept me there for so many years. And it did. It was the game as a whole. While I could never take the game all that seriously, it was the main point as to why I loved it so much. Being a hoovy, a pyroshark or just a dumbass annoying scout that yells for the dispenser even after it's built and hits the engi with his pan. I am just that kind of player in TF2. I recently even went in with the thought of tryharding until I don't like it anymore. I go soldier, get into the enemy base, yell medic once and the enemy soldier stands infront of me and does the same. I went from tryhard mode to "I wanna have fun" mode. What followed was a voicecommand conversation of about 5 minutes until the teams got sick of it and killed us both. Which didn't stop us from becoming hoovies. God, I love this game.
And as much as I do love it, I also have to say this very little but also major fact. TF2 is on its deathbed. And before you hit that dislike button and rage at me for saying this: Hear me out. TF2 has been on its deathbed for years. I mean, hell, it's an old game. Look at when it came out. There are more players jumping off now because they have gotten into other things, as it goes normally. But they will also come back from time to time. Or they go and play Overwatch. Kinda like I did. But of course everything has a reason.
TF2 on its own is a great game. The concept, the gamemodes and the classes are fun to play. Some harder than others but, hey, that's the fun of it. And while the base of TF2 couldn't be greater, it's the devs and a small but dedicated part of the community which made and still make it a rather bad experience. So let us begin with my points.
"Ragers"
We all know, back in the day without casual and competitive, we had to play all on one server. Back then, their anger at hoovies who wouldn't play or spycrabs etc was understandable. Now with this update in place however the amount ragers got smaller, but the ones that stood their ground are so annoying and rather rude even though there is a perfect mode just for them to play. Leave us, the silly hat people, in peace and you can play the game. Noone is going to stop you.
"The competitive update"
With the update many things have changed. Community servers still exist, but they went from 100% to 20% in terms of the amount of them. Valve servers no longer exist and I know how much time I spent on them. More than on Skial, that's for sure. 'cause screw fast-respawn. Y'all are noobs, if you wanna play like that. Jokes aside, I have been let down with the update as a whole. The competitive aspect is rather disappointing and if you go in with a good team it's still not good enough as you are reminded of what pubstomping means when you are in your very first game. Or in other words: If you don't get 20 kills in one life as a scout, don't play competItive. It just isn't worth it.
But what about casual? The new "Valve Servers". Hit and miss kind of. I like the idea, but I hate having to wait to join one. It isn't all that bad, especially as you can actually just play as you would normally. Everyone is chill, not totally focused on winning and all is as casual as it can get. But I still don't like waiting. I don't like it in OW either for that matter! Skirmishes ftw!
And what about the rest of the community servers? Well, imagine a world in which most rotation servers are either empty at most times or gone. Imagine a world in which most servers are minigames or something else. Jumpservers, surf and more. Fast respawn, times 10 and so on and so forth. There still are good classic community servers. However you will be lucky to find one without a single little modification. Like Fast respawn. Who in the hell likes fast respawn?!
"MVM and the trader community"
Disclaimer: If you don't belong to these types of people, all is fine. I don't mean you or the community in general. But I feel like I should mention what I experienced myself.
In my time of playing MVM I met so many disgusting people. It ranges from pure tryhard who doesn't give a damn about the team to: "obey me or you will get kicked". And not to forget the lovely farmers. In my whole time playing MVM I think I had like 3 good matches and all of them were with friends.
As for the trading community? Well this might be just a small part of it but never have I ever been more insulted in my life. Those few months that started out well became just a grand annoyance in the end. It went from trading to selling and buying. Noone cared for having good well rounded trades. Everyone just wanted to make profit. And that surely isn't trading anymore. People tried to force me to give them certain items for others, tried to scam me and so much more. From mere insults in the chat to harrassment on my profile until I blocked and reported them. I went out of there as fast as I could and just kept on playing the game from there on out.
|-[Edit]-|
After the most recent experience, my opinion on the casual mode has changed quite a lot. You are better off finding community servers that work instead of playing casual mode. The casual experience has a huge toxicity problem and I am sad to say that just yesterday, it ruined many a game. I was told to kill myself/that the person wants to kill me just for having 9 kills as a trolldier no less while he had 50 as sniper. Another game chimed in just because I was merely typing instead of speaking over my mic calling me a ♥♥♥♥♥ and many other things. After it died down for 2 - 3 minutes, suddenly the second guy called a votekick on me which sadly worked out. On this day, I realised that the community of casual mode, NOT of TF2, is as bad as it can get.
|-[Edit End]-|
Anyhow, these are my overall thoughts on TF2. I love the game. It couldn't be more brilliant. But we have to see the facts: It is on its dying breath. It sure as hell refuses to die and I hope it lives for a good time but it is dying. And when it happens I will mourn the loss as everyone else who has ever played it. It brought me great times. So many great times. I don't want to miss any of it. But everything in life has a start and an end. And at some point TF2 will cease to exist as well.
So to all of you to still play TF2: Game on my friends and greet a hoovy for me if you were to find one. And please, protect my brothers from any harm as I am not able to anymore.

(This review is a rewrite of my old one, which was far less serious)
Team Fortress 2, even after over 8 years since its release, remains one of Steam's most played games. TF2 has exciting FPS gameplay, 9 classes that all feel different from one another, and it feels incredibly smooth to control your character and shoot people. Each class has unlockable weapons, which are (mostly) side-grades to the stock. The game has several bright, well-designed, and interesting maps to play on. This game still hasn't gotten old for me, because there's so much stuff to learn and do. Even after getting the hang of all the classes, you can still learn about things like sentry jumps, trimping, and entering the reference pose to screw with people. This is because so many people have played the game and discovered new mechanics over the years.
Team Fortress 2 also has an amazing free-to-play model. Every single map, weapon, class, and mechanic is available to everybody for free. All things you are required to invest money in are completely cosmetic, mostly hats and weapon reskins.
The TF2 community can be rather toxic at times. People often do things like spam memes and bully new players, even if they themselves are relatively new. Nice players are still playing this game though. I run into players who are good sports and display kind manners toward their opponents and new players.
Not everything is completely balanced in TF2, either. Some weapons and weapon combos can be unfair to fight against, but every once in a while Valve steps in and fixes these things. Speaking of which, Valve has been helping the game out a lot recently, with bug fixes, balance changes, a new competetive mode (not perfect but in the making), and cosmetic updates. I have a lot of hope for the future of TF2 and its community, and I invite anyone who wants to play a good shooter game to join us.

Summary:
If I had to summarize Tf2 in one sentence, I'd say it's one of the most entertaining, balanced, and relaxing games to play.
Pros:
From the moment I laid my eyes on this game a year ago, I literally haven't played any other game besides it. The 3 things that seprate it from all the FPS games out there are it's:
1. Great community
The Tf2 community is very friendly, and you can always find people to play with and hang out with on servers, from group hosted events to just chilling out with your friends.
2. Balanced classes
The balance between classes is another thing that makes this game the way it is. There is a counter for pretty much any weapon, so it's a battle of skill and prediction.
3. Everlasting entertainment
It's almost impossible to get bored of this game because of the hundreds of weapons and styles to play each class that exist, from trolling engies to tryhard soldiers to spawncamping demos. There's also hundreds of maps and gamemodes to play as well, so the fun never ends.
Cons:
Error, not found.
Rating:
All in all, hugely recommended for any experienced or new gamers. Try it out, and I guarantee you won't be dissapointed! 10/10
