How To Make a Basic Butter Cake from Scratch
Makes one 2-layer cake
What You Need
Ingredients
1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened (plus extra for greasing the pans)
1 1/2 cups sugar
3 large eggs.
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon salt
3 1/2 teaspoons baking powder
1 1/4 cups whole milk
1 teaspoon vanilla
2 1/2 cups buttercream frosting, such as basic buttercream
Equipment
2 9-inch round pans
Stand mixer or hand mixer
Measuring cups and spoons
Cookie scoop or measuring cup, for dividing the batter
Instructions
Heat the oven to 350°F.
Sift together the flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
Prepare the pans: Rub the bottoms and sides of the cake pans with a little butter, shortening, or baking spray. Make sure to get into the corners and all the way up the sides. Flour the sides and bottoms of the pan by scooping a bit of flour into the pan, then shaking and tapping to coat the bottom and sides of the pan with flour; dump out the excess. Alternatively, cut out a parchment round and use this to line the bottom.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy and light. Cream together for about 3 to 5 minutes on medium spread (see above notes for more information).
Add the eggs one at a time. Beat until the batter is very smooth and creamy-looking. Adding the eggs one at a time gives them a better chance at incorporating into a smooth batter. Be sure they are room temperature so the batter does not appear curdled.
Beat in half the flour, salt, and baking powder. Add the sifted dry ingredients with the mixer running at low speed. Continue to mix until incorporated.
Beat in the milk and vanilla. Alternate adding in the liquids with the dry ingredients so the milk has a chance to be absorbed without needing to overmix the batter. Stream in the milk with the mixer on low until combined.
Beat in the remaining flour mixture until just combined and no more visible flour remains. Stir a few times with a spatula to make sure no more flour remains on the bottom of the bowl.
Divide the batter between cake pans. Use a scale or mechanical ice cream scoop to evenly divide the batter. Smooth the tops with an offset spatula. Drop the pans against the counter to shake out air bubbles.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes: When done, the cake should be puffed like a pillow, golden, and pull away from the sides of the pan. When done, a toothpick inserted into the center of the cakes should come out clean.
Cool for 15 minutes in the pan. Run an offset spatula around the cake to make sure it's completely loosened from the sides of the pan.
Flip the rounds out of the pan, remove the parchment lining, and flip right-side up to cool completely.
Once cool, frost and assemble the cake with the buttercream.

Team Fortress 2 is a revolutionizing FPS for Valve Software. Team Fortress 2 consists of two teams: Red and Blu.
In these two teams, there are nine total classes that are separated into offense, defense and support. These classes are: Scout, soldier, pyro, demoman, heavy, engineer, medic, sniper and spy. There are also tons of maps and gamemodes that you will have fun with endlessly throughout your time in TF2. Now, let's get into the PROS and CONS.
In my opinion, Team Fortress 2 is a great game! If you're interested in making things for the community, making friends, or just having some casual fun, this is probably the game for you. Although you may rage and quit sometimes and you may quit for MONTHS, maybe even YEARS, you'll always come back, trust me. My final rating for this game is eight out of ten. The reason for this is that there is a lot of variety in this game, but the community can be pretty crappy sometimes. Nonetheless, this is a great game, I think you should try it and if you don't like it, just remember you got it for free.

First off, Team Fortress 2 was one of the first FPS games I played on PC when I got my Steam account. It left a good enough impression on me to continue playing for this long, which explains the 1,000 hours of play time at the time of this review. Now, the upsides of this game... The community itself is great, aside from those who abuse their microphones or decide to use hacks. I've met good people and become friends with them through this game. There are big updates that always bring in new content, mainly hats and cosmetics and the occasional new maps, that are usually community-created. Nine classes, each with unique weapons, cosmetics, and hats, (Yes, hats. You heard me right.) The gameplay itself is pretty well-balanced, random crits aside. Oh, and Phlogistinator pyros. (Seriously, Valve, what the hell?!) Gamepads are supported with this game, so you can use your favorite Xbox controller to play the game after adjusting your sensitivity. The game also supports virtual reality headsets, so you can enjoy the game in REAL FIRST-PERSON! The game's graphics are breathtakingly BEAUTIFUL... provided your computer can handle it!
Now for the downsides... Lately, Valve seems to be more concerned with BALANCING the game rather than trying to fix the small things that can create big problems in the long run. Like an enemy engineer using a map exploit to get into the skybox and set up a sentry, proceeding to spawncamp you and your team for an entire ten minutes. New maps will wreak havoc on your framerate if you aren't careful. Hackers banned by the VAC system can easily create a new account just to do it all over again.
Reiterating on the point I made earlier, this game has left a big impression on me. I highly recommend it to new players and look forward to its progression and development as well as many more hours logged.

There will always be those games that seem as if they could stand up to thousands leaving them.Team Fortress 2 is one of those games.Sure, it has a few bugs here and there (looking at you, dead ringer spy bug!), but they almost always end up being fixed (even if it takes a few months).The great thing about this game is that you can always improve while playing.I mean, it took more than a few hours for me to just learn to rocket jump!
The sad thing is, though, that many new players start off playing custom servers and not experiencing a pub match.Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying public servers are bad (I do love me some Zombie Fortress), but new players who experience gamemodes like x10 and Randomizer aren't seeing the real deal.A good thing to see, though, is that gamemodes like Terratorial Control (Hydro) and Medieval Mode (Degroot Keep) are starting to be revived.
In the end, I give Team Fortress 2 a 8/10.It has a few bugs and can be difficult to learn, but overall it's a good game.Playing it non-stop, though, can get boring.If you like games like Team Fortress 2, I suggest checking out Block n Load if you ever get bored of it.In conclusion, it's a great game that just has some bugs and can get tiresome.

Since I've been playing TF2 for a while now, I've decided that I will make a review about the game.
TF2 is an F2P Multiplayer FPS game with 9 classes that have different weapons and different abilities.
Since Casual wasn't that fun for me, I mostly play on community servers since there are tons of maps you can choose from.
In community servers, there are tons of very fun servers you can play one, few of them that I can name are, x10 where the weapons stats are x10. (e.g. Imagine an AK47 had a stat that said 10% faster fire speed, well in x10 it will multiply it to 100% faster fire speed. And of course, including the negatives are x10) Zombie servers where you can play as a Zombie (Medic) or as Survivors (Engineer). When a survivor dies he/she turns into a Zombie (Medic) and respawns. In other games like CS:GO they have surf servers which are included in TF2s community servers.
Then there are jump servers where you play as Demoman or Soldier, and complete maps by using your Rocket launcher (Soldier) or Stickybomb (Demoman) and your skills. There are tons of more community servers that I've might have missed or can't talk about it because there's so many.
There are hackers in this game which is quite sad to hear about, but don't worry cause there is a voting menu where you can decide which people you want to kick, then the team you're in has to decide to kick or not in order for the vote to finish.
People had said there are admin abusers in community servers, but I haven't had any experience of that feeling of having an admin abuser in community servers.
Thanks Valve for such a good game! It absolutely 100% changed my whole entire life.

Meet Your Match.
They were going in the right direction with Competitive Matchmaking, but they took a hard turn with Valve pubs and combined them into their own setting called Casual Matchmaking, which doesn't even work most of the time. Searches are slow, you'll be placed into servers out of your area, hackers have still not been dealt with, and the constant unnecessary customization blacklists (weapons, animations, sounds, models, FX, the list goes on).
Performance hasn't been getting better either. The game is so poorly optimized to the point where you have to run DX8 for high frames and minimal input lag, and yet Competitive Matchmaking forces your game to run in DX9+. Great.
My favorite thing about tf2 was when you boot it up, look through the server list, find a game mode/map you want to play and join the server. This process usually takes less than a minute. After the Meet Your Match update, now you have to wait in a matchmaking queue for a minimum of 2 minutes to find a game, and that's ANY game mode and map. This may not be an issue in America where it's very populated but in Australia we don't have the biggest audience. There's not a lot of variety in Community Servers either. You'll mainly find minecraft_trade, achievement_idle, UGC-Gaming (which are generally laggy because their servers never restart/reboot), 24/7 Dustbowl/Hightower (oh, boy), Hitler's Jewfort (which is always populated with abusive admins), and that 1% of vanilla servers with hardly any players.
This is what I want from the TF2 Team: Performance and Optimization update, the return of Valve Pubs (which shouldn't be a problem, you can keep Casual Ranking exclusively for Valve Pubs), and updated VAC. They should be working on these problems while the community creates content for the game. I say this because there are already several community updates in the making, and they look very promising. We've got the Mayann Project, the Iron Gauntlet, and the Frontline update. You should check them out.
I disagree with everything Valve has done with the past few updates, but that doesn't mean I don't recommend the game. It's not unplayable, it's just not as great as it use to be. Hopefully Valve will change their minds about their recent decisions.

Let's talk a bit about TF2..
In TF2, there are nine classes, and 3 categories.
Offense: Scout, Soldier, Pyro.
Defense: Demoman, Heavy, Engineer.
Support: Medic, Sniper, Spy.
If you want more details, go to the wiki @
Let's get to the Pros and Cons.
Pros:
Diverse Class Selection.
Gameplay that never gets old.
Fun for the whole family(?)
Hats.
Content-packed updates.
Infinite play styles.
Cons:
Highly unoptimized.
Large learning curve.
You can have 8k hours and still not know everything about the game.
The community can be really, really salty.
The updates rarely bring good content. (I.E. New maps, new weapons, etc.)
Did I mention highly unoptimized?
Your skill is judged by your material wealth.
Let's talk a bit about my mains.
I mostly play Medic and Demoman.  Medic's role is to heal the team; it's as simple as that.  Although it sounds underwhelming, it can be very exhilarating due to the fact that you are the sole reason your team is alive.  Without a Medic, the strongest of teams can crumble like a Nature Valley granola bar.
Demoman on the other hand, is centered around Offense.  Although his category is Defense, he is more of an offensive class.  His job is to dish out high amount of damage, and protect the high priority classes, such as Medic, and Engineer.  Demoman's sheer amount of mobility allows him to be almost everywhere at once, making him an ideal class for taking out the other teams' Medics and Engineers.
TF2 is a great an diverse game, and I urge you to try it.(If you haven't already!)

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding cheese cake recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1 cup digestive plain sweet biscuit crumbs
3 tablespoons sugar
3 tablespoons melted butter
40 ounces softened cream cheese
1 cup sugar
3 tablespoons flour
1 tablespoon vanilla
1 cup sour cream
4 eggs
Directions:
For The base:.
If you're using a dark pan, preheat the oven to 350. If you are using a shiny pan, 375.
Combine the crumbs, melted butter and 3 tbsp sugar well and pat onto the bottom of a 9 inch springform pan. I also like to very very lightly butter the sides of the pan so that the cheesecake will not stick later on.
Bake for 10 mins in your preheated oven and remove. Let it cool while you prepare your batter.
For the batter:.
Make sure everything is at room temperature.
Combine sugar, cheese, flour and vanilla in a big bowl and mix on medium speed till well combined. Don't forget to scrape the bowl as you're doing this.
Mix in the sour cream till its incorporated well. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing well after each addition.
Pour the batter into the springform and let it bake for 1 hour and 10 minutes After the baking time, turn off the oven and leave the door ajar. Let the cake cool in there for about 1 1/2 hours.
Remove the cake and let it cool thoroughly. Refrigerate overnight.
Release the sides of the springform.
Eat.

Let's talk a bit about TF2..
In TF2, there are nine classes, and 3 categories.
Offense: Scout, Soldier, Pyro.
Defense: Demoman, Heavy, Engineer.
Support: Medic, Sniper, Spy.
If you want more details, go to the wiki @
Let's get to the Pros and Cons.
Pros:
Diverse Class Selection.
Gameplay that never gets old.
Fun for the whole family(?)
Hats.
Content-packed updates.
Infinite play styles.
Cons:
Highly unoptimized.
Large learning curve.
You can have 8k hours and still not know everything about the game.
The community can be really, really salty.
The updates rarely bring good content. (I.E. New maps, new weapons, etc.)
Did I mention highly unoptimized?
Your skill is judged by your material wealth.
Let's talk a bit about my mains.
I mostly play Medic and Demoman.  Medic's role is to heal the team; it's as simple as that.  Although it sounds underwhelming, it can be very exhilarating due to the fact that you are the sole reason your team is alive.  Without a Medic, the strongest of teams can crumble like a Nature Valley granola bar.
Demoman on the other hand, is centered around Offense.  Although his category is Defense, he is more of an offensive class.  His job is to dish out high amount of damage, and protect the high priority classes, such as Medic, and Engineer.  Demoman's sheer amount of mobility allows him to be almost everywhere at once, making him an ideal class for taking out the other teams' Medics and Engineers.
TF2 is a great an diverse game, and I urge you to try it.(If you haven't already!)
TL;DR
Medic carries peoples' asses.
Demoman hands peoples' asses to them.
Another Con:
Eats your social life and your wallet.

Team Fortress 2 has been a source of great joy and fun for me in the past 2000 hours ive played, this game has a very special dynamic of timeless ingame graphics that still remain modern disregarding the fact this game is 10 years old. Its only in light of recent times, that this game has managed to instigate a new TF2 era of greed, hackers, un-balances, and false promises. The introdution of weapon skins in the game has moved tf2 one step closer to being like every other FPS on steam. Lack of updates and patches in recent time has led to a all time high in bugs and hackers. Valves Anti Cheat system, is a complete and utter joke, as it does nothing to stop or recognise atleast 3/4 of the hackers that are present in almost every game. Wait times for casual and competitive are ungodly, sometimes reaching into the 30 minute mark just so you can play a single game thats about to end. Ive spent my fair share of money on this game, and with little regret up until now. The game economy has begun to collapse as its main currency Refined metal, and Keys have all fluxuated unstably in the past year. The developers are unable to keep up with the expectations of its players, and have♥♥♥♥♥♥out 'major' updates such as MYM, as a poor attempt to introduce a matchmaking system that would rely on 'ranks', which might as well be glorified stickers as they have NO, ZILCH, NADA, role in sorting you into a server. This fantastic game has been overrun with hackers and scammers that are looking to make a quick profit over its broken, and dying in game currency. The time i have spent in UGC games have been some of the last fun times i have had in this game. The backlash from the TF2 community everytime Valve fails to deliver a promise has helped excavate a deep, sizeable grave for this dying game. Rest In Peace. Pootis will be missed.

text:
I have logged 5,124 hours at the time of editing this review at this moment in time.
The fact that this game is currently a decade old, showing no signs of becoming replaced, and is still currently more often than not the 3rd or 4th most played game on Steam should hint to you something;
that this game can stand up to the test of time.
This game has a special place in my heart; there's not one game that has let me know people from all sorts of walks of life, and get to play with, or against, or end up being Sandvich-sharing, congaing friends in the end with someone of the opposite team. A game that can hold my interest for 5,010 total hours, and people's overall interest for 10 whole years, is obviously a game you need to try.
Now, to the core value of the game; this is easily one of the most balanced shooters out there; this game is "Pay2Pimp", otherwise known as
Every statistically (not cosmetically) unique weapon in this game can be earned by just playing the game, and there's nothing in this game that exclusively a P2P user can get over a F2P user that actually gives them an advantage in-game, it's truly F2P, and doesn't require you to buy stuff to get ahead in the game, unless you want to really get involved in TF2's dynamic trading which is entirely optional but oh-so recommended if you like to put stuff on your head.
Team Fortress 2 has more gamemodes than any shooter I have ever seen before; and I genuinely
you to find a game with more vanilla gamemodes and variety than TF2. Along with the core implemented gamemodes in TF2, there are a ton of mods, or other gamemodes made by the community if you get tired of Capture Points (Including your default flavor; Symmetrical/Linear Control Points, and the Domination Control Point version used by Standin), Payload (Some maps come with multiple stages in this gamemode!), King of the Hill, Capture the Flag, Attack/Defend (Including your default flavor of Attack/Defend, but also Medieval Mode Attack/Defend, and End of the Line's Attack/Defend which puts a unique twist on the gamemode as a whole, playable on Snowplow. These also can come often in multiple stages per map.) Mannpower, Territory Control, Medieval Mode, PASS Time, Robot Destruction (While still in Beta, I'm counting it so nobody yells at me saying that even I forgot it!), Mann vs Machine, Player Destruction (Deliver beer to aliens to get them drunk and to crash their UFO. What more can I say?), Payload Race (Maps can come with multiple stages in this gamemode aswell!), Special Delivery, Arena Mode, along with competitive twists on these aforementioned modes, along with over a hundred offical maps to go along with these core modes, along with more maps from the community workshop being added into the game over time. You'll never have something you haven't done in TF2.
You have competitive; an intense, action-packed, fast-paced organized team versus organized team scene, a more laid-back casual, public-server stomping, conga-around-the-map-instead-of-playing-the-objective, four-Snipers-and-three-Spies-on-one-team cluster-♥♥♥♥ scene, and of course, the infamous, yet ever-so hat-involved trading scene with a functioning, living, breathing, striving economy that's just waiting for you to have the next most expensive chunk of pixels uncrated or traded for in the game. Whether you want to take this game seriously, semi-seriously, or not seriously whatsoever, you're going to have
.
This game is free; there's no risk to trying it. You have nothing to lose, and so goddamn much to gain, after playing it for a little; I wish everyone could see the magic behind this game, the same way I do. It's really just beautiful, it almost genuinely brings a tear to my eye sometimes.

text:
I have logged 5,124 hours at the time of editing this review at this moment in time.
The fact that this game is currently a decade old, showing no signs of becoming replaced, and is still currently more often than not the 3rd or 4th most played game on Steam should hint to you something;
that this game can stand up to the test of time.
This game has a special place in my heart; there's not one game that has let me know people from all sorts of walks of life, and get to play with, or against, or end up being Sandvich-sharing, congaing friends in the end with someone of the opposite team. A game that can hold my interest for 5,010 total hours, and people's overall interest for 10 whole years, is obviously a game you need to try.
Now, to the core value of the game; this is easily one of the most balanced shooters out there; this game is "Pay2Pimp", otherwise known as
Every statistically (not cosmetically) unique weapon in this game can be earned by just playing the game, and there's nothing in this game that exclusively a P2P user can get over a F2P user that actually gives them an advantage in-game, it's truly F2P, and doesn't require you to buy stuff to get ahead in the game, unless you want to really get involved in TF2's dynamic trading which is entirely optional but oh-so recommended if you like to put stuff on your head.
Team Fortress 2 has more gamemodes than any shooter I have ever seen before; and I genuinely
you to find a game with more vanilla gamemodes and variety than TF2. Along with the core implemented gamemodes in TF2, there are a ton of mods, or other gamemodes made by the community if you get tired of Capture Points (Including your default flavor; Symmetrical/Linear Control Points, and the Domination Control Point version used by Standin), Payload (Some maps come with multiple stages in this gamemode!), King of the Hill, Capture the Flag, Attack/Defend (Including your default flavor of Attack/Defend, but also Medieval Mode Attack/Defend, and End of the Line's Attack/Defend which puts a unique twist on the gamemode as a whole, playable on Snowplow. These also can come often in multiple stages per map.) Mannpower, Territory Control, Medieval Mode, PASS Time, Robot Destruction (While still in Beta, I'm counting it so nobody yells at me saying that even I forgot it!), Mann vs Machine, Player Destruction (Deliver beer to aliens to get them drunk and to crash their UFO. What more can I say?), Payload Race (Maps can come with multiple stages in this gamemode aswell!), Special Delivery, Arena Mode, along with competitive twists on these aforementioned modes, along with over a hundred offical maps to go along with these core modes, along with more maps from the community workshop being added into the game over time. You'll never have something you haven't done in TF2.
You have competitive; an intense, action-packed, fast-paced organized team versus organized team scene, a more laid-back casual, public-server stomping, conga-around-the-map-instead-of-playing-the-objective, four-Snipers-and-three-Spies-on-one-team cluster-♥♥♥♥ scene, and of course, the infamous, yet ever-so hat-involved trading scene with a functioning, living, breathing, striving economy that's just waiting for you to have the next most expensive chunk of pixels uncrated or traded for in the game. Whether you want to take this game seriously, semi-seriously, or not seriously whatsoever, you're going to have
.
This game is free; there's no risk to trying it. You have nothing to lose, and so goddamn much to gain, after playing it for a little; I wish everyone could see the magic behind this game, the same way I do. It's really just beautiful, it almost genuinely brings a tear to my eye sometimes.

Right, I'm not sure exactly how many reviews I have done, or the level of intelligence at which I wrote them, but here's my review of Team Fortress 2.
I love this game - even with a measly 800 something hours. I feel that even in this time I'm able to provide a solid review of this fantastic game, and one to try it is!
The gameplay is always refreshing; I'm a pubstomping prick, so I like to join Valve servers (not to mention that I have a frankly trash connection to servers such as Skial, but that's beside the point.) and every time I do it's a new experience - at least more or less. Since TF2 is now free, there's a huge amount of "F2P" noobies, these guys are always fun. They're the sort of player's I'd compare to Dodos - completely oblivious to
and even they seem to still love the game.
Even those who are slightly more experienced manage to make the game entertaining, it's always nice to see half a team of "Unusual" hat wearers pocket healing "minecraftboy2005", who is playing sniper with all default items. This brings me on to my next point, weapons:
The fact that the "Stock weapons" are arguably the best in the game makes for extreme helpfulness for new players. I tend to use custom skins or remodels for stock weapons, such as the AWPer hand, or the Botkiller varieties of stock - and these are purely cosmetic changes that make the game that little bit special.
Team Fortress 2 is possibly the most cosmetic-based game out there, you can't join one server without seeing someone wearing anything from a Gibbus to an Unusual "Burning" Team Captain, or even the Anger. This opens up doors to a world of opportunity for players who want to make their character that little bit more individual. TF2 is known as a "War-themed hat simulator", while this comic-y joke is very funny, it does actually represent the enormous scene that TF2 has for trading, selling and buying. TF2 has a flourishing market, from Bill's hats, to Buds, to keys. This means that you can literally make TF2 a living if you invested enough time and money into it
- which many people do (almost). How many other games have a FREAKIN' frying pan that is worth more than a bog-standard car? Not that many!
The TF2 community is so wonderful, as mentioned before, the playerbase is something to marvel upon. From F2Ps to pros, everyone seems to love eachother. Rarely do I see any salty people in games, though those who are ususally get talked down by lenny spams
.
Hackers get taken down like a lead balloon, this is something I praise TF2 for. As soon as the "Get good get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; binds come in, there's instantly a vote-kick. This happens across teams, if somebody is suspicious of "Big weed" who's 200 and 0, there's usually someone there to spectate and confirm these suspicions.
Well, that's my less-than-brief review of Team Fortress 2, I hope you enjoyed reading it, as I am slightly new to this review scene, but I feel so passionately about this game!
I'd absolutely play it, there's really no reason not to try - it's free, ya damn fool!

Team Fortress 2 is one of the more classic examples of class based multiplayer shooters in gaming history, and while I could give a whole big page about the good, the bad, and the ugly of this game, i'm just going to give my experience so far, what i think is good, bad, and ugly.
My experience so far has been fairly good, I've played worse, much worse multiplayer based games, but there's a underlining tone and set of players that just can become a pain. Not the Free To Play's as the some would say, not the Tryhards (as personally i am VERY competitive and i guess that makes me a tryhard cause i get into it all a lot), but rather a set of people that just get so bored or so overly skilled at the game that they just steam roll teams giving their all (or the few players that can't fight back cause it's 4v12 thanks to their team being lazy or jerks)
Granted, ALL games have this, I know this. The problem is that TF2 has a little more then too many people like this and people just let it slide because you for some reaon can't have fun and try to win at the same time; so matches become annoying, boring, or pitiful. Speaking of annoying, boring, and pitiful, if your pretty unentertained by meme's, chat spam, and hackers, best avoid this game, cause there's a lot more of those kinds of people as well alongside the college kids that would rather hide behind their monitors and say their better by score. (Remember the days you could die a lot and no one cared long as you helped? The days gone by and literally every other game)
The game its self is pretty simple, (though the comics, story, and other insanity of this game is not. To me, and many others, just makes it a lot better though) Red Verses Blu, Red usually defends whatever the objective is, Blu attacks it, or in some game modes, it's just the teams going at it to see how long they can hold a point or kill more people. The 9 classes, though some i am completely terrible at, are fun, have unique styles, and there is definatly a set of weapons for a class that'll not only adhere to your playstyle, but make you love any of the playable classes even more (Such as, I adore playing the Engineer class, and am a very straight forward supportive team member in the sense of killing a lot of people, and keep a lot of people alive to help them kill or kill for)
The Co-op mode Mann Verses Machine is six players defend from waves of robots, be them the size of the characters, or giants, and they always come in hordes. The upside? It's fun, challenging but not really stressful as long as you work together and play smart. Downside? You have to pay a dollar for one set of rounds on a map just for somewhat decent or normal items you could get randomly. Plus, a lot of people either are too relaxed and unhelpful, or are more worried about beating the mode, getting their loot from winning, and will kick you from the servers if you don't play 1 of 6 "recommended classes" for that mode. Easy way to say it, forget playing what you want, how you want, unless your with friends or have played sets of maps for 300 tours. (Which depending on the set of maps, can range from 3 to 6 maps, with 4 to 7 rounds, times that by 300 complete tours and see why some people are a little TOO into that mode)
Their also adding a competitive 6 verse 6 mode, same comments about Mann Verses Machine exist, but reduce the number of "recommened classes" to 4 then 6.
So what's good that i may or may not have mentioned? It's fun, creative, got good characters and good weapons that Valve try to fairly balance and the community behind tf2 can submit and have a chance to have their homemade content become a actual item in the game.
Bad? Players are tend to be annoying, overly competitive, unwilling to listen or change class despite it may help the team, multi isn't really fair and subsequently fun due to that at times. Matches are utter clusters of horror and annoyences because if you try to do the thing this video game was clearly meant for; competing and having fun at the same time (AKA, a multiplayers goal of making you fighting and win for fun on top of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ comments, jokes, and rebuttles will be made for that remark i'm sure), and the co-op or competitive mode are a little too "Do this and win, or go away" themed with palyers anymore
Finally, the Ugly is simply a lot of items, or normal items of greater quality need to be bought with money (including the actually challenging or fun side of Mann Verses Machine). Crates and Boxes that can be bought or get randomly require almost 3 dollars to open only to get a 10 cent item on the community market for items (To give you a example of how ridiculous this is or can be, a gold gun, only winnable every 7 tours in Mann Verses Machine is worth anywhere between 20 to 40 dollars, but a normal vintage item that's been around since the earlier days of the game is only worth a dollar.) and the updates and fifty fifty of what they bring, be them weapon improvements or new maps. Also, some updates of recent have things called "contracts" which basically mean do something a certain amount of times to get a crate or free reskinned weapon of low quality. That's not fun either.
So, in roughly a sentence or two, do i recommend Valve's Team Fortress 2? Somewhat, but i think honestly it's not a question anymore of if it's good or bad, but if the game still holds up. The answer I give is simply, no. It is fun, and it's nice to get in a half decent match where people try but remember it is a game and lay back to have fun, but the thing both Valve and tf2's community has failed to do is one simple word. Evolve.
Valve refuses to listen, update properly, and even care enough to give this game a proper team. The player community just let's things slide, treats each other like garbage for wanting to try and win on a public game and even try to defend the game with excuses; the "best one" I remember being "It's *curse word* casual, no one cares about winning because it's not fun to win. That's why their making a competitive mode." So... it's a game between a rock and a hard place, a developer that doesn't want to deal with it anymore, a community that clearly doesn't either, and hopefully will just go out peacefully unlike how other games have. I do think it's fun, but if it's developer and community refuse to sort things out and make tf2 a good game again, then there's no point to play this. It's fun, but not a game that holds up anymore; at all so take what you will and take a chance. You might have fun, or like many and soon myself, leave this game as a relic of Valve's past.

Finally, there isn't much variation when it comes to guns. The only guns are The Dragon's Fury and some sort of jetpack along with a gas can, a flamethrower, and a trumpet flamethrower.
My final judgement? I feel like if Valve tries to add new classes (because only one class of Pyro gets boring fast), fixes matchmaking, and adds more varied weapons, Pyro Fortress 2 could become a playable game.

This game has been nothing but a test bed for in-game economies. Now that CS:GO is making bank off of weapon skins, TF2 has been scooting closer and closer to the edge of Valve's worktable- and straight into the shredder.
-Pyro is a monstrosity that was given a bunch of rainbow-colored band aids to try and pretend it wasn't fundamentally flawed. There are people super invested in its meta, so they'll give you a nice 'lenny face' and go back to combo-spamming people into corners & afterburning people post-mortem.
-Melee is fundamentally flawed as the game treats melee swings like a projectile/surgeons knife- meaning if your crosshair isn't aimed directly at any part of the hitbox you can completely miss at point blank range. Now add hitbox latency.
-New items have been %90 community made, this wouldn't be a bad thing if they were new weapons or something, but it's nothing but stupid cosmetics. Go look at some of the top-rated workshop weapons, and you'll see a correlation with some of the weapons in Overwatch. Valve didn't want to waste their resources programming new weapons- so Blizzard's gonna sap their playerbase.
-Every time they add a new game mode, they never expand on the concept. Medieval mode? Special Delivery?? At least payload race got a a few maps- aaaand they're all community made. MvM is the only exception- but that's only because it was making Valve some good money for a while.
-Sometimes the games weapons get completely rebalanced. This produced weapon unlocks that were straight upgrades for a while, but now Valve has wisened up and decided to make unlocks as BORING as possible.
-Speaking of weapons, there are so many weapons that give you guarunteed critical hits (3 times the base damage, mind you) that any class has more than a fair chance at defeating a Heavy Weapons Guy. The skill ceiling doesn't come anywhere close to the inherent advantage some of these weapons give you.
-Valve servers are a soul-crushing experience. There are people ranging from 'installed the game 5 minutes ago' to '5000+ hours'. It's so uncoordinated that people on your team will instruct the opposing team to CAPTURE POINTS if necessary.
Valve might not be upfront about straight up killing their game, but at this point they're just throwing the veteran players a bone by adding competitive matchmaking.

Team Fortress 2 is a FPS with cartoonish graphics and heavy reliance on teamwork. It used to be paid, but it went free to play in 2011.
The graphics, despite being a bit old already, still look good and stylish. The maps are usually well-designed and interesting to look at.
The gameplay stands out from your other FPS games for being very different than conventional shooters out there. You can pick from nine different classes: offensive (Scout, Soldier, Pyro), defensive (Demo, Heavy, Engineer) and support (Medic, Sniper, Spy), each with their own unique tools, style, strengths and weaknesses. This forces you to work with your teammates to cover each other's weakpoints and emerge victorious.
There are two main gamemodes: PvP and MvM. The former has a lot of sub-modes, such as Payload, Control Points, Attack / Defense, King of the Hill, or Capture The Flag. The latter, on the other hand, pits a team of six players in a co-op tower defense mode against hordes of bloodthirsty robots, with the objective of preventing them from delivering a bomb to the end of the map.
There is a lot of unlockable weapons, which allow you to customize and change your gameplay style, as well as a ton (and I mean a ton) of cosmetic items, which serve no purpose besides looking cool.
The music, while it can't be heard outside of main menu or promotional videos, is very good and fun to listen to even outside the game.
Unfortunately, this game also has cons. Due to the amount of hats content, the game is very heavy, so computers that aren't brand-new might experience some performance issues. Also, due to it being free to play, pub servers are often filled with noobs who have no idea what they're doing, which can destroy your gaming experience considering the game is teamwork-reliant. Multiple Snipers and Spies is a common occurence.
The community is also... well, not the worst, but one of the worst. Just a quick glance at the forums reveals a ton of unusual and Australium-toting "git gud" elitists who aren't very pleasant to talk to if you're new... or in general. However, that doesn't mean there aren't any people who are actually helpful towards newcomers.
Overall, I highly recommend this game to everyone. FPS veterans however should be prepared for a drastically different experience.

Team Fortress 2 is a FPS with cartoonish graphics and heavy reliance on teamwork. It used to be paid, but it went free to play in 2011.
The graphics, despite being a bit old already, still look good and stylish. The maps are usually well-designed and interesting to look at.
The gameplay stands out from your other FPS games for being very different than conventional shooters out there. You can pick from nine different classes: offensive (Scout, Soldier, Pyro), defensive (Demo, Heavy, Engineer) and support (Medic, Sniper, Spy), each with their own unique tools, style, strengths and weaknesses. This forces you to work with your teammates to cover each other's weakpoints and emerge victorious.
There are two main gamemodes: PvP and MvM. The former has a lot of sub-modes, such as Payload, Control Points, Attack / Defense, King of the Hill, or Capture The Flag. The latter, on the other hand, pits a team of six players in a co-op tower defense mode against hordes of bloodthirsty robots, with the objective of preventing them from delivering a bomb to the end of the map.
There is a lot of unlockable weapons, which allow you to customize and change your gameplay style, as well as a ton (and I mean a ton) of cosmetic items, which serve no purpose besides looking cool.
The music, while it can't be heard outside of main menu or promotional videos, is very good and fun to listen to even outside the game.
Unfortunately, this game also has cons. Due to the amount of hats content, the game is very heavy, so computers that aren't brand-new might experience some performance issues. Also, due to it being free to play, pub servers are often filled with noobs who have no idea what they're doing, which can destroy your gaming experience considering the game is teamwork-reliant. Multiple Snipers and Spies is a common occurence.
The community is also... well, not the worst, but one of the worst. Just a quick glance at the forums reveals a ton of unusual and Australium-toting "git gud" elitists who aren't very pleasant to talk to if you're new... or in general. However, that doesn't mean there aren't any people who are actually helpful towards newcomers.
Overall, I highly recommend this game to everyone. FPS veterans however should be prepared for a drastically different experience.

Pros: (before i start, i would like to say, please remeber that this is my opnion and your ideas may differ.)
1. ITS @#$@IN FREE!
2. it has multiple creative yet simple gamemodes that are all fun and easy to adapt too.
3. it has one of the most diverse, comedic, and briiliant cast of charachters and classes that i've ever seen, their funny to listen too, always have something to say, and are always sporting nice attire.
4. ok this one is a little touchy, it has one of the most balanced systems of weapons and classes i have seen, this is usually based on the time and how recent some weapons are, but i usually find the weapons in team fortress 2 too be extremley balanced, yes there are some pretty controversially overpowered weapons in the game (ex. backburner,phlog,danger shield, crit-a-cola, etc.) however each usually has a pretty solid counter or sutibale enough draw backs.
5. compared to most other communities out there, this games community is relatively good.
6. has a pretty good f2p format, now others say "you need to pay real money to get the good and overpowred weapons" but the truth is, the stock (regular) weapons are statistically the best and superior to the unlocks in overall versatlity, and also, you can aquire all of the weapon unlocks through achives, which you can get pretty easily on an achivement server in like, 15 minutes.
7. is just fun in general, all the different ways you can play mean that there is always some new crazy and fun strat just around a corner, and it never gets old, theres just sometihing so addicting about this game.
Cons:
1. while i did say earlier that the community was pretty ok compared too most, there is no "good" gaming community all the way through, theres always gona be some bad apples in the community of any game, and some may have more than others, personally i think Tf2 has less, i have to admit it still has a lot of just overall bad community members, hackers,scammers,some may say 8 year old squeakers, tryhards with now sense of decency (i say this because there are some good tryhards, as in they have honor and decency), or just overall ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s telling people how much they suck at this game, or how they suck because their f2p. I love this game and i wish there were less garbage people in the community, but hey, what are you gona do.
2. fps issues, im not totally educated on all this, but from what i hear, the frame rate of tf2 can be garbage at times, some people with beast gaming compters can't even run it at optimal settings, i never notice this for some reason but if it exsits, then i have to put it on here.
3. valve neglects this game, ok this might raise some controversy, but i dont think i have that influence so im going to say it, valve completly squanders this games potential as an actual game, now some may say, "but we have had like 3 campains in the last year and a half, anf they added new unsuals and stuff" yes, but tell me, whens the last time you saw a real new weapon in TF2? like 3 ♥♥♥♥in years, and even then, it was only 3 and all of them were gimmick weapons and only one or 2 were even remotely useful while the other was complete garbage, now, the lack of new weaps is something everyone complains about, but im not here to completely talk about that, rather id like to say that valve pours like 75% of their attention into cs:go, now no, im not trashtalking cs:go, in fact i quite like it, however the amount of new overall game features added to cs:go, as well as updated VAC sytems, towers massively over that of TF2, if you just look at the items, skins, and weaps added too cs:go, and compare it too TF2, you could probably tell the difference, now i should stop before this becomes even more of a rant, so I will end this with, valve pays little to no attention to this game and its potential.
now i think ive wasted enough of your time so good day, or afternoon, or night.
final rating
gameplay:10/10
gameplay plus other aspects (ex. community) 9/10
P.S for the final rating i would like to say that i included 2 seperate counters because, not to give the game more almighty praise, but i cant find anything wrong with the core gameply, some argue the weaps can be O.P, but no matter how insanely powerful, there is always a counter. if you notice i forgot something or am incorrect, that kind of thing, please feel free to comment on this review and share your opnion with me, please just keep in mind that this is my personal opnion, thank you.

With more hats than weapons at this point I feel it's preety clear that the game can be for some a hat simulator. My opinions are sometimes mixed about the cosmetics since they are often used as fillers for updates.
If I had to give an overall score, it would probably be about 7/10. The game isn't bad, but it could be a lot better. Has to be one of the most unique FPS I have every played. What sets this apart from other FPS games shoud be obvious. Your not some soldier with a ak-47, 3 flashbang grenades, and a melee knife, running around shooting people in a typical game of team deathmatch. Instead you get to choose what you want to be, And How you want to play! Alas! you don't have to be stuck being a typical COD soldier! You can be an engineer! spy! scout!  pyro! demoman! medic! lions, tigers and bears oh my! You can have very unique weapons each with very unique skill sets! You can dress up your favorite classes with hats and apparel! You can craft items, weapons and hats! You can play unique game-modes such as payload, mann vs machine, special delivery! You can dance! You can taunt! What Other FPS game have all these? Most creative and inventive FPS game thus far hands down!

The idea behind the game seems as if it would make for some good fun. Well, the game is fun. Unfortunately it's taken a turn for the worse. Now it's constantly being ruined by bad updates, and if you fall into the same hole as I did-all the microtransactions of hats, skins, etc. will ruin it too. Playing this game will most likely empty your wallet, as you will be scrambling to buy hats, weapons, keys, passes, and more. But not only hats et al. will soil your experience. The updates are procedurally getting worse, with the addition of "Counterstrike Fortress 2 (Tough Break, Gun Mettle, etc)." Hopefully, if you do decide to play this game, you won't run into these problems, and you will be able to enjoy the game for what it is.
The game at least runs farily well, as long as you have some RAM (≥4GB), and a midrange processor (No graphics card needed!). On my old Mac Mini, the game ran fairly well, with occasional freezes that lasted for 5+ seconds. You will need good internet to be able to play the game without lag spikes, so you don't have to blame lag for everything. Controller-wise, I find the game doesn't work too well, so if you are looking to use this with
, be warned (especially since the steam link controllers tend to be interesting to use).
Gameplay is very fun on its own. The basics of gameplay are as follows: There are two teams, RED and BLU. They compete in a fire fight to win some objective, whether it be returning a flaming briefcase to your base or pushing a cart with a bomb on it into the enemy base. There are many unique modes to play, including Capture the Flag, Attack/Defense, Payload, Special Delivery, and more. There are over 200 weapons to use, so you will be able to pick favorites and eventually hone your skills to be a great player.
In the earlier days of TF2, updates were very fun and unique, such as the introduction of humans versus robots with Mann vs. Machine, and the Hatless Update, which added coaching, training, voting, duels, bot improvements, and much more. But recently, updates have been getting a bit unoriginal. And by a bit, I mean a lot. With the introduction of the Gun Mettle update, the game was starting to look more like Counter Strike: Global Offensive than TF2. This CS:GO update added skins, cases, stattrak, and more things that completely copied CS:GO (it's totally okay, Valve owns both games). The only good part of this update gameplay-wise was contracts (and new maps), a concept that has stuck around with the Invasion update and Tough Break update. This shows that Valve is still listening to some things we say, and trying to encourage fun gameplay rather than trading hats, weapons, etc. for profit.
This part of the review isn't influential upon my rating, this is just my warning to you. I've wasted a lot of money on this game, and the end result was a negative profit. Don't fall into the same hole as I did. Don't become jealous of other players who don expensive hats and equip fancy weapon skins and crap like that. You
end up wasting lots of money. You will start wasting your life on the market trying to make profits. You will waste your items and money on gambling for virtual hats and weapons. Seriously, don't let jealousy overcome you and cause you to waste a lot. But if you do end up doing this, you will be lucky if you end up making a profit. Despite the description of the game, TF2 is NOT about who has the best hats. It's about having fun and enjoying the game for what it is.
The game runs well on almost any setup, except for use with a controller. Gameplay is fun and (mostly) unique, with many modes and weapons. Updates have changed the way the game works, and have added fun ways to enjoy TF2. Updates have also ruined the game partially due to a lack of creativity from Valve. Jealousy should be avoided while playing this game, as it will lead you into wasting money on hats and weapons. Enjoy the game for what it is, not for what it isn't. Based on gameplay, I would give the game a 10/10, but on the terms of other additions for the game, I'd rate it 7/10.

The attack on Pearl Harbor was a surprise military strike by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service against the United States naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii Territory, on the morning of December 7, 1941. The attack, also known as the Battle of Pearl Harbor, led to the United States' entry into World War II. The Japanese military leadership referred to the attack as the Hawaii Operation and Operation AI, and as Operation Z during its planning.
Japan intended the attack as a preventive action to keep the U.S. Pacific Fleet from interfering with military actions they planned in Southeast Asia against overseas territories of the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and the United States. Over the next seven hours there were coordinated Japanese attacks on the U.S.-held Philippines, Guam and Wake Island and on the British Empire in Malaya, Singapore, and Hong Kong.
The attack commenced at 7:48 a.m. Hawaiian Time (18:18 UTC). The base was attacked by 353 Imperial Japanese aircraft (including fighters, level and dive bombers, and torpedo bombers) in two waves, launched from six aircraft carriers. All eight U.S. Navy battleships were damaged, with four sunk. All but the USS Arizona were later raised, and six were returned to service and went on to fight in the war. The Japanese also sank or damaged three cruisers, three destroyers, an anti-aircraft training ship, and one minelayer. One hundred eighty-eight U.S. aircraft were destroyed; 2,403 Americans were killed and 1,178 others were wounded. Important base installations such as the power station, dry dock, shipyard, maintenance, and fuel and torpedo storage facilities, as well as the submarine piers and headquarters building (also home of the intelligence section), were not attacked. Japanese losses were light: 29 aircraft and five midget submarines lost, and 64 servicemen killed. One Japanese sailor, Kazuo Sakamaki, was captured.
The surprise attack came as a profound shock to the American people and led directly to the American entry into World War II in both the Pacific and European theaters. The following day, December 8, the United States declared war on Japan, and several days later, on December 11, Germany and Italy declared war on the U.S. The U.S. responded with a declaration of war against Germany and Italy. Domestic support for non-interventionism, which had been fading since the Fall of France in 1940, disappeared.
There were numerous historical precedents for unannounced military action by Japan, but the lack of any formal warning, particularly while negotiations were still apparently ongoing, led President Franklin D. Roosevelt to proclaim December 7, 1941, "a date which will live in infamy". Because the attack happened without a declaration of war and without explicit warning, the attack on Pearl Harbor was later judged in the Tokyo Trials to be a war crime.

The idea behind the game seems as if it would make for some good fun. Well, the game is fun. Unfortunately it's taken a turn for the worse. Now it's constantly being ruined by bad updates, and if you fall into the same hole as I did-all the microtransactions of hats, skins, etc. will ruin it too. Playing this game will most likely empty your wallet, as you will be scrambling to buy hats, weapons, keys, passes, and more. But not only hats et al. will soil your experience. The updates are procedurally getting worse, with the addition of "Counterstrike Fortress 2 (Tough Break, Gun Mettle, etc)." Hopefully, if you do decide to play this game, you won't run into these problems, and you will be able to enjoy the game for what it is.
The game at least runs farily well, as long as you have some RAM (≥4GB), and a midrange processor (No graphics card needed!). On my old Mac Mini, the game ran fairly well, with occasional freezes that lasted for 5+ seconds. You will need good internet to be able to play the game without lag spikes, so you don't have to blame lag for everything. Controller-wise, I find the game doesn't work too well, so if you are looking to use this with
, be warned (especially since the steam link controllers tend to be interesting to use).
Gameplay is very fun on its own. The basics of gameplay are as follows: There are two teams, RED and BLU. They compete in a fire fight to win some objective, whether it be returning a flaming briefcase to your base or pushing a cart with a bomb on it into the enemy base. There are many unique modes to play, including Capture the Flag, Attack/Defense, Payload, Special Delivery, and more. There are over 200 weapons to use, so you will be able to pick favorites and eventually hone your skills to be a great player.
In the earlier days of TF2, updates were very fun and unique, such as the introduction of humans versus robots with Mann vs. Machine, and the Hatless Update, which added coaching, training, voting, duels, bot improvements, and much more. But recently, updates have been getting a bit unoriginal. And by a bit, I mean a lot. With the introduction of the Gun Mettle update, the game was starting to look more like Counter Strike: Global Offensive than TF2. This CS:GO update added skins, cases, stattrak, and more things that completely copied CS:GO (it's totally okay, Valve owns both games). The only good part of this update gameplay-wise was contracts (and new maps), a concept that has stuck around with the Invasion update and Tough Break update. This shows that Valve is still listening to some things we say, and trying to encourage fun gameplay rather than trading hats, weapons, etc. for profit.
This part of the review isn't influential upon my rating, this is just my warning to you. I've wasted a lot of money on this game, and the end result was a negative profit. Don't fall into the same hole as I did. Don't become jealous of other players who don expensive hats and equip fancy weapon skins and crap like that. You
end up wasting lots of money. You will start wasting your life on the market trying to make profits. You will waste your items and money on gambling for virtual hats and weapons. Seriously, don't let jealousy overcome you and cause you to waste a lot. But if you do end up doing this, you will be lucky if you end up making a profit. Despite the description of the game, TF2 is NOT about who has the best hats. It's about having fun and enjoying the game for what it is.
The game runs well on almost any setup, except for use with a controller. Gameplay is fun and (mostly) unique, with many modes and weapons. Updates have changed the way the game works, and have added fun ways to enjoy TF2. Updates have also ruined the game partially due to a lack of creativity from Valve. Jealousy should be avoided while playing this game, as it will lead you into wasting money on hats and weapons. Enjoy the game for what it is, not for what it isn't. Based on gameplay, I would give the game a 10/10, but on the terms of other additions for the game, I'd rate it 7/10.

The attack on Pearl Harbor was a surprise military strike by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service against the United States naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii Territory, on the morning of December 7, 1941. The attack, also known as the Battle of Pearl Harbor, led to the United States' entry into World War II. The Japanese military leadership referred to the attack as the Hawaii Operation and Operation AI, and as Operation Z during its planning.
Japan intended the attack as a preventive action to keep the U.S. Pacific Fleet from interfering with military actions they planned in Southeast Asia against overseas territories of the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and the United States. Over the next seven hours there were coordinated Japanese attacks on the U.S.-held Philippines, Guam and Wake Island and on the British Empire in Malaya, Singapore, and Hong Kong.
The attack commenced at 7:48 a.m. Hawaiian Time (18:18 UTC). The base was attacked by 353 Imperial Japanese aircraft (including fighters, level and dive bombers, and torpedo bombers) in two waves, launched from six aircraft carriers. All eight U.S. Navy battleships were damaged, with four sunk. All but the USS Arizona were later raised, and six were returned to service and went on to fight in the war. The Japanese also sank or damaged three cruisers, three destroyers, an anti-aircraft training ship, and one minelayer. One hundred eighty-eight U.S. aircraft were destroyed; 2,403 Americans were killed and 1,178 others were wounded. Important base installations such as the power station, dry dock, shipyard, maintenance, and fuel and torpedo storage facilities, as well as the submarine piers and headquarters building (also home of the intelligence section), were not attacked. Japanese losses were light: 29 aircraft and five midget submarines lost, and 64 servicemen killed. One Japanese sailor, Kazuo Sakamaki, was captured.
The surprise attack came as a profound shock to the American people and led directly to the American entry into World War II in both the Pacific and European theaters. The following day, December 8, the United States declared war on Japan, and several days later, on December 11, Germany and Italy declared war on the U.S. The U.S. responded with a declaration of war against Germany and Italy. Domestic support for non-interventionism, which had been fading since the Fall of France in 1940, disappeared.
There were numerous historical precedents for unannounced military action by Japan, but the lack of any formal warning, particularly while negotiations were still apparently ongoing, led President Franklin D. Roosevelt to proclaim December 7, 1941, "a date which will live in infamy". Because the attack happened without a declaration of war and without explicit warning, the attack on Pearl Harbor was later judged in the Tokyo Trials to be a war crime.

* DISCLAIMER: IGNORE THE THUMBS-UP, AND PRETEND IT'S A NEUTRAL RATING. *
I've been a TF player since TFC, and TF2 is a nice successor. I believe vanilla TF2 is still the best version. Not to say all the additons of hats and other items have ruined the game, but I feel that certain charm vanished long ago. It was also perfectly balanced. If you've played from the beginning, some new things were weird getting used to, but you deal with it, now. If you're a new player, there's a good chance you'll hate this game, at first. You'll see a giant mess in practically any server you choose. You'll see stray lasers, Soldiers parachuting around, a Demo spamming pill grenades, another Demo wildly swinging a sword and zooming around, a Heavy actually fighting, a Heavy doing nothing but crouching and throwing out sandwiches, a Spy walking around in a cardboard box, a newbie Sniper who doesn't understand you can't shoot through windows, just so much crap going on. You'll be confused. You'll be lost. You'll be unsure if you even want to keep playing.
If you get over all of that, and realize this is basically "Absolute Chaos: The Video Game", you'll be wondering how you acquire all those neat and fancy weapons that you do not have, and everyone else seems to have. Well, there are several ways of obtaining new weapons. First is being patient. Every now and then, the server will give you a random weapon after a death. Impatient? You can buy some through the in-game Mann Co. store with real money, or some can also be purchased through the Steam community marketplace for much cheaper. Before you go there, no, this actually isn't a Pay-to-Win game. I'll let you in on a secret. Ready?
- Stock weapons (the ones you start out with) are the best ones. -
Sure, there might be one or two that are direct upgrades, but honestly, you can still play just fine with nothing but stock loadouts. Most other weapons are gimmicks for you to mess around with for a few lives, then switch to something else. Don't let anyone tell you different. It's not an issue of enjoying using them, as I am not denying they can be fun, but for best results, roll stock.
If you like map variety, you're in luck. There are a ton of maps, official and fan-made. There's also a very nice selection of different game modes. Payload (attacking team pushes a bomb cart to certain points of the map, while defending team tries to hold them off until time runs out), Payload race (A cart for each team), Control Point (Tug-of-war of capping  different points on the map in order), Capture the Flag (I mean, what is there to say? It's CTF, but instead of a flag, it's a briefcase), Arena (Basically Counter-Strike round rules), and some others which you can discover for yourself. Variety is not an issue.
I subscribe to the belief that this game got worse since it went F2P. Cheer or boo that notion all you want, but in my experience, the community is nowhere near what it used to be. Thanks to the F2P model, that obviously means anyone can play, which contributed to the influx of players that make me want to set myself on fire, and jump out a window. Granted, good F2P players exist, but my ♥♥♥♥ing god, the level of human garbage you can encounter is staggering. I'm not even talking about their skill level, but their personalities alone. Do you like completely unfunny text binds of memes being spammed? Yes? Welcome home. No? Prepare your sanity, or completely turn off the chat via the console. (Google it.) Go ahead and just mute every player when you enter a game, as well. These often occur in official Valve servers, but community ones can suffer the same. There are also good people, but you may have to sift through the dirt, first. Just be ready.
The game itself, if you don't mind the sheer chaos, can be a fun time. There are no iron-sights, grenades (sans the Demoman's grenade launcher), or ranks. So, if you're tired of online games that favor players who play more, give this one a try. Yeah, they'll still have more weapons than you, but none of them came at a certain time, and you can get them at any time. Also, remember, stock weapons are (mostly) king. Oh, you can craft weapons, too. Though that may also take time to get the one you want.
Like I said, my view on this game is pretty much 50/50. There are aspects that I enjoy, and others I loathe. Sometimes I have to take long breaks. Sometimes it's all I play in a day. It's weird. It's a ♥♥♥♥ing weird game.

I'm assuming most people reading this have some inkling on what TF2 is, so I'll just cut to the knitty-gritty.
Pros:
* Basically free, and if you pay five bucks you can get access to just about all of the weapon content. Valve has handled the F2P model pretty well.
* LOTS of content, especially weapons; the game is rebalanced every so often so there's a lot of gameplay diversity.
* Both competitive and casual scene, plus a large community. Don't know how the game's doing community server-wise anymore, but I'm sure you can still find a pretty good number of modded servers, custom maps and the like.
* The classes are their core are all great. TF2 is basically an expansive MMO built off of really good core gameplay. With the amount of unlocks this game has to offer, you're sure to find a playstyle that clicks.
Cons
* Pretty bloated now. Lot of distracting cosmetics and "crates" (dlc ads basically), plus the file size is bigger than it has any right to be.
* Doesn't run well on low-end computers. Seriously, it was released in 2007 and it's optimized like garbage. And here I can run Killing Floor 2 on my toaster.
*
slowly dying. There's still activity for sure, but the game's not going to last forever. The new updates are usually pretty hit or miss.
Recommended if you're looking to get into the FPS genre or just want some teamplay action, but only if you have some pretty good specs. And of course it's virtually free, so no harm in trying it. But if you've already played this game before and are wondering if you absolutely need to redownload it... you're not missing that much. You'll probably replay it for a couple weeks and forget about it. YMMV.

* DISCLAIMER: IGNORE THE THUMBS-UP, AND PRETEND IT'S A NEUTRAL RATING. *
I've been a TF player since TFC, and TF2 is a nice successor. I believe vanilla TF2 is still the best version. Not to say all the additons of hats and other items have ruined the game, but I feel that certain charm vanished long ago. It was also perfectly balanced. If you've played from the beginning, some new things were weird getting used to, but you deal with it, now. If you're a new player, there's a good chance you'll hate this game, at first. You'll see a giant mess in practically any server you choose. You'll see stray lasers, Soldiers parachuting around, a Demo spamming pill grenades, another Demo wildly swinging a sword and zooming around, a Heavy actually fighting, a Heavy doing nothing but crouching and throwing out sandwiches, a Spy walking around in a cardboard box, a newbie Sniper who doesn't understand you can't shoot through windows, just so much crap going on. You'll be confused. You'll be lost. You'll be unsure if you even want to keep playing.
If you get over all of that, and realize this is basically "Absolute Chaos: The Video Game", you'll be wondering how you acquire all those neat and fancy weapons that you do not have, and everyone else seems to have. Well, there are several ways of obtaining new weapons. First is being patient. Every now and then, the server will give you a random weapon after a death. Impatient? You can buy some through the in-game Mann Co. store with real money, or some can also be purchased through the Steam community marketplace for much cheaper. Before you go there, no, this actually isn't a Pay-to-Win game. I'll let you in on a secret. Ready?
- Stock weapons (the ones you start out with) are the best ones. -
Sure, there might be one or two that are direct upgrades, but honestly, you can still play just fine with nothing but stock loadouts. Most other weapons are gimmicks for you to mess around with for a few lives, then switch to something else. Don't let anyone tell you different. It's not an issue of enjoying using them, as I am not denying they can be fun, but for best results, roll stock.
If you like map variety, you're in luck. There are a ton of maps, official and fan-made. There's also a very nice selection of different game modes. Payload (attacking team pushes a bomb cart to certain points of the map, while defending team tries to hold them off until time runs out), Payload race (A cart for each team), Control Point (Tug-of-war of capping  different points on the map in order), Capture the Flag (I mean, what is there to say? It's CTF, but instead of a flag, it's a briefcase), Arena (Basically Counter-Strike round rules), and some others which you can discover for yourself. Variety is not an issue.
I subscribe to the belief that this game got worse since it went F2P. Cheer or boo that notion all you want, but in my experience, the community is nowhere near what it used to be. Thanks to the F2P model, that obviously means anyone can play, which contributed to the influx of players that make me want to set myself on fire, and jump out a window. Granted, good F2P players exist, but my ♥♥♥♥ing god, the level of human garbage you can encounter is staggering. I'm not even talking about their skill level, but their personalities alone. Do you like completely unfunny text binds of memes being spammed? Yes? Welcome home. No? Prepare your sanity, or completely turn off the chat via the console. (Google it.) Go ahead and just mute every player when you enter a game, as well. These often occur in official Valve servers, but community ones can suffer the same. There are also good people, but you may have to sift through the dirt, first. Just be ready.
The game itself, if you don't mind the sheer chaos, can be a fun time. There are no iron-sights, grenades (sans the Demoman's grenade launcher), or ranks. So, if you're tired of online games that favor players who play more, give this one a try. Yeah, they'll still have more weapons than you, but none of them came at a certain time, and you can get them at any time. Also, remember, stock weapons are (mostly) king. Oh, you can craft weapons, too. Though that may also take time to get the one you want.
Like I said, my view on this game is pretty much 50/50. There are aspects that I enjoy, and others I loathe. Sometimes I have to take long breaks. Sometimes it's all I play in a day. It's weird. It's a ♥♥♥♥ing weird game.

I'm assuming most people reading this have some inkling on what TF2 is, so I'll just cut to the knitty-gritty.
Pros:
* Basically free, and if you pay five bucks you can get access to just about all of the weapon content. Valve has handled the F2P model pretty well.
* LOTS of content, especially weapons; the game is rebalanced every so often so there's a lot of gameplay diversity.
* Both competitive and casual scene, plus a large community. Don't know how the game's doing community server-wise anymore, but I'm sure you can still find a pretty good number of modded servers, custom maps and the like.
* The classes are their core are all great. TF2 is basically an expansive MMO built off of really good core gameplay. With the amount of unlocks this game has to offer, you're sure to find a playstyle that clicks.
Cons
* Pretty bloated now. Lot of distracting cosmetics and "crates" (dlc ads basically), plus the file size is bigger than it has any right to be.
* Doesn't run well on low-end computers. Seriously, it was released in 2007 and it's optimized like garbage. And here I can run Killing Floor 2 on my toaster.
*
slowly dying. There's still activity for sure, but the game's not going to last forever. The new updates are usually pretty hit or miss.
Recommended if you're looking to get into the FPS genre or just want some teamplay action, but only if you have some pretty good specs. And of course it's virtually free, so no harm in trying it. But if you've already played this game before and are wondering if you absolutely need to redownload it... you're not missing that much. You'll probably replay it for a couple weeks and forget about it. YMMV.

* Doesn't run well on low-end computers. Seriously, it was released in 2007 and it's optimized like garbage. And here I can run Killing Floor 2 on my toaster.
*
slowly dying. There's still activity for sure, but the game's not going to last forever. The new updates are usually pretty hit or miss.
Recommended if you're looking to get into the FPS genre or just want some teamplay action, but only if you have some pretty good specs. And of course it's virtually free, so no harm in trying it. But if you've already played this game before and are wondering if you absolutely need to redownload it... you're not missing that much. You'll probably replay it for a couple weeks and forget about it. YMMV.

A game with a play for nearly everyone- thanks to its variety of classes, anti-frustration features (no grenades) and cartoonish atmosphere it is easy to get into, but has hidden depths, it takes a while to get boring and new play-styles are always evolving. Unfortunately due to the lack of any kind of matchmaking, you can easily end up in lobbies where you and your team will be steam-rolled by much more skilled players.
For all its positives, it does have some issues. Some classes with 'complicated' mechanics(i.e more than just shooting)- like engineer, spy and medic need specific tutorials that the game does not provide- you have to learn either through trial and error, watching more experienced players or finding tutorials on-line. In addition, certain classes like soldier, demo, pyro have 'hidden' abilities- rocket-jumping, sticky-jumping/trimping, reflecting that are not immediately apparent and are essential for a specific class to really shine- depending on your perspective you can view this as a feature or an oversight.
On its surface, team fortress 2 may not seem as 'hard-core' as games like CS, Quake and others, but don't let that fool you- this game has hidden depth and rewards a variety of players and play styles, not just the careful aiming of CS or the twitch reaction of Quake, but also for strategic placement of sentries, healing mechanics and more. So long as Valve does not screw it up royally, it will continue to be an excellent.

With the "Jungle Inferno" update launching today (as I write this review), I thought it's high time to write a real review for this game. Before I get into it though, let me say that i've had this game on multiple accounts since ~2012-2013, and though I only have 300 hours or so on this account, i'd estimate I have at least 1200-1500 possibly even 2000 hours total. Long story short, i've switched accounts a couple times for a bunch of different reasons and probably have more around 1500 hours than 300.
The game is extremely unique. Although other class based shooters exist and have existed since Team Fortress, Valve originally perfected the idea with Team Fortress 2. The way the classes all have the perfect balance of jobs and skills that make them all a completely unique experience to the other is amazing.
The unlockable weapons in this game are at times both a blessing and curse. The unlockable weapons help in reinforcing my previous point, with such weapons as the Crusader's Crossbow, Ambassador, Force of Nature and many more for every single class.
Though crate drops are unfuriating, if you're one for gambling, arguably crates and unboxing can be a great system. It works to regulate the in-game economy (yes, the game has an economy and trading system!) and you get the chance at a rare "Unusual" hat, which is worth a ton of in-game and sometimes real-life currency.
Going back onto that very crate system, though unusuals are expensive and great to have, they are way rarer then they have any business being, and the amount of keys you'd have to use to open the crates to even get one is to the point where you'd probably be able to just buy one with that very same amount of keys. I believe it's 1% every 100 crates or so, which is a huge money trap for unaware customers.
The game is made on Source engine, and that's usually a pretty great engine for physics if made well, but the engine is well over ten years old now, and the spaghetti coding is real within the engine. Many glitches can and will be exploited to players advantage, and most of them are unfixable due to Source itself. Though the game being ugly or not is up for debate, the art style could certainly be overhauled to make the game look much better, if this infamous rumoured "Source 2" ever comes out.
The game is rarely updated at all. Major updates take at least a year and a half or so to come out, and though this isn't neccessarily the fault of the TF team (they only have a very small active staff), I feel Valve should really get their♥♥♥♥♥♥together and realize this game still has a huge community, and can and will grow bigger if the game is actively supported. I'm just glad Jungle Inferno is coming out.
I am not a prominent player nor am I a prominent youtuber/streamer, but I do sometimes make youtube videos, and recently I made a YouTube video explaining the fatal flaws of TF2. Jungle Inferno has fixed some of these, but many still stand. Problems that I have mentioned, and problems that I have not, such as the tutorial system.
Speaking of the "tutorial" system, it's incredibly basic and simplified to the point where it's not even useful. The only way a player is going to learn the game is to hop into a casual match and probably get destroyed by better players. The tutorial system has VERY basic tutorials for 4 different classes, and half the time is broken and unaccessable, you just have to get lucky to even have it be usable.
Either way, that's just a "quick" analysis on what I think about the current state of TF2. Though in my mind i'm very conflicted about if I should recommend it or not, I went with no because of it's unfriendliness to new players. I'm sorry Valve.
