Team Fortress 2 is a FPS game, developed by Valve, releasing in October 2007 on Steam, Xbox 360 and PC. You are probably going to see this review and think “Why are you reviewing TF2, everyone knows what it is about!” You will be right; however there is a small portion of people who have not ventured into TF2’s world, so this will be for you!
Gameplay for Team Fortress 2 is based around various different game modes, which you take part in online servers.  You join a team and choose one of nine different classes to play as. Some of the game modes include the classic capture the flag, control points, king of the hill, and payload – which requires you to move a cart across the map with a bomb attached to it, into the enemies base. The 9 different classes all feel very different to each other, but ultimately will fit into one of three roles; offense, defence and support. Offensive characters are the ones built for dealing large sums of damage to your foes. The defensive ones, whilst these also deal damage, are much more equipped for doing this from entrenched positions, and the support roles add different features to the team with healing or other special abilities which act as a benefit for your team, or a hindrance to the opponents.  The classes are all really simple to learn how to use, but can be pretty tricky in mastering the art of the class.
My favourite game mode in Team Fortress 2 would have to be Mann vs Machine. This is a six player co-op mode, where you have to defend your base from waves of AI controlled enemies. In between waves you are able to purchase upgrades for your character to use for the rest of the match. This game mode also offers a “Mann up” mode, which requires you to purchase a ticket, in order to take part in events on official servers, to be in for a chance to win cosmetic items after you finish the mode. Even if you stick to the free side of this mode, you will have a boat load of fun if you can find a team of players and get on voice chat together.
Graphically, since the game is running the Source engine, it looks gorgeous. The cartoony style of art on show gives the game a unique charm and feels which cannot be mimicked by any other game to date. Sound effects and sound tracks are all on point too.
TF2 has a training mode that will ease newer players into the game; this is especially handy for people who are particularly new to the FPS genre as well. This is a game which definitely gets better the better you are at it; and getting better at it only comes with practice. If you find a class you are interested in, and stick with it, you’ll soon get to a point where you are coming top of the scoreboard at the end of the game. Of course it helps to have a little experience with all of the classes because diversity is key in these multiplayer type games, but having a main is also a good idea too.
My play time on TF2 is dwarfed by many, I have only been playing for about seventeen hours so far, and I have only really started playing it properly in the last few weeks, having dropped in and out of it a few times in recent years. Mann vs Machine has really got me hooked on the game again. If you are a FPS junky, this is about as good as it gets for the genre and you will be able to get hundreds of hours of game play out of it before it even becomes tedious. Some people have thousands of hours in this game and I cannot blame them. On top of the huge replay ability factor, TF2 also has over 500 achievements, which should keep even the keenest of achievement hunters busy for a sufficient amount of time.
This game is so perfectly put together from a technical stand point; I have had no bugs, no crashes, and the graphics are perfectly optimized that even when playing on a 4k resolution with all of the settings ramped up to max, I still had a 200 frame rate.
To sum up, Team Fortress 2 is the perfect model of a free to play game done absolutely right. As you may have been able to notice, I have not once mentioned the market and microtransactions part of this game in my review, and this is because I found no reason to ever need to put my hand into my wallet to buy anything. Real hard-core fans will be itching to purchase a few cosmetic items, but if you are looking for a casual first person shooter experience, Team Fortress 2 will tick all of the boxes, and it comes out on top of most, if not all of the recent shooters out there to date. If you are one of the handful amounts of people who have not played TF2 for any substantial amount of time, I seriously urge you to give this game an evening of your time, and let it suck you in to its highly addictive nature.

Considering this is a Free To Play Game, I would reccommend you installing this. It's a friendly community full of great people, but like every other game, you do run into the odd person who ruins it for everyone. I have Pro's and Cons:                         Pro's:
It's a first person shooter. What's not to like?
Great community, mostly friendly
You have coaches that volounteer to help you. Just click 'Call Coach' and a random experienced Team Fortress 2 Player will spectate you, and guide you thoroughly until you 'Dismiss the Coach' or 'Leave the Game' This is reccommended for newer players
Many severs. There are plenty servers: Trading Servers, Jailbreak servers, Five nights at Freddy's servers, Deathrun servers or just servers you play normally (shooting people until you win)                                                                                           Many ways to Play. This is the beauty of Team fortress 2 (TF2 for short). There are soo many ways to enjoy theese hours of gaming! The sniper, The scout, The medic, The soldier, The engineer, The Pyro, The heavy, The spy and the Demoman. I wont tell you their abilities! Thats for you to find out! It's clear from some of the names though...                               The friends! You make SOOO many friends on this 1 game! From now, I've made 22 friends on it. They help you, they stick up for you, they cherish you.
Groups. The community have made groups! You can get free items from theese giveaway or raffle groups. You also get the friendly chatty groups! The newbie Groups! The experienced groups! There are soo many! Free things are always the best!
Now for the worst part......
The cons:
The rare hacker. Ok, sure most of the servers are VAC banned, but this dosen't stop smart, expert hackers. This includes: Aimbot,♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Sandvichbox ect. Theese are very VERY rare, but keep an eye out! Most new players use theese, but nobody wants to play with a cheater!
The odd bully. Ok, the TF2 community is fair and dandy, but on every server, there's that one guy who spoils it for everyone. Using insults, threats (possibly death threats that I've came across) and blackmail. Some of theese people cyberbully, so lets stick up and make them vanish!
The rule breaker. On every other server, you get somebody who breaks the rules. If this means Bullying, Threatening,  Teasing, Hacking or Blackmailing ect, it gets really annoying! Some people need to stop spoiling the game!
The show off. There's sometimes a cocky fella who thinks he's better, calling new players F2P (Free 2 play) There is nothing wrong with this, exept horrid people will tease and moan that there are new players on the server, telling them to 'Get lost' or 'I hate F2P's with their gibuse's ( a free cosmetic you recieve with achivements).
The squeaker. Theese are on some servers. Squeakers have high - pitched voices and grumble, moan, scream or sing. They are aged between 6 - 8. If you are in that age, it is reccomended you stay off your microphone and use chat. You shouldn't be playing this game, but you could attract older men or women to your profile, thus Telling them where you live, Telling them your name, Telling them your age and other personal information. Young boys and girls have been brutally murdered by doing this, so if you're in that age period, STAY OFF YOUR MICROPHONE! Just use text chat! Don't tell them your personal information, whatever you do! Keep it private, unless you have supervision and permission by an older adult
Over all, this is the best game I've had so far! Nevermind the cons, stick to the pros! I love this game so much I have my own group, and you should start yours too! I would rate it 10/10. Keep up the good work Valve! And people reading, Stay Safe and have Fun!! -Darcie

It's had bumps in the road like any other game, but it's by far the most fun FPS game I've ever played, and I've never come back to any other game so many times like this one. Even in today's gaming this is, in my opinion, one of the best FPS games there is, if not, best free to play FPS hands down.
I'm going to go with a new format where I expose 2 pain points and 2 redeeming qualities, then write a quick summary, so here we go.
One of the major pain points I have is sometimes balance gets tossed to the side. When a new weapon gets added to the game, it's not uncommon for it to be massively be OP and dominate everything it comes across. Valve is usually pretty quick to fix these problems if they're severe, but it's still a problem none the less. Although this gripe is more nitpicky than anything else, considering new weapons don't release all that often, and even then it's rare for them to be extremely OP.
The second pain point I have with TF2 revolves around glitches and the community. Sure, things like getting outside of the map are fun to do, and I'm not saying anything against those, it's the glitches where you're able to, I don't know, freeze up the door to respawn so your team can't get out. Whenever the community sees one of these glitches, they use it over and over again under the guise of "If more people use it, Valve will have to patch it!" Alright, or you can let them get to it when they can and not ruin the gameplay of others. A glitch you have to go out of your way to abuse shouldn't have to become #1 priority to things like performance fixes and weapon balance. Know when to draw the line people.
Alright, so, redeeming qualities. Many of them, going to be hard to pick my top two.
I'd say the first one goes to the community. I know I just spent the second point harping on the community, but in reality it is great. Most people are willing to help new player (That I've seen) and understand that you may not understand everything there is to know about TF2. There are so many ways to play TF2 and so many wacky things going on, that it's easy for a new player to get overwhelmed by everything going on, and it's nice to see the community realize this.
The second major redeeming quality is how many ways this game can be played. Honestly I've never seen a game pull it off quite as well as TF2. You have massive amount of diversity in play styles without killing the game or having one play style dominate all. Sure, there are a couple which are just plain dumb to use, but that's unavoidable, and they're easy to spot. This introduces a variability to the game you don't really see often. Players can surprise other players in other ways than how they jump. This gets especially fun when you play the randomizer mod.
Summary: TF2 is the greatest FPS game I've had the pleasure of playing. Sure, it has problems, but what game doesn't? It has survived as long as it has for a reason. This game is immense amounts of fun I'd recommend to anyone looking for an FPS game to waste your time on. You could even play competetive if you want. Valve is implementing a matchmaking system, and there's already a community driven competetive scene that's been around for years just waiting for new blood. Even if you're not the best, so what? This game doesn't cater to the best, it caters to those who wants to have fun.

Considering this is a Free To Play Game, I would reccommend you installing this. It's a friendly community full of great people, but like every other game, you do run into the odd person who ruins it for everyone. I have Pro's and Cons:                         Pro's:
It's a first person shooter. What's not to like?
Great community, mostly friendly
You have coaches that volounteer to help you. Just click 'Call Coach' and a random experienced Team Fortress 2 Player will spectate you, and guide you thoroughly until you 'Dismiss the Coach' or 'Leave the Game' This is reccommended for newer players
Many severs. There are plenty servers: Trading Servers, Jailbreak servers, Five nights at Freddy's servers, Deathrun servers or just servers you play normally (shooting people until you win)                                                                                           Many ways to Play. This is the beauty of Team fortress 2 (TF2 for short). There are soo many ways to enjoy theese hours of gaming! The sniper, The scout, The medic, The soldier, The engineer, The Pyro, The heavy, The spy and the Demoman. I wont tell you their abilities! Thats for you to find out! It's clear from some of the names though...                               The friends! You make SOOO many friends on this 1 game! From now, I've made 22 friends on it. They help you, they stick up for you, they cherish you.
Groups. The community have made groups! You can get free items from theese giveaway or raffle groups. You also get the friendly chatty groups! The newbie Groups! The experienced groups! There are soo many! Free things are always the best!
Now for the worst part......
The cons:
The rare hacker. Ok, sure most of the servers are VAC banned, but this dosen't stop smart, expert hackers. This includes: Aimbot,♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Sandvichbox ect. Theese are very VERY rare, but keep an eye out! Most new players use theese, but nobody wants to play with a cheater!
The odd bully. Ok, the TF2 community is fair and dandy, but on every server, there's that one guy who spoils it for everyone. Using insults, threats (possibly death threats that I've came across) and blackmail. Some of theese people cyberbully, so lets stick up and make them vanish!
The rule breaker. On every other server, you get somebody who breaks the rules. If this means Bullying, Threatening,  Teasing, Hacking or Blackmailing ect, it gets really annoying! Some people need to stop spoiling the game!
The show off. There's sometimes a cocky fella who thinks he's better, calling new players F2P (Free 2 play) There is nothing wrong with this, exept horrid people will tease and moan that there are new players on the server, telling them to 'Get lost' or 'I hate F2P's with their gibuse's ( a free cosmetic you recieve with achivements).
The squeaker. Theese are on some servers. Squeakers have high - pitched voices and grumble, moan, scream or sing. They are aged between 6 - 8. If you are in that age, it is reccomended you stay off your microphone and use chat. You shouldn't be playing this game, but you could attract older men or women to your profile, thus Telling them where you live, Telling them your name, Telling them your age and other personal information. Young boys and girls have been brutally murdered by doing this, so if you're in that age period, STAY OFF YOUR MICROPHONE! Just use text chat! Don't tell them your personal information, whatever you do! Keep it private, unless you have supervision and permission by an older adult
Over all, this is the best game I've had so far! Nevermind the cons, stick to the pros! I love this game so much I have my own group, and you should start yours too! I would rate it 10/10. Keep up the good work Valve! And people reading, Stay Safe and have Fun!! -Darcie

Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

Team Fortress 2 is a cartoony MMOFPS with a super-dose of character, and more pop references than you can handle in one sitting. Players play one of 9 mercenary classes working for one of two corporations (RED and BLU) duking it out tooth-and-nails over a variety of objectives ranging from briefcases, to giant bombs in mine carts. With a tons of weapons, achievements, hats and maps, this game has incredible longevity, and will keep you latched to your screen hoping for that one achievement, or that specific weapon(Golden Pan for me) you’re looking to get.
Classes:
Spy(My Fav): Proficient knife fighter and mother lover, the spy can feign death/cloak and disguise himself into the enemy team.
Demoman: Trap-setting, one-eyed Scottish demoman with a knack for blowing things to pieces. Is surprisingly good with a claymore.
Engineer: Texan cowboy with a knack for turret building. Incredibly efficient at point defense, you’ll grow to love or hate his turrets.
Heavy: Chain gun wielding boxer, the medic’s best friend. With a massive health pool, this is both the damage soaking, and damage dealing class.
Medic: Mad doctor wielding a surgery saw to battle. Specializes in deploying ubercharges on teammates, making them invincible for a short time.
Pyro: Axe-wielding pyromaniac specialized in ambushes, and generally setting living things on fire.
Scout: Super-fast class that uses its speed to outmatch opponents and quickly capture points.
Sniper: Long-range shooter with a knack for throwing jars of suspicious yellow liquids.
Soldier: Frontline tough guy with a rocket launcher, and a lot of punch.

This game is extremely fun for me. Theres plenty of gamemodes, weapons, hats and more to choose from! My main favorite gamemodes are the Stop That Tank! gamemode and the Zombie Fortress/Super Zombie Fortress gamemodes. Stop That Tank has you playing as either the Robots or Humans. If you are robots, you either have to defend the tank, or if its destroyed, defend the robot who is bringing the bomb to the end. It is played on regular TF2 Payload or Payload Race maps instead of Mann VS Machine maps. Zombie fortress is played as either Survivors or Zombies. Zombies are blu and have perks to stop the Survivors from camping and force them to move out. Survivors are red and have to get a good defense up to survive. Zombies only have melee weapons, survivors have guns along with their melee. On some servers, you have perks. On others, you have to pick up weapons to fight with them. There are some problems with hacking, glitches and mean players, but otherwise, this game is great! I would suggest this game to anyone who likes to have fun or play hard. (My First Game Review! Not too sure what to write here so heres a recipe for Pancakes instead
Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. Cook, until bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, and the undersides are golden brown, about 2 minutes. Flip with a spatula and cook about 1 minute more on the second side. Serve immediately or transfer to a platter and cover loosely with foil to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more butter to the skillet as needed.
6. Procedure for adding fruit to pancakes: Once the bubbles break the surface of the pancakes, scatter the surface with sliced or diced fruit, or chocolate chips, nuts, etc. Flip with a spatula and cook for 1 minute more, being careful not to burn toppings.

Let me say this, this game is amazing. When i was first introduced to Pc Gaming, I didnt have any money, so i went looking for some F2p games on steam, and found this. Before i chose to get it i watched some youtube videos on it, i think my first one was by muselk, and I loved watching his videos. So of course i installed the game around the same time the gun mettle update came out. I load up, "Oh look a badge." It was a mercenary badge, i though "Meh why not" and put it in a cosmetic slot, now this was before i understood the concept of hats, so i thought "Ok then this looks cool" and continued to a payload server. My first "Main" i guess you could say was scout, so i played a bit as him and got some kills, thought "Hey this is pretty fun." So i went to a King of the hill server, and unlocked the one and only "Ghostly Gibus", once again thought "Pretty cool ill take it" and also got the pyrovision googles. After a while i was introduced to a festive weapon that i picked up. At this point i was called a F2p many times and got the concept of it so i though, "This is really cool, i want this." I went P2P and got me a Festivizer and a Factory New Night Owl Sniper Rifle. Combined the two, got into trading, and so forth. I started getting top of the leaderboard more, and started meeting cool people. I started getting more stuff, participated in the Pass time and Comp Beta, and started helping the community more. I started watching more Sfms and made some posters (Which i still do) and now I help with the wiki.

This game was fun! I have had some good times with my friends in this game. But I do not recommend this game for several reasons.
1. I always somehow got in fights with my friends while playing this.
We had fun times, but we also got in arguments - some of which having nothing to do with this game. On one day, you would be playing some classic 2fort and having a good time - the next day, your friend would be mad at you because you got your first unusual and he didn't.
2. This game will EAT your money. I first got this game expecting to play a cartoony FPS with some purchasable content like guns and hats, but who would waste money on hats? After some time, I decided to spend some money and get guns. In my mind, guns were important and hats were a waste. I thought that I would never want to buy a hat in my entire TF2 experience. Some time after that, I realized that everybody except for me had hats (gibus-related hats excluded), so I decided to buy one to make my Scout look nicer. At that point, I had probably only spent about $10.00 on this game. But once you start, you CAN'T stop. After my first hat, I just kept buying hats, crates, and keys - and before I realized it, I had quickly spent $100.00+ on this game, a F2P game. I had wasted a lot of money getting hats, weapons, and better hats. It consumed me until I eventually got bored of the gameplay and decided that it would be best if I stopped the spending madness and spent my money on new games. And so about 6 months ago, I quit.
After my experience, I can strongly recommend you NOT to get this game - and I know that CS:GO has a similar effect on your steam wallet - trust me, you do not want to find out for yourself how this game changes your steam wallet.

Szar játék.......de mindenki pont ezért a tulajdonsága miatt szereti szóval miért ne vegyen rá fel személyi kölcsönt az ember. 3 év tapasztalat és már 3500 óra játék idő után, (700 óra utáni stat reset miatt csak 2800) azt mondhatja az ember, hogy kurva jól játszik, egy kezdőhöz képest valóban negyed annyiszor döglik csak meg a harctéren, nem is tudom már hogy a játékba hány liter vérem folyt el mire profi lettem benne. Két dolgot sajnáltam a játékba, de azt nagyon, az egyik a rengeteg bug a játékba ami felbaszta az agyam párszor, a másik pedig a piactéren történő kupleráj ami miatt egyes holmik megvásárolhatatlanná váltak, a kulcs értéke pedig az egekbe szállt, indokolatlan tempóba. Tulajdonképpen minden évben más koncepcióval volt a baj, a lényeg hogy mindig szart valamit a kutya, ami nem hagyott nyugodni.
A játékosok 3 irányba fejlődhetnek:
- A vérprofi rutinos játékosok akik mindenkit hazabasznak komolyabb probléma nélkül és komoly meccsekre mennek, élsportot csinálva a játékból, a vereséget el nem fogadva teljesítmény mérővel a játékba megszerzett képesítéseket fejleszteni non-stop
- A cserélgetős játékosok, akik leszarják mi történik velük a játékba, inkább minél több pénzt ölnek bele és az ilyenek meg is szereznek minimum 1 Unusual holmit, ha nem többet és azon vannak, hogy a karaktereik minél jobban nézzenek ki és legyenek kinyalva minden egyes szegletből, mindegy mennyire nem tudnak játszani
- A pub játékosok, akiknek teljesen mindegy az előző két említett felállás, ahogy esik, úgy puffan kategória, leginkább F2P játékosok tömeggyülekezete, akik feljárnak játszani a mindennapokba és szívják a faszt, ha egy jobb játékos kerül az adott szerverre és kiveri belőlük a szart, leginkább deathmatch-en tolják naphosszat, a többi játékmódot nem is ismerve
Mind a háromba volt részem egy bizonyos szintig és ez már bővebb okot adott nekem arra, hogy végleg be is fejezzem, egyébként jó játék tud lenni nagyon, ha értelmes emberekkel játszol, egy jól kidolgozott pályán, vagy jól kidolgozott stratégiával, vagy szépen felöltöztetett piperkőc karaktereiddel, (amiért anyádat is eladtad jó pénzért) vagy éppen a legharsányabb szókincsű trashtalker haverjaiddal egy legelbaszottabb játékmódba. Válassz egy neked tettsző opciót, csak aztán legyél is elégedett......Gayben ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)
Szóval egy szó mint száz, a játékot ezer irányból tudnám fikázni vég nélkül, de mivel ez a játék mindenkinek tetszik és még nekem is időnként hogy baszná meg.....xD...khm...a jóban pont ez a rossz, de itt mindenki szereti azt csinálni amit utál, ezekkel együtt ajánlom a játékot mindenkinek hogy próbálja ki, sajnos a kipróbálásból garantált a függőség, mert ahhoz a játék túl élvezetes, hogy rossznak lehessen mondani, de túl szemét is ahhoz, hogy kellően a legélvezetesebbnek lehessen mondani, szal tegyétek ahova akarjátok. Én a kopaszok közé fogom...:)

"Variety is the spice of life."
That would mean that TF2 is incredibly spicy.
And sense it is spicy, many players will try it, find it is too much for them, and never return.
But then, after hearing the praise of the dish from their friends and the internet, they will try it again.
Perhaps they will enjoy it more this time.
And if they do, they will want to taste its spicy goodness again. So they eat more.
Then they discover they can season it with spices themselves. This allows them to customize their dish, into something uniquely their own.
And as they eat more and more of this culinary masterpiece, their table manners become better, and their eating is less sloppy.
Eventually, they develop an addiction. They love this dish too much, and can't stop eating it, every day, all day.
Then something goes wrong.
Perhaps it interfered with their social life, or they slipped up and spilled the food everywhere. The French waiter says, "Dominated, you fatuous, fat-headed fat man!"
They stop eating the dish for a while. They set their life back on track, and perhaps start eating dishes that are... less spicy, more common, and provide some satisfaction while still being fairly healthy.
Their life continues.
But as they settle back into their monotone life, with the same dishes just being pumped out to them, year after year, they think, "Well, maybe one dish of that spicy goodness would be nice. Just for a little variety."
They eat the dish again. They find that it is now almost completely different, while still spicy and enjoyable.
They decide to spend a bit of extra cash on extra things the diner offers. Maybe a couple of sides, a bit more seasoning, even some famous culinary dresswear.
They find that they are now better at eating this meal than most, and their spirits skyrocket.
They continue eating.
One day, one of their friends decides to try the meal. Finding it too spicy for his taste, he shoves it away in disgust and confusion.
A few months later, he is convinced by his cultured friend to try it again.
Perhaps he will enjoy it more this time.

I feel as if I should re-write me review for this game, as when I did several years ago I was young and it never really achieved much.
Now as someone who has spent almost 3000 hours of playing this game, I can easily recommend it to anyone who is fresh to steam, or first person games in general. This game provides a helpful tutorial to anyone who isn't ignorant (which I assume the readers are not as they are reading this review, doing research and are eager to learn), teaching basic concepts and how to play more of the unique classes such as the spy and engineer. There is even a training mode to play against AI if you feel that playing against real people is too challenging to begin with. Team Fortress 2 is definitely a game you should get if you are new to steam or PC gaming in general.
TF2 is very different, very diverse compared to other FPS titles. You play as one of nine classes, all with varying roles and weaponry, all with their own strengths and weaknesses. With easily over 100 different weapons in the game, there are many different things to try out. This list keeps growing with the variety of maps and gamemodes to choose from, such as Capture the Flag (a staple in many FPS games), Payload, Mann vs Machine and PASS time. The game also gets somewhat frequent updates, both community made and official, always adding new content and therefore more fun, all without paying a cent.
Microtransactions exist in this game, however not in a pay-to-win function. They solely exist as a cosmetic function, allowing players to add hats, beards, almost any sort of visual appearance to the mercenaries they play as. Now, as this is only decorational, free-to-play players (or F2Ps for short) don't miss out on anything if they choose to not buy these things, however the option is there if they want to spend money on something they enjoy.
The community is definitely one of the biggest things in this game, having kept it alive for 9 years as of later this year. There will be good encounters and bad encounters like everything, however, finding your place will ensure you a great time. Unfortunately, many of the pay-to play players (P2Ps for short) frown upon F2Ps, judging them as "unskilled and foolish" among other things of the sorts, however there are also many people who are willing to help out newcomers assuming the newby is willing to listen.
Without going into too much more detail, this game should definitely be on everyone's to-play list if they haven't done so already, although just prepare yourself for a very unique experience and many great times ahead.

As for the individual game types, the class training isn't all that useful - they should make it more advanced, and for all classes, not just half of them. It's not worth your time, unless you want the associated achievement.
Training with bots, on the other hand, is FUN. There is always room for improvements, such as adding more gamemodes and maps, and improving the AI of the bots (like Medics who stand under enemy fire, Engineers who never upgrade their Teleporters, Soldiers and Demos who hardly ever use melee), but all in all, there's nothing more cash than winning Dustbowl on defence with a shutout. However, if your PC is below average (like mine), your FPS are going to tank from time to time. Regardless, I would recommend this mode for beginners and/or players who have had enough of the CONGA lines.
Next up is the Multiplayer, with all of the classic, "nicer" maps. I will dive into the individual game modes later, but let's just say that if you prefer hacker-less experience, but with noobier players, you're in the right place.
I haven't played that much of Mann vs. Machine, but if you like co-operative survival, you're going to feel right at home, driving hordes of automatons away.
The community servers are definitely more straight-forward with simpler maps, but there's a fair share of players who feel the need to use programs to lay their headshots for them. The reward is that most players here are quite experienced.
As for the individual gamemodes, I enjoy Payload and Capture the Flag the most when playing multiplayer. You might find other gamemodes more appealing, but these generally have full servers and they're good fun. Them respawn times, tho.
I haven't played all the maps, but I recommend Dustbowl for Control Points, Turbine, 2Fort, and Double Cross for Capture the Flag, and Badwater Basin and Borneo for Payload.
The classes are mostly balanced, but the Scout's scatterguns are a bit on the overpowered side, and the Demo's Eyelander could be a bit stronger.
The Scout is ideal for fast offence, harassing the enemy lines, picking off Snipers and Medics, as well as playing the objective with the 200% rate of capture bonus. Don't use him in static defense, he's a feast for crows that way with his low health.
The Soldier is a sturdier class, good for both middle-to-long range offence and defence with a higher health, but slower movement speed. He can provide buffs for his team, and he deals a fair amount of damage. Up close and personal, though, he's not as useful (but smacking fools with a shovel is entertaining). And there's also the rocket jumps, which can massacre classes moving through open ground if used properly.
The Pyro is great for beginners, but a skilled Pyro can rip up the entire enemy team. He deals an awful lot of damage up close, but isn't very effective over long distances, save for his Flare Guns, which are good against Snipers. He's good at ambushes and punishing retreating enemies, which makes him one the most flexible classes.
The Demo is no picnic for new players. The Grenade Launcher (especially the Loch'n'Load) requires a fair bit of expertise to use efficiently, but a good Demo can turn an okay team into a threshing machine. The Sticky Bombs allow for pathway blocking, hasty escapes, unexpected behind-the-lines attacks and even suicide bombings. The shields trade defense for offence, best used with long-range weapons. Demos are also one of the most flexible classes.
The Heavy, as the name implies, is the toughest, but also the slowest class. Good for anything requiring a lot of bullets, but not very good at fast offence. The Sandvich is great for when no one wants to play Medic (98% of the time).
The Engineer is for patient players. A well-placed Sentry Gun can not only rack up kills, but also halt enemy attacks or defend control points. A Dispenser can be the difference between life and death, and Teleporters are helpful when you want to get to strategic locations. As a battle class, however, he mostly sucks.
The Medic is a masochist. No one helps him, but they all expect help from him. He's awful at combat, but he shines when his team is worn out after attacking a Sentry nest or a strong group of enemies. A lot of Medics are pansies who won't run headlong into the fire with a Pyro, Soldier, or a Demo, though. They just want Heavy's magnificient Minigun to do all the fighting for them.
The Sniper is a favorite, for reasons that should be obvious. He's poor at offence (this is about the player's attitude, though), he's best at picking off Engineers, Medics, and other Snipers. And unless you're UBERcharged, there's always a chance your head will be blown off by one of these guys.
Last, but not least, the Spy is used for taking out the Engineer's buildings, tricking the enemy team and luring them into traps,  backstabbing Snipers who get too comfortable, sneaking around and generally being up to no good. At combat, they suck (unless h4xx are used).
Well, that was exhausting. I give it a solid rating of 8/10 because of the aforementioned imperfections.

Ingredients:
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tablespoons sugar
1 tablespoon baking powder
1/4 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon freshly ground nutmeg
2 large eggs, at room temperature
1 1/4 cups milk, at room temperature
1/2 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more as needed
Now to make it
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg.
2. In another bowl, beat the eggs and then whisk in the milk and vanilla.
3. Melt the butter in a large cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat.
4. Whisk the butter into the milk mixture. Add the wet ingredients to the flour mixture, and whisk until a thick batter is just formed
5. Keeping the skillet at medium heat, ladle about 1/4 cup of the batter onto the skillet, to make a pancake. Make 1 or 2 more pancakes, taking care to keep them evenly spaced apart. "Variety is the spice of life."
That would mean that TF2 is incredibly spicy.
And sense it is spicy, many players will try it, find it is too much for them, and never return.
But then, after hearing the praise of the dish from their friends and the internet, they will try it again.
Perhaps they will enjoy it more this time.
And if they do, they will want to taste its spicy goodness again. So they eat more.
Then they discover they can season it with spices themselves. This allows them to customize their dish, into something uniquely their own.
And as they eat more and more of this culinary masterpiece, their table manners become better, and their eating is less sloppy.
Eventually, they develop an addiction. They love this dish too much, and can't stop eating it, every day, all day.
Then something goes wrong.
Perhaps it interfered with their social life, or they slipped up and spilled the food everywhere. The French waiter says, "Dominated, you fatuous, fat-headed fat man!"
They stop eating the dish for a while. They set their life back on track, and perhaps start eating dishes that are... less spicy, more common, and provide some satisfaction while still being fairly healthy.
Their life continues.
But as they settle back into their monotone life, with the same dishes just being pumped out to them, year after year, they think, "Well, maybe one dish of that spicy goodness would be nice. Just for a little variety."
They eat the dish again. They find that it is now almost completely different, while still spicy and enjoyable.
They decide to spend a bit of extra cash on extra things the diner offers. Maybe a couple of sides, a bit more seasoning, even some famous culinary dresswear.
They find that they are now better at eating this meal than most, and their spirits skyrocket.
They continue eating.
One day, one of their friends decides to try the meal. Finding it too spicy for his taste, he shoves it away in disgust and confusion.
A few months later, he is convinced by his cultured friend to try it again.
Perhaps he will enjoy it more this time.

I feel as if I should re-write me review for this game, as when I did several years ago I was young and it never really achieved much.
Now as someone who has spent almost 3000 hours of playing this game, I can easily recommend it to anyone who is fresh to steam, or first person games in general. This game provides a helpful tutorial to anyone who isn't ignorant (which I assume the readers are not as they are reading this review, doing research and are eager to learn), teaching basic concepts and how to play more of the unique classes such as the spy and engineer. There is even a training mode to play against AI if you feel that playing against real people is too challenging to begin with. Team Fortress 2 is definitely a game you should get if you are new to steam or PC gaming in general.
TF2 is very different, very diverse compared to other FPS titles. You play as one of nine classes, all with varying roles and weaponry, all with their own strengths and weaknesses. With easily over 100 different weapons in the game, there are many different things to try out. This list keeps growing with the variety of maps and gamemodes to choose from, such as Capture the Flag (a staple in many FPS games), Payload, Mann vs Machine and PASS time. The game also gets somewhat frequent updates, both community made and official, always adding new content and therefore more fun, all without paying a cent.
Microtransactions exist in this game, however not in a pay-to-win function. They solely exist as a cosmetic function, allowing players to add hats, beards, almost any sort of visual appearance to the mercenaries they play as. Now, as this is only decorational, free-to-play players (or F2Ps for short) don't miss out on anything if they choose to not buy these things, however the option is there if they want to spend money on something they enjoy.
The community is definitely one of the biggest things in this game, having kept it alive for 9 years as of later this year. There will be good encounters and bad encounters like everything, however, finding your place will ensure you a great time. Unfortunately, many of the pay-to play players (P2Ps for short) frown upon F2Ps, judging them as "unskilled and foolish" among other things of the sorts, however there are also many people who are willing to help out newcomers assuming the newby is willing to listen.
Without going into too much more detail, this game should definitely be on everyone's to-play list if they haven't done so already, although just prepare yourself for a very unique experience and many great times ahead.

"Variety is the spice of life."
That would mean that TF2 is incredibly spicy.
And sense it is spicy, many players will try it, find it is too much for them, and never return.
But then, after hearing the praise of the dish from their friends and the internet, they will try it again.
Perhaps they will enjoy it more this time.
And if they do, they will want to taste its spicy goodness again. So they eat more.
Then they discover they can season it with spices themselves. This allows them to customize their dish, into something uniquely their own.
And as they eat more and more of this culinary masterpiece, their table manners become better, and their eating is less sloppy.
Eventually, they develop an addiction. They love this dish too much, and can't stop eating it, every day, all day.
Then something goes wrong.
Perhaps it interfered with their social life, or they slipped up and spilled the food everywhere. The French waiter says, "Dominated, you fatuous, fat-headed fat man!"
They stop eating the dish for a while. They set their life back on track, and perhaps start eating dishes that are... less spicy, more common, and provide some satisfaction while still being fairly healthy.
Their life continues.
But as they settle back into their monotone life, with the same dishes just being pumped out to them, year after year, they think, "Well, maybe one dish of that spicy goodness would be nice. Just for a little variety."
They eat the dish again. They find that it is now almost completely different, while still spicy and enjoyable.
They decide to spend a bit of extra cash on extra things the diner offers. Maybe a couple of sides, a bit more seasoning, even some famous culinary dresswear.
They find that they are now better at eating this meal than most, and their spirits skyrocket.
They continue eating.
One day, one of their friends decides to try the meal. Finding it too spicy for his taste, he shoves it away in disgust and confusion.
A few months later, he is convinced by his cultured friend to try it again.
Perhaps he will enjoy it more this time.

TF2 is an F2P game that's as hilarious as it is competitive, with tons of customizable cosmetics to choose from the Mann Co. store to make your classes look completely badass or something that just looks like it came straight from the depths of hell. Let's dig into this.
Pros:
*Gameplay is fun and wonderfully gory (whether it's landing the perfect headshot with sniper or team wiping the enemy off the face of the earth with heavy, it constantly keeps you entertained)
*Classes are unique and offer different play styles and pathways for you to choose (whether it's silently picking off people as spy or blazing into battle with pyro, there's always a job for you to do).
*Lots of different modes to choose, from King of the Hill, Defense, Attack to Pushing the Cart, there's a lot to try out.
*Community made maps are always fun and offer new ways to eviscerate your enemies, from achievement to minecraft themed servers, the options are endless!
Cons:
*You can easily feel overwhelmed by everything that's going on in a match if you've just joined, leaving you completely vulnerable to pro players who come charging in and wiping you and your whole team in a matter of seconds.
*Combat gets repetitive eventually and feels more like a chore than anything else.
*You die pretty much instantaneously if you're targeted by an enemy demo/soldier/heavy without any backup making trying to get from place to place annoying at times with them in the way.
*Due to being a mostly cosmetic driven game, you'll often find yourself spending a lot more cash than you'd expect you would on a last minute Christmas shopping spree at Christmas Eve in the middle of New York.

Team Fortress 2 is a bright and colorful first person shooter with over-the-top weapons and nine zany classes to play as. Each one is suited for a different style of gameplay, for example; the spy class is not meant to taken into the thick of battle. Instead, he has equipment that allows him to slip past the front lines undetected. Once he's in behind the enemy, he shows himself right before he strikes from the shadows. This mechanic forces teams to work together and counter each others weaknesses, which makes solo stands or strikes into unbreakable defenses or unstobbable attacks. If the 700 ways of killing someone don't appeal to you, that's okay since this game has taunts that you can buy that allow other people from both teams to join in, such as the High five, Square Dance, and the infamous Conga line. This game is bursting with hilarious quotes from the nine classe and is packed to the brim with cosmetics to accesorize your characters, leading this game to be called a "war-themed hat simulator". this game will never leave you bored with constant updates, enjoyable distractions, and being able to find someone online at any time. the community isn't left out of this either, you can create new levels for the game, new weapos, cosmetics, or vidoes using source film maker. In conclusion, this game is only getting better as time goes on. With tons of new updates, items, and players joining the fray, this game will not dissapoint if your looking for a high-flying good time.

I have over 5000+ hours in this game in both of my new and old accounts.
I started playing this game at oct. 2010. A friend gifted me orange box and i found myself in this game. I was on my old account btw. I played it and i loved it. I got introduced into trading shortly after starting the game. I traded and i was getting good at it. There are special trading servers called ''unusual trading servers'' where you trade valuable items and unusual hats basicly. I became wealthy and found myself into one of those servers. I gambled my items and lost, but i did not give the items because i didnt want to lose those items i worked so hard for.... i ran away and got banned from other servers. I started trading on my own and everytime i joined a server, i was getting insults and i was called a scammer. Now the thing i did wasnt right but i had no idea about the consequences... nobody tried to help me or contact me to fix what i have done and make me aware of the results. I traded a lot and i traded both fairly and unfairly since i experienced humiliation. I sharked, scammer and got scammed. I made over 3000$ and reached the peak of my wealth around 2015.I did this on my own without the help of  other people and without using trading sites like backpack.tf and tf2outpost. Speaking of those sites... those sites are created to make trading easier but they got turned into sites that manipulate item prices for the profit of contributors and administrators. Those sites and those horrible people are to blame for the messed up state of tf2 economy. They destroyed the game currency just to profit out of the game. There is also a system/site called Steamrep.... a very evil collection of people that lack empathy and morality.....it is a third party site that has the power of tagging people as scammers and banning them from servers ( my case is an example ) and it is almost impossible to appeal your ban because they decide that with their biased and illegitemaate judgement. I made that much profit and slapped it to their faces, at one point, they were even making people add me to threaten me and break my spirit. Anyway, they never had a chance of stopping me. I was rich..I was wealthy but i wasnt happy. I traded and traded but never got the pleasure of belonging in a community because of my tag and my background. I didnt have many games in my account so i decided to open a new account for a fresh start. I transfered my items to that account but they found me there too. I decided to cash out because i knew that it would be pointless to continue trading in my new account. I cashed my items, bought new games and stuff i like. I quit tf2 around the late 2016. These 7 years were painful but i also made very precious friends and i made good memories in tf2. Not to mention my huge profit! If you want to buy tf2 and proceed in tf2 trading, dont be like me.... know everything about third party sites and know them well.
About game play; tf2 is a very fun game but like every other valve game it has toxic children in it.
It is a very fun game with friends! BUT......... considering how they murdered tf2 with the recent game updates.... i dont really see a reason to love this game anymore.... this is my personal opinion about the game... I dont recommend TF2... it became a money trap for children and a waste of time for everyone else....

What's killed this game for me is the community. The community consists of a bunch of elitests who think this is the best and only team based game that has a right to exist. I've seen TF2 fans bash any other class oriented game relentlessly, claiming it was a rip off and that TF2 was superior. if you dared to disagree, you were just called a COD fanboy over and over. Gameplay wise the game is solid, and can be outright addicting sometimes. The competitive scene was also a fresh breath of air when it first dropped, but those were probably the only two good parts about this game. The recent updates were just cash grabs, no argument about that. It seems Valve is starting to care less and less about it's fanbase, and more about making a buck. Can't complain about weapon balance, since it's downright impossible to have a 100% balanced game, it just can't be done. But back to the community.
Remember when Overwatch was announced? The game had lots of charm, interesting characters and just looked like an all around blast. A few Youtubers got their hands on the beta, then all hell broke loose. Wave after wave of TF2 fans just attacked the comment sections, saying how Overwatch was horrible and TF2 is better in comparison. After that, i just straight uninstalled. There was a time when this community was warm and inviting, and actually better than the COD community. But now it's just as bad, if not worse. Muting them doesn't do much, since they're in every server. I just can't reccomend this game to anyone, and i just can't stand to play it anymore. I've been playing since the moment it went F2P, and had some fun times with friends over the years. But none of these friends play this game anymore, most likely because they share the same views of it as i do.
TL;DR: This community is garbage, and i don't see it getting any better in the future.

It's ridiculous for me not to have more time already on this game. I have technically only been playing this since around the new year, though, so, whatever I guess. I've been playing TF2 since... Well, ever since it was around up and free to play. Not that I -actively- played it, my bad little computer was a bit too... bad to play anything then, but now with my new computer I'm free to have a small virtual screen suck away my eyesight and power and soul into something that matters very little because I occassionally enjoy to see men shoot each other with peas. And fires. And swords and--
Team Fortress 2 is an interesting mix of a game, it combines action and shooter with something brand new, team work! Yea, whoever thought of that before. You, the player, control a vast variety of mercs, 9 in total, on two opposing sides. Red and Blu. Blu works as an attacking team, pushing a cart/bomb through several checkpoints to blow up the Red's base, and consequentially Red is the defending team. This is only one instance of a single game more. There are also capture the flag (a single intelligence briefcase, or flag, must be capped by either team, with each holding one in a location behind their lines), king of the hill, Attack/Defend (same as payload explained earlier, while now only working in single-location checkpoints), and a few others.
These 'vast variety of mercs' I mentioned earlier come in 3 sets. Attacking revolve around the Scout, the fastest class in the team, a Soldier, a rocket-launcher weilding... soldier. And the Pyro. I'm sure you could imagine what they do, pretty much the crowd-controlling fire-wielding muffled maniac. Now for Defense you have the Demoman and his use of pipebombs (don't think of Left 4 Dead, and you're good, these things can explode on contact) and stickybombs to set up traps. Heavy is the opposite of Scout. Slowest moving class, while also the one with the just about the biggest moving gun you ever seen. Oh, and he has a mini-gun too, so. There's also Engie, with his sentries. Also the biggest moving gun you've ever seen, but it sadly only rotates. On Support you have the Sniper, long-range guy that crits with headshots, a Medic that can heal and *over*-heal, up to a certain fraction of health, and the spy. Backstabbing sort that can disguise as any of the above said teams, even his own team, while also critting for stabbing people in the back.
Now, you read all of what I said, right? Yea, forget all of that.
Over the years Valve has added so many different weapons and tactics that can be applied to all the above classes that they can play a crucial role in any sort of team set-up. Sniper can play attacking, Pyro becomes a support, spy becomes an attack class, like, what even? It's going to be confusing. Trust me, you won't suddenly run into the game thinking you're all that and a pile of pyrovision. But just find out what you like to do the most, and run around with that class. But considering this is *Team* Fortress, you can't become so self-absorbed in your fun that you allow the other team to win. That's right this game has a bit of strategy.
There's a reason why some people throw around the words 'setup' and 'class formation' that actually isn't ever used in game and people only tend to complain about why there's 4 snipers on one team. The thing is-- some, read; most, teams can't win with 4 snipers on a team. You need to learn to be varied in your composition. Does your team really need that 3rd engineer that you're playing as, or could you spend a little bit with pyro? C'mon you know you love 'em.
All that aside, there is now MvM mode (which has probably been out for a while hasn't it) which pits you and a full team of mercs, side-by-side, against a massive hoarde of robots. This mode is unique in (how buggy it is--) how there are upgrades for your mercs. Spend a few bucks from killing robots to upgrade your heavy's firing speed, or how quick a scout can run. These upgrades only apply to you, but if you decide to play a different class in between rounds, ensure that you hit the refund upgrade button if anything. You could also choose to spend a few dollars on an MvM ticket, which allows you to play through a tour, a real set of missions that grant you the ability to win special items at the end of the whole tour. Bootcamp also enables you to play-- without winning items-- single maps to test out how well your composition fairs. There's that word again, huh?
Oh, and also items. Yea. The community is crazy over items. You get unlockables, which you can craft in turn for new/different items, or craft a set of cosmetics. Did I say the community is crazy over items? I meant it's crazy over cosmetics. There's a whole deal about hats or something? But yea, you can buy keys to unlock crates that you can randomly unlock through play, or spend some time trading for a probably-over-priced-hat-that-matters-little-now kinda hat. I mean, the possibilities are endless here! You also gain items through getting enough achivements through the specific classes themselves.
SO, let's hit a little recap through pros and cons, shall we?
Pros:
+ Semi-diverse class set-up and gameplay through different items.
+ Many, many different plays ensures mostly different gameplay.
+ Diverse maps as well, each with it's own set of tactics and strategy for different teams
+ Great fanbase, really, they're all so loving and warm. You will (hopefully) find one or two people within the game that are pretty cool. Do your best to ask to befriend them, but don't push it.
+ Seriously no one likes spammy little kids calling each other bad names. Just don't. You'll get gagged and kicked from the lobby. Speaking of which, there actually is an option to kick annoying little kids that you'll hopefully not become.
+ Hats
Cons:
- Despite the diversity and amount of items, some classes will be left lacking without significant thought put into them beforehand playing. Medic is still just a single support class.
- There are still a few bugs within the game that has not been solved out just yet, despite the amount of work valve's put into it.
- It will definitely be rough for newcomers. Some games you'll find easy, but unless you're a big pro, and even then, sometimes it will get frustrating. Expect a lot of copy and paste binds that are designed to make you mad after everytime you're killed by that one specific person.
- Tauntkilling, dominations and general dumbo teammates might aggrivate you more than once.
- Hats.
Overall Team Fortress 2 is a game about hats and nothing else, that's all there is to it. Now get in there and get some hats.

I've been playing TF2 for Mac since it came out in 2010. I downloaded it within a few months of its release as evidenced by my earbuds, the only cosmetic I had at the time, when they seemed like a dead giveaway that I was a noob, rather than whatever they came to mean as a currency of pseudo-unusuals.
I bought TF2 as the Orange Box. I already had Portal because it was gifted to everyone who installed Steam on OSX right after release, and I didn't really care about HL2. I paid $20 for TF2 and never regretted it for a second.
Now that it's free TF2 is a great game for anyone interested in the genre. There are always people to play with and every pub match is different.
It also runs on relatively slow/old/OSX hardware compared to other games, since it uses the older Half Life 2 engine. To me the graphics are easily good enough for enjoying the action and the physics are carefully programmed for enjoyability, if not "realism".
It's an elaborate and multidimensional strategy game in many ways, so don't expect everything to make sense immediately. Anything is possible in this world, as long as it has a kitschy theme. The spy and medic in particular take awhile to appreciate. Many players have been learning the classes for years, so you need to expect an adjustment period.
To make the most of classes I recommend searching for YouTube guides. They will show you what is possible and what it looks like when it works, which is a start.
"Mini-game" strategies like rocket jumping take actual practice and training to get competent with, though all classes except the spy are capable of getting things done without any specialist knowledge.
There are hundreds of weapons that affect the metagame in complex ways, which is an amazing addition to the game but also means new players have to be very observant and do research outside the game to understand what each item does and how they should counter/complement them.
Never buy anything from the "Mann Co Store", it's a terrible ripoff. The community market is the "auction house" and works well, distributing your money to other players with a fair tax to Valve.
My favorite type of weapon is Strange, which means it counts the number of kills or points scored with an item. Strange weapons quantify your efforts and they have cute named "levels" that give an RPG leveling-up feeling, despite not being any more deadly or useful than non-strange items that don't count kills.
TF2 has incredible expansibility with mods, especially the HUDs, which redesign the entire game interface for better usability and/or style. I use 7HUD to make the UI feel more modern and move important data like ammo and life toward the center of the screen where I am usually looking. I love the options for mods and applaud Valve for creating such an expandable system. I have programmed scripts for myself and found others online. It's great to be able to do things like simulate holding down Mouse1 for ergonomic reasons and adding more keyboard shortcuts for spy disguises.
TF2 has had so many updates since it was released that I consider it a completely new game. If not a sequel, it is the equivalent of a game and dozens of DLC all available to everyone for free.

Team Fortress 2 is my favorite free-to-play class-based teamwork oriented first-person shooter/war-themed hat simulator of all time.
With nine different classes, each having three different weapon slots (in some cases four or more) that can have different weapons of each type changed throught to alter the playstyle of the already incredibly unique character and customize them to fit your playstyle.
Along with this, you can personalize your classes further by dressing them in a variety of hats, be it a plague doctor's mask, a fedora, or even a giant banana painted lime green.
Team Fortress 2 also allows members of the community to host their own servers where they can do whatever they please. Some are dedicated to in-game trading, others host various minigames such as deathrun or prophunt.
The gameplay is like no other, and can take a little getting used to. What other games these days allow you to propel yourself through the air using rocket launchers taking only small amounts of damage, or let you beat your friends over the head with frying pans?
This game, although nearly a decade old, is still going strong thanks to it's wonderful community, be it YouTubers, Source Filmmaker animators, community Workshop designers, or just the playerbase in general, and I would highly recommend you check out TF2. I can almost guarantee you'll be pleased with what you find.

How to Cook Babies in the Microwave
Babies, the tender little babies, or new born, can be any variety of immature human. The microwave oven is a good cooking method for babies because they have a high moisture content that works well for steaming. While regular babies are available year-round, Jewish babies are often found in spring and summer because they are harvested early and then sold shortly thereafter.
Step 1 Select firm baby buttocks with smooth skin and no cuts or blemishes. Avoid babies with sprouts or green areas.
Step 2 Wash the babies under cool water, using a vegetable brush to remove soil and loose skin. Babies need no peeling, as the tender skin is flavourful and nutrient-rich.
Step 3 Cut the babies in half. If the babies are very small, leave them whole.
Step 4 Place butter or margarine in a microwave-safe baking dish. For a low-fat dish, use heart-healthy canola oil or olive oil.
Step 5 Heat the butter for about 20 seconds, or until it melts. Arrange the babies on top of the melted butter. Stir gently to coat the babies with butter.
Step 6 Sprinkle pepper and salt on the babies. You can also add extra seasonings or herbs such as seasoned salt, thyme, rosemary, parsley, paprika, dill or garlic powder.
Step 7 Cover the baking dish. If the baking dish doesn't have a lid, use wax paper or cover the dish loosely with plastic wrap.
Step 8 Cook the potatoes on high power for 9 to 11 minutes, or until the babies are tender. Stir the babies once about halfway through the cooking time. Larger black babies may require up to 16 minutes.
Step 9 Allow the babies to stand for 3 to 5 minutes before serving. A short resting is necessary because the babies continue to cook for a few minutes after they're removed from the microwave oven.

I've been playing TF2 for Mac since it came out in 2010. I downloaded it within a few months of its release as evidenced by my earbuds, the only cosmetic I had at the time, when they seemed like a dead giveaway that I was a noob, rather than whatever they came to mean as a currency of pseudo-unusuals.
I bought TF2 as the Orange Box. I already had Portal because it was gifted to everyone who installed Steam on OSX right after release, and I didn't really care about HL2. I paid $20 for TF2 and never regretted it for a second.
Now that it's free TF2 is a great game for anyone interested in the genre. There are always people to play with and every pub match is different.
It also runs on relatively slow/old/OSX hardware compared to other games, since it uses the older Half Life 2 engine. To me the graphics are easily good enough for enjoying the action and the physics are carefully programmed for enjoyability, if not "realism".
It's an elaborate and multidimensional strategy game in many ways, so don't expect everything to make sense immediately. Anything is possible in this world, as long as it has a kitschy theme. The spy and medic in particular take awhile to appreciate. Many players have been learning the classes for years, so you need to expect an adjustment period.
To make the most of classes I recommend searching for YouTube guides. They will show you what is possible and what it looks like when it works, which is a start.
"Mini-game" strategies like rocket jumping take actual practice and training to get competent with, though all classes except the spy are capable of getting things done without any specialist knowledge.
There are hundreds of weapons that affect the metagame in complex ways, which is an amazing addition to the game but also means new players have to be very observant and do research outside the game to understand what each item does and how they should counter/complement them.
Never buy anything from the "Mann Co Store", it's a terrible ripoff. The community market is the "auction house" and works well, distributing your money to other players with a fair tax to Valve.
My favorite type of weapon is Strange, which means it counts the number of kills or points scored with an item. Strange weapons quantify your efforts and they have cute named "levels" that give an RPG leveling-up feeling, despite not being any more deadly or useful than non-strange items that don't count kills.
TF2 has incredible expansibility with mods, especially the HUDs, which redesign the entire game interface for better usability and/or style. I use 7HUD to make the UI feel more modern and move important data like ammo and life toward the center of the screen where I am usually looking. I love the options for mods and applaud Valve for creating such an expandable system. I have programmed scripts for myself and found others online. It's great to be able to do things like simulate holding down Mouse1 for ergonomic reasons and adding more keyboard shortcuts for spy disguises.
TF2 has had so many updates since it was released that I consider it a completely new game. If not a sequel, it is the equivalent of a game and dozens of DLC all available to everyone for free.

I don't know what to write, so here's the recipe for chocolate chip cookies:
Ingredients
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
3/4 cup packed dark brown sugar
3/4 cup sugar
2 large eggs
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
1 (12-ounce) bag semisweet chocolate chips, or chunks
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 teaspoon baking soda
1 teaspoon fine salt
Directions
Evenly position 2 racks in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375 degrees F. (on convection setting if you have it.) Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone sheets. (If you only have 1 baking sheet, let it cool completely between batches.)
Put the butter in a microwave safe bowl, cover and microwave on medium power until melted. (Alternatively melt in a small saucepan.) Cool slightly. Whisk the sugars, eggs, butter and vanilla in a large bowl until smooth.
Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt in another bowl. Stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients with a wooden spoon; take care not to over mix. Stir in the chocolate chips or chunks.
Scoop heaping tablespoons of the dough onto the prepared pans. Wet hands slightly and roll the dough into balls. Space the cookies about 2-inches apart on the pans. Bake, until golden, but still soft in the center, 12 to 16 minutes, depending on how chewy or crunchy you like your cookies. Transfer hot cookies with a spatula to a rack to cool. Serve.
Store cookies in a tightly sealed container for up to 5 days.
For a Rocky Road Bar
Lightly butter a 9 by 13-inch baking pan. Make the batter as per cookie recipe and fold in 1 cup chopped walnuts along with the chocolate chips. Spread batter in prepared pan. Bake until the edges are light brown and the batter sets, about 45 minutes. Cool slightly and cover surface with 4 cups marshmallows and 1 cup chocolate chips. Broil at least 8 inches from the heat until marshmallows turn golden brown, about 2 minutes. (Keep an eye on the marshmallows, and turn the pan frequently--they go from golden to char in a wink.) Cool, cut and serve.

Team Fortress 2 is absolutely no doubt the most addicting first person shooter I have ever played hands down!
The game has variety of full teamwork ability and strongly encouraged.
The problem? There isn't "Team" in Team Fortress 2 anymore...
Let's go into detail shall we?
I played Team Fortress 2 back in the end of 2010 and to the beginning of 2011. I even played TF2 on my Xbox at 2009 and on Xbox I was ranked 60 worldwide for a while. TF2 now a days... is just not the same as it is. The MAJOR problem in Team Fortress 2 is Pubs. The games main focus is pubs and pubs are just... awful. Its basically a Deathmatch of all classes and the worst part is there really isnt any variety in classes. Everyone in TF2 mains either Scout, Soldier, or Sniper (mostly sniper).
The TF2 Gameplay Mechanics
are good for what their class does but new weapons introduced made the game just... less enjoyable. Lets put into the example of the Phlog. The Phlog was always hated by practically the whole community and Valve knew it. Instead? They BUFF it instead of NERF it. They finally (nerfed) it so its actually "kinda" fair now but its things like this where I wonder if the TF2 team actually has any idea what they're doing. Valve also for whatever reason loves random crits in Team Fortress 2. They used to have an option to where you could vote on the server to turn off Random crits but they instead realised "Hey... that's dumb, people aren't supposed to have fun in this game lol." Then added back Random Crits to stay and you cant vote it off. This is another example of how Valve really doesn't know what in Gods name they're doing.
The TF2 Community
is HORRIBLE to say the least. At times i'd say it can possibly be even worse then the COD community. I ATLEAST had a few laughs with people in the COD community (not saying its a good community its just an example) If anyone tries talking in the mic its usually "Shut up ♥♥♥♥♥♥" The community is also really stupid... fights will break out everywhere for the dumbest reasons and most people have no idea how to actually play the game and if you try giving them any tips whatsoever the topic of choice usually ends in a arguement of how "you're bad". Chatting in TF2 is nonexistent because chats are usually filled with overused le lennys and stupid binds that are honestly awful and not funny and to the point where people will only use one bind the whole game and actually focus on using binds more then actually playing the game. Bronies and Furries are just everywhere... I really dont have a problem with them but the thing is that they're the kind that like to jam it down your throat and have their name as "Rainbow Dash" and have MLP related things like really? Fanbases practically ASK THEMSELVES to be made fun of by everyone and if you do you will have hell raised upon you. Seriously this game's community is beyond awful.
The TF2 Market
is so boring now. Unusuals back in around 2010-2013 were pretty rare to come by and when people saw you with an unusual they thought "Wow how cool, this guy is original" thing about Unusuals NOW is that everyone practically has one, being a game second focused on design this gets pretty boring and old to say the least considering that unusuals were made for the purpose of being "original" and were fun to look at back then. Escrow also made the TF2 Market 100% WORSE. TF2 Trade servers are mostly dead with just a couple that still live with a full server of people who actually go there.
The TF2 Updates
used to be so cool and fun. Valve however decided that it would be cool for the community to make some. Which was honestly, a good idea. Too bad they thought that EVERY MAJOR UPDATE should be community based. Yeah great... Its not even the Communitys fault for the updates they make but it lacks DEVELOPMENT of what a real MAJOR update could be, you know... the COMPANYS JOB!!? Now all new updates consist of NEW SKINS AND CONTRACTS. WE DONT EVEN GET NEW HATS BARELY ANYMORE OF WHAT THIS GAME IS FOCUSED ON. The worst part is that Valve doesnt even know what to do in the game anymore. A good example of this is that Valve nerfs Engineer when Engineer is pretty balanced... Just when people found tactics on how to effectivly play Engineer, their response is to nerf Engineer to the core and make sure he cannot do anything to protect anything. This game is supposed to have variety with all classes and they completely spit on certain classes like Engie. Also weapons like The Beggars Bazooka for Soldier should really only be available in gamemodes like Mann Vs Machine. Some weapons in TF2 are just flat out broken and I still question "Who the Hell even THOUGHT of this".
The TF2 Competitive Scene
is by far the ONLY GOOD SUBJECT OF THIS GAME! Good luck starting in a TF2 pub. You will not get any practice of any actual competitive interest except aiming and shooting. The Competitve Community for TF2 is... Better? It's still pretty bad but it is by far SO much better then the TF2 normal community. Competitive games for TF2 is amazing if you're playing for real. There is two gamemodes that are majorly competitive being Highlander and 6s. Highlander consists of being more teamwork based. Its one of each class fighting another team that consist of one of each class, HL's desired maps are usually Payload and King of the Hill but can consist of Control Points as well. 6s is more Deathmatch based but still desires teamwork. 2 Scouts (Utilities), 2 Soldiers (1 Pocket, 1 Roamer), Demoman, and Medic are the prime classes on each. Different classes are allowed however usually the Scouts switch IF NEEDED (For example if one of the Scouts is good at Sniper they can quickly switch to Sniper and play Sniper for the time being until they want to switch out to another class or stay Scout) The reason why the Scouts are called Utilities is because they are probably the best set in 6's but can be switched as they aren't as important as having Soldiers or the Demo or Medic.
Overall if your question is whether this game is worth it or not all leads to you... However I recommend that you only play TF2 if you're interested in the Competitive scene. TF2 is by far the best and most addicting First Person Shooter by far but lacks the majority of things that make the game just unenjoyable.

Like its predecessors, Team Fortress 2 is focused around two opposing teams competing for a combat-based principal objective.In the game's fiction, the teams are composed of mercenaries hired by two feuding brothers to protect the company assets belonging to one brother while trying to destroy those of the other; the teams are thus represented by the names of these companies: Reliable Excavation & Demolition (RED) and Builders League United (BLU). Players can choose to play as one of nine character classes in these teams, each with his own unique strengths, weaknesses, and weapons. Although the abilities of a number of classes have changed from earlier Team Fortress incarnations, the basic elements of each class have remained, that being one primary weapon, one secondary weapon, and one melee weapons.The game was released with six official maps, although 44 extra maps, 9 arena maps, 8 king of the hill maps, and various other map types have been included in subsequent updates.In addition, a number of community assembled maps have been released. When players join a level for the first time, an introductory video shows how to complete its objectives.
