A free game.    Nothing to loose here than right. Runs on any pc practically. alot of content.  Feels very original.
It isnt a pay to win.  there are 9 unique classes to choose from with unique abilities and purposes. Most of the best gear is often stock standard starting gear so rookies start at somewhat an advantage. But there are so many weapons or loadouts to make for your characters to change the way you play. Characters are very well balanced, but like every game some characters can be abused (refer later). The only reason to pay for anything is to get something rediculous like a glow in the dark hot dog on your head or a taunt which often is interactive. But more often than not because the community has created an economy, you can trade resources for what you may want (cheaper). So its stupid.  At the same time it is competative and tactical.
There are 2 main gameplay types. The first original game which is a red (defenders) vs blue (attackers) scenario where there are heaps of gametypes and maps and its just get the objective there and kill the guys along the way. Game types are fun and its very decently balanced.
Only problem just like any other game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s who abuse game mechanics. Very rare but there are players who spawn kill and its hard to avoid when they simply keep throwing explosive traps in the spawn point and continously detonate them.  Thats the worst of it. And they dont last very long.
There is also holiday events too with unique map and scenario/gametype.
Then theres Man vs machine where its human players of their choice of class and loadout defending against waves of robot version of the classes you play as. (they can vary heavily from their loadout, to their size, to their modifier. eg. 100 baseball giant scouts or rapid fire soldier). Collect money from dead enemies to upgrade your character. You and your team can upgrade your character's attack or defence or abilities to take on the hoard. Requires teamwork.
This game also has somewhat custom games where if you search in the server list, you can find very unique gametypes or modified original gametypes.  EG  FAVE: slenderman multiplayer (there is more than just slenderman, like fnaf, weeping angles doctor who, amnesia, anythign horror based),  Sports, huge mvm maps, weird campaigns, obsticle cource, death run, race, minecraft, trading servers, and there are things almost copied right over from other games like smahs brothers campaign.

So, what's so great about Team Fortress 2?
Well first off it's free, but that's not my point. It is the free-to-play model in TF2 that makes it work so well. Instead of buying boosts for in-game perks or having in-game currency, TF2 has hats.
Yup.
Hats, cosmetics, taunts to enrage your opponents, crates with a 0,004 % chance of containing a smoking sombrero (witch would actually be worth like 60 $).
Secondly, this game is 10 years old. Believe me, the graphics wont be a disturbance; the unique cartoony style of this game hides the graphical limitations of the time it was released shockingly well. But it is not a game made for today's expectations of competitive shooters. At the time of this review, competitive matchmaking is in Beta, but it has only been available to certain players.
Oh, the gameplay? Well, it is a bit of everything. It is easy to get in to, yet it offers so much to learn and to master. There are 9 classes that each have an unique and interesting playstyle, there are certainly 30 different maps and 7 different gamemodes. If you like hectic and variated gameplay, but are not afraid to learn by your mistakes, this is a game for you.

I don't know what to write, so here's the recipe for chocolate chip cookies:
Ingredients
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
3/4 cup packed dark brown sugar
3/4 cup sugar
2 large eggs
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
1 (12-ounce) bag semisweet chocolate chips, or chunks
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 teaspoon baking soda
1 teaspoon fine salt
Directions
Evenly position 2 racks in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375 degrees F. (on convection setting if you have it.) Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone sheets. (If you only have 1 baking sheet, let it cool completely between batches.)
Put the butter in a microwave safe bowl, cover and microwave on medium power until melted. (Alternatively melt in a small saucepan.) Cool slightly. Whisk the sugars, eggs, butter and vanilla in a large bowl until smooth.
Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt in another bowl. Stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients with a wooden spoon; take care not to over mix. Stir in the chocolate chips or chunks.
Scoop heaping tablespoons of the dough onto the prepared pans. Wet hands slightly and roll the dough into balls. Space the cookies about 2-inches apart on the pans. Bake, until golden, but still soft in the center, 12 to 16 minutes, depending on how chewy or crunchy you like your cookies. Transfer hot cookies with a spatula to a rack to cool. Serve.
Store cookies in a tightly sealed container for up to 5 days.
For a Rocky Road Bar
Lightly butter a 9 by 13-inch baking pan. Make the batter as per cookie recipe and fold in 1 cup chopped walnuts along with the chocolate chips. Spread batter in prepared pan. Bake until the edges are light brown and the batter sets, about 45 minutes. Cool slightly and cover surface with 4 cups marshmallows and 1 cup chocolate chips. Broil at least 8 inches from the heat until marshmallows turn golden brown, about 2 minutes. (Keep an eye on the marshmallows, and turn the pan frequently--they go from golden to char in a wink.) Cool, cut and serve.

Team Fortress 2 is a great game. Despite what people say it is not 'pay to win' every weapon (with the exception of reskins) can be found by just playing the game over time. Weapons are constantly being re-ballanced with every major update so that nothing is 'too overpowered' or 'too underpowered' and you don't need hats (or hacks) to get good at the game. Before you join your first game, lose and then get yelled at by that one Soldier with 3 unusuals just remember this: There are really nice player out there that will help you get good at the game and practice and there are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ players out there who will talk crap in chat when they kill you and wont bother telling you that the Rocket and Sticky Jumper do no damage. When you play Team Fortress 2 if you think you will like it, please, take your time to just sit down and play even if you don't get many kills because (from my experience at least) one day you will find a class you enjoy playing, get batter at it, find out new things you can do to help your team and different playstyles, start top scoring more and maybe just maybe you will find yourself here on the TF2 steam page writing a review that will get new players to give the game a try. TF2 is going through a rough time right now but remember this: TF2 has had bad updates in the past and many many good ones, I have full faith in the TF Team to start listening to us and relecing great updates again.

After 360 hours played, I think it's clear that I enjoy this game. I feel like I should explain to the community that hasn't gotten this game yet why.
I really like the cartoonish feel of this game. Unlike CounterStrike, Battlefield, or Call of Duty, this game offers a graphic experience like no other. Sure, it still has blood and gore, but it's not as much of a kill-them-all simulator as it is a fun, light game to play around on after a long day.
Another thing is the variation. I love the fact that there are so many weapons and qualities to choose from, and each rare weapon you find is a trophy to show off on the killcam. You need to earn each weapon, which is what I like about them. You can get killed by a not-so-rare weapon, like a Scarcely Lethal Shotgun, or a rare weapon, like an Australium Hale's Own Botkiller Professional Killstreak Scattergun.
While I like the game as a whole, there are some elements that could be improved upon, such as VAC. Hackers run without fear of getting caught in this game, because when a report with footage IS submitted, it is usually not seen by the administrators due to all the community garbage that fills up everything they have to look over. But overall, I like this game.

Do you have a favourite hobby?
Maybe you like skiing or riding a bike or maybe like me, you play video games. I like to play a game called Team Fortress 2. Team Fortress 2 is fun because it has a huge community of players from all over the world. Its also fun because I can play and chat with my friends and I can also trade items with people.
Even though I'm homeschooled and I don't see my friends much, I've still met heaps of new people who play TF2. Ive also introduced some of my other friends to the game as well.
One of the reasons I love the game so much is because of how much variety the game has to offer. For example TF2 has 12 different game modes, 9 different classes and OVER 1000 different hats and cosmetics!
Each class can have many different weapon load outs.
Each load out consists of one primary weapon, one secondary weapon (usually a pistol or shotgun) and one melee weapon (or close quarters weapon). There is one class that does not follow the rule of primary, secondary, melee. The spy has a knife as a primary a revolver as a secondary and an invisibility watch in his melee slot.
Team Fortress 2 has a huge community of over 100,000 players.
Many players make 3D models of new weapons and cosmetics and submit them to VALVe, VALVe the gets people from the community to vote on whether they want to see this item in the game or not.
If your item gets enough votes and is added to the game, you will be awarded that item with a special "self made" quality, to be used in game.
Playing online games such as TF2, can be a great way to make new friends that share your interests. But, as with all things you must take care in how much information you put out there. I love TF2 because there is so many different ways to play. With new content being released every few months players never get bored. TF2 is an enjoyable, mentally stimulating and social activity that can be experienced of people of all ages.

After 360 hours played, I think it's clear that I enjoy this game. I feel like I should explain to the community that hasn't gotten this game yet why.
I really like the cartoonish feel of this game. Unlike CounterStrike, Battlefield, or Call of Duty, this game offers a graphic experience like no other. Sure, it still has blood and gore, but it's not as much of a kill-them-all simulator as it is a fun, light game to play around on after a long day.
Another thing is the variation. I love the fact that there are so many weapons and qualities to choose from, and each rare weapon you find is a trophy to show off on the killcam. You need to earn each weapon, which is what I like about them. You can get killed by a not-so-rare weapon, like a Scarcely Lethal Shotgun, or a rare weapon, like an Australium Hale's Own Botkiller Professional Killstreak Scattergun.
While I like the game as a whole, there are some elements that could be improved upon, such as VAC. Hackers run without fear of getting caught in this game, because when a report with footage IS submitted, it is usually not seen by the administrators due to all the community garbage that fills up everything they have to look over. But overall, I like this game.

Team Fortress 2 is an online F2P FPS. It focuses on its 9 classes and massive item options. There are hundreds of weapons to collect, and each one actually feels unique and plays differently. It’s one of the most popular games for obvious reasons, such as its genre, community, and just how old it is.
You will have no issues with controlling this game, standard FPS with a few extra buttons here and there for doing various extra things depending on what class you are playing as. 10/10
The game sounds great, the titles screen music is fantastic. The voice acting is nice to hear when in combat, and fits each character perfectly. Rockets, flame throwers, guns, and melee weapons all sound good, some even have unique sounds exclusive to them. Sadly, there is rarely any music in the game, when you are fighting. 9/10
The game looks great in Source 2. Everything is polished well, the only real noticeable problem is some collision with different custom items on characters, but that doesn't affect gameplay at all. You can get this game to run on a variety of systems, allowing it to be played on Massive Gaming Pcs, and puny laptops to expand the player base. With all the settings you can get just the right performance you are looking for, at the frame rate you want.
10/10
The game is based completely online, so depending on what server you join and who you meet in battle, the game may be harder. However, to get combat ready, new users are given a tutorial to go through, as well as the option to host their own bot matches with a wide selection of difficulties. 10/10
The TF2 community is a mixed bunch. You have friendly players mixed in with the common online FPS player. I've never had any major problems in TF2 servers, but I usually disable talking in this game. It saves me the time of tracking that one annoying kid or jerk that is just screaming over the microphone. You also have community integration with those who wish to design weapons, it’s pretty cool. But I rarely see it used at all by valve. To finish, you have the trading community. I don't know what to say about these guys. Somehow, the community has managed to regulate prices on everything, Key to Refined metal rates, item values of unusual as such. I'll admit it’s amazing to see a market control itself under no guidance, but it ruins trading for me. the problem is everything has value. I can't trade anyone without hearing about the market. The idea of I want this and you want this is non-existent. It feels like I have to match values rather than wants with the other side, and to be honest, its rather annoying. 6/10
TF2 is a great shooter experience, and luckily, valve has made extensive community interaction completely optional, allowing you to focus on the bulk of the game. There is almost no reason to not try this game.
8.5/10 Strongly Recommended

I started playing Team Fortress 2 when I was a kid (6 years ago).
My dad invited me to play with him. I was so fascinated!
In that time:
-I experienced a first kiss with a girl,
-I bought a gaming PC,
-I traveled a lot,
-I got more than 450 games on Steam,
-I learned several programming languages,
-I started to work,
-I learnt English from nothing.
And all that time I was playing TF2. Every day, every evening.
I tried to stop, I thought that would make my life better.
It made it even worse, so I decited to continue playing it.
Forgive me for it!
Now I have around a thousand of hours in-game.
Now I have a lot of friends in different countries, some of them I met in real-life.
Thank you TF2 for helping me pass through my teenage years. Now, it's time to pass through even more difficult part of my life. I hope we'll do so together.

Team Fortress 2 is the team based, free to play sequal to the "Granddaddy of class-based multiplayer gaming", Team Fortress. While I have not played the original or its source version, Team Fortress Classic, I have played this one for a more than sensible amount of time...
The game's classes are very balanced, thanks in part to Valve constantly updating the game on a regular basis, as are the weapons you can aquire through random drops and completeing a certain amount of achievements for said class. The game types avalible are also very enjoyable to play, as are the large variety of maps said gamemodes occur on.
The game also allows for the customisation of the 9 classes using hats and costmetics which can be bought from the Mann Co store. While they do not actively affect the game itself, by giving players who are wearing the cosmetics as buff, they have created a large community of people who trade said hats for profits or, as I do, to create sets that they like.
This brings me onto my final point and what I see as both the best and worse parts of Team Fortress 2, it's community.
On one side we have the good parts of the community who create the amazing SFM shorts we see on youtube or the people who help add to this game by creating map, hats ect in the workshop so valve can focus on more imporant things like the very much anticipated Matchmaking Update. Also with them are the people who help teach the newer players the basics of the game and even befriend them, gifting them items that would otherwise be difficult to obtain. There are more people like this, but I like to think as these 3 examples as the best parts of this community.
Then, sadly, we have the other side of the community. TF2 is a free to play game and so, sadly, contains the bad parts of of the internet, as well as the good. In my time playing this game I have met some truely awful people. People who had such inflated egos it made them completely insufferable and made me switch teams just to dominate them. People who then starting flaming their team-mates when they started losing and would ♥♥♥♥♥ and complain until the round was over. Thankfully these people are rare and can easily be muted and ignored.
In conclusion, TF2 is a very balanced, fun, team based game to play with a somewhat decent community. However, some parts of said community are some of the worst people I have ever seen on the internet and are best ignored.

This was my first Team-Based First Person Shooter. I have fond memories which may nudge the store up a bit.
Pros:
+A fun, action packed TBFPS, with multiple gamemodes and tons of maps.
+Decently balanced weapons and classes
+Fun cosmetics
+Game community has it's own fluid economy
+It's Free-To-Play
Cons:
-VALVe's progress on this game is infuriatingly slow, and as one of its best money makers, that is nearly unforgivable
-This game can cost you a lot overtime if you allow the allure of crates and keys to overcome your common sense.
-Some of the maps and gamemodes are just bad
-The game's Free-To-Play nature attracts a low of cheaters
-Community is slowly dying due to Overwatch
-Some of the weapons are unbalanced, either becoming the meta or are never used, with few inbetween
On an "F- to A+" scale, this games gets a "B." Would recommend if you are bored and are too poor to buy Overwatch.

Team Fortress 2 is the team based, free to play sequal to the "Granddaddy of class-based multiplayer gaming", Team Fortress. While I have not played the original or its source version, Team Fortress Classic, I have played this one for a more than sensible amount of time...
The game's classes are very balanced, thanks in part to Valve constantly updating the game on a regular basis, as are the weapons you can aquire through random drops and completeing a certain amount of achievements for said class. The game types avalible are also very enjoyable to play, as are the large variety of maps said gamemodes occur on.
The game also allows for the customisation of the 9 classes using hats and costmetics which can be bought from the Mann Co store. While they do not actively affect the game itself, by giving players who are wearing the cosmetics as buff, they have created a large community of people who trade said hats for profits or, as I do, to create sets that they like.
This brings me onto my final point and what I see as both the best and worse parts of Team Fortress 2, it's community.
On one side we have the good parts of the community who create the amazing SFM shorts we see on youtube or the people who help add to this game by creating map, hats ect in the workshop so valve can focus on more imporant things like the very much anticipated Matchmaking Update. Also with them are the people who help teach the newer players the basics of the game and even befriend them, gifting them items that would otherwise be difficult to obtain. There are more people like this, but I like to think as these 3 examples as the best parts of this community.
Then, sadly, we have the other side of the community. TF2 is a free to play game and so, sadly, contains the bad parts of of the internet, as well as the good. In my time playing this game I have met some truely awful people. People who had such inflated egos it made them completely insufferable and made me switch teams just to dominate them. People who then starting flaming their team-mates when they started losing and would ♥♥♥♥♥ and complain until the round was over. Thankfully these people are rare and can easily be muted and ignored.
In conclusion, TF2 is a very balanced, fun, team based game to play with a somewhat decent community. However, some parts of said community are some of the worst people I have ever seen on the internet and are best ignored.

Honestly, I'm beyond disappointed.
Prior to the Mortal Kombat X launch, I was genuinely excited for the game. I had some good memories ofplaying the older games as a kid, and I some fun with MK9, but was a bit disappointed with the balance of the game.
So, I preorder this game. It looked well polished, great graphics and sound, smooth looking gameplay, tons of content, it had it all right? The launch was shaky at best. NRS tried a "streaming download" system with this game, where you downloaded the game in parts, and could play it as soon as it downloaded the parts necessary for gameplay. It's imilar to Blizzard's system in that respect, except it didn't work. I'm going to largely ignore the launch issues here, because they were fixed pretty soon, even if they left a bad taste in my mouth.
So, game finishes installing finally, and I hope online after a bit of practicing combos. I'm greeted with the most unplayably laggy online fighting game experience of my entire life. I am talking a solid 2 seconds of delay here. After a few more matches, all ending the same way, I decide to play some story mode. To be fair, the story is pretty fun, and well done for a fighting game.
I decided to wait until the port was fixed, with the lag issues and a nasty memory leak being present. I kind of forgot about the game for a while until I saw some cool Jason and Predator DLC matches on youtube. I figured "Hey, the port has been out a while, they probably fixed the problems right?", no they didn't.
Not only was the game still a mess, but NRS decided that they would completely abandon development of the PC version of the game, and it would no longer recieve any patches or DLC. This for me was the last straw. I'm personally never supporting NRS or WB games on PC again until they can prove to me that they deserve respect as a developer on the platform.
Do yourself a favour, save yourself a headache, and buy a game that actually works like Guilty Gear or Street Fighter.

The issue with TF2 is, I used to recommend it and like it. Now my recommendation has dwindled into something "iffy."
I personally don't have very many hours logged- certainly not as many as some people who exceed 1,000 hours. However my partner actually does have about that many hours, and I've watched him play far longer than I myself have actually played (to be honest, I kind of suck at it lol)
Here's the problem. It used to be a sort of funny, zany, silly, chaotic game that bordered on too difficult- it has a very high learning curve and can be extremely unforgiving to new players- but the community used to be nice and it was still fun to play. You really have to put in A LOT of time to "get good" at it, though. Otherwise prepare to die constantly.
Now, after many years, things have changed. I've watched my partner go from playing obsessively, to losing interest, to really disliking the game. Why? Here's why:
THE COMMUNITY.
It's turned over the years into more of a safehouse where teenagers who get bored of Call of Duty go to hang out. Neither of us can go on ANY servers now without being subjected to verbally abusive and immature 12 year olds with nothing else to do. People tagging softcore porn, spamming chat, screaming obscenities and berating each other... it's turned into a complete mess. Mods do nothing, reporting does nothing. It seems the target audience has just slipped from "young adults" to "inane children."
Also the whole thing about microtransactions is another downside. Idk why Valve decided to start selling weapons skins as a sort of status symbol, which allows people to feel superior simply because they paid $6.99 for a polka dot sniper rifle... The hat gimmick was cute and funny and didn't cause any problems, but then they started with those damn crates, and the keys became LITERALLY currency that people sell to each other to buy new outfits and skins. And now the weapon skins. Why has Valve turned TF2 into a cash grab? Who knows. All I know is it supports this idiotic psychology of "I'm better than you because I paid for this meaningless thing" and the type of people who make up all the players nowadays is toxic enough already.
So I've quit. My partner has quit after YEARS of playing. Many long-time players are just done now. Sad to see it go to waste but that's what happens with online communities apparently...

. TF2 is a great multiplayer first-person shooter that will be fondly remembered by many for years to come.
TF2 have a lot of maps and nine classes of characters: Pyro, Heavy, Spy, Scout, Sniper, Medic, Engineer, Demoman, and Soldier.
The focus in TF2 is on teams of players competing against each other to complete specific objectives on a variety of maps. These objectives can include stealing intelligence from the enemy team's base (this game's version of Capture The Flag) or capturing all the control points on a given map. There are several variations on the latter game type, each of which has its own subtleties. The most interesting game type is territorial control, which plays out as a series of smaller battles in a larger battle to control all the areas on a map.
All the classes are important and useful for a team's success. Scouts are far and away the fastest, and their ability to double-jump and change direction in mid-air makes then all the more difficult to hit. Spies, in addition to being able to one-hit kill backstab the enemy, cause general chaos among enemy ranks. If your opponents know a spy is running around, they'll waste time and lose focus by shooting at their own teammates to try and reveal a disguised culprit.
Pyros tend to be the most effective spy detectors, and can be frequently seen doing fiery pirouettes in the matches, as a spy incognito will betray his cover by bursting into flames upon contact with the burning spray.
Community participation in the game is colossal. New things are always being implemented, new weapons, new props, etc. Honestly, in my opinion, it's the community that made the game great. And it continues to do. You are always updated with new releases, what is incredible. Basically, all you need is a Steam account to play.

Honestly, I'm beyond disappointed.
Prior to the Mortal Kombat X launch, I was genuinely excited for the game. I had some good memories ofplaying the older games as a kid, and I some fun with MK9, but was a bit disappointed with the balance of the game.
So, I preorder this game. It looked well polished, great graphics and sound, smooth looking gameplay, tons of content, it had it all right? The launch was shaky at best. NRS tried a "streaming download" system with this game, where you downloaded the game in parts, and could play it as soon as it downloaded the parts necessary for gameplay. It's imilar to Blizzard's system in that respect, except it didn't work. I'm going to largely ignore the launch issues here, because they were fixed pretty soon, even if they left a bad taste in my mouth.
So, game finishes installing finally, and I hope online after a bit of practicing combos. I'm greeted with the most unplayably laggy online fighting game experience of my entire life. I am talking a solid 2 seconds of delay here. After a few more matches, all ending the same way, I decide to play some story mode. To be fair, the story is pretty fun, and well done for a fighting game.
I decided to wait until the port was fixed, with the lag issues and a nasty memory leak being present. I kind of forgot about the game for a while until I saw some cool Jason and Predator DLC matches on youtube. I figured "Hey, the port has been out a while, they probably fixed the problems right?", no they didn't.
Not only was the game still a mess, but NRS decided that they would completely abandon development of the PC version of the game, and it would no longer recieve any patches or DLC. This for me was the last straw. I'm personally never supporting NRS or WB games on PC again until they can prove to me that they deserve respect as a developer on the platform.
Do yourself a favour, save yourself a headache, and buy a game that actually works like Guilty Gear or Street Fighter.

The issue with TF2 is, I used to recommend it and like it. Now my recommendation has dwindled into something "iffy."
I personally don't have very many hours logged- certainly not as many as some people who exceed 1,000 hours. However my partner actually does have about that many hours, and I've watched him play far longer than I myself have actually played (to be honest, I kind of suck at it lol)
Here's the problem. It used to be a sort of funny, zany, silly, chaotic game that bordered on too difficult- it has a very high learning curve and can be extremely unforgiving to new players- but the community used to be nice and it was still fun to play. You really have to put in A LOT of time to "get good" at it, though. Otherwise prepare to die constantly.
Now, after many years, things have changed. I've watched my partner go from playing obsessively, to losing interest, to really disliking the game. Why? Here's why:
THE COMMUNITY.
It's turned over the years into more of a safehouse where teenagers who get bored of Call of Duty go to hang out. Neither of us can go on ANY servers now without being subjected to verbally abusive and immature 12 year olds with nothing else to do. People tagging softcore porn, spamming chat, screaming obscenities and berating each other... it's turned into a complete mess. Mods do nothing, reporting does nothing. It seems the target audience has just slipped from "young adults" to "inane children."
Also the whole thing about microtransactions is another downside. Idk why Valve decided to start selling weapons skins as a sort of status symbol, which allows people to feel superior simply because they paid $6.99 for a polka dot sniper rifle... The hat gimmick was cute and funny and didn't cause any problems, but then they started with those damn crates, and the keys became LITERALLY currency that people sell to each other to buy new outfits and skins. And now the weapon skins. Why has Valve turned TF2 into a cash grab? Who knows. All I know is it supports this idiotic psychology of "I'm better than you because I paid for this meaningless thing" and the type of people who make up all the players nowadays is toxic enough already.
So I've quit. My partner has quit after YEARS of playing. Many long-time players are just done now. Sad to see it go to waste but that's what happens with online communities apparently...

So let's break it down:
Gameplay: 10/10
Doesn't matter whether you like to do your own thing (On pubs you can just run around killing the enemy however you like) or want to play with friends (MvM or communities), you'll probably have fun. The game has endless replayability, but even if you get bored, there are updates every few months with new content and a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of achievements, so I doubt you would run out of things to do.
Performance and bugs: 8/10
The past few updates made the game run worse on potatoes, but I never had any performance issues myself. There are bugs, but only after bigger updates, and volvo usually fixes them asap.
community: 5/10
Seen worse. Veterans in this game have an endless hate for F2Ps (Players who play the game for completely free, so they never even bought anything in-game), mainly because they're usually 9 to 13 year olds who like to commentate their game constantly while they're standing on their ptt. Some people hate F2Ps because most hackers are also free to play.
There's also a bit of elitism between players who play MvM, which in the most extreme cases lead to kicking players who don't have much experience.
this isn't a problem if you play with your friends or in private communities. Also, most people in pubs are just silently playing, and even if you find a yelling 11 year old, you can just mute him, or disable voice communication altogether.
To sum it up, pros:
-Free to play
-lots of content
-huge replayability
-constant updates
-relatively stable, few bugs
cons:
-Not too great community, but way more bearable than CS:GO or LoL for example

. TF2 is a great multiplayer first-person shooter that will be fondly remembered by many for years to come.
TF2 have a lot of maps and nine classes of characters: Pyro, Heavy, Spy, Scout, Sniper, Medic, Engineer, Demoman, and Soldier.
The focus in TF2 is on teams of players competing against each other to complete specific objectives on a variety of maps. These objectives can include stealing intelligence from the enemy team's base (this game's version of Capture The Flag) or capturing all the control points on a given map. There are several variations on the latter game type, each of which has its own subtleties. The most interesting game type is territorial control, which plays out as a series of smaller battles in a larger battle to control all the areas on a map.
All the classes are important and useful for a team's success. Scouts are far and away the fastest, and their ability to double-jump and change direction in mid-air makes then all the more difficult to hit. Spies, in addition to being able to one-hit kill backstab the enemy, cause general chaos among enemy ranks. If your opponents know a spy is running around, they'll waste time and lose focus by shooting at their own teammates to try and reveal a disguised culprit.
Pyros tend to be the most effective spy detectors, and can be frequently seen doing fiery pirouettes in the matches, as a spy incognito will betray his cover by bursting into flames upon contact with the burning spray.
Community participation in the game is colossal. New things are always being implemented, new weapons, new props, etc. Honestly, in my opinion, it's the community that made the game great. And it continues to do. You are always updated with new releases, what is incredible. Basically, all you need is a Steam account to play.

is very competitive, similar to what happens in any competitive game. For some friends of mine there is life before TF2, and there is life after. They said after is better.
TF2 is always in the top-5 of the most played games on Steam. I think this says it all. TF2 is highly made for fun and it is filled with light-hearted animation. For a game that started out as just a multiplayer shooter, TF2 has become something astonishing.

Team Fortress two has been one of, if not, the best free shooters of all time. It boasts a stunning selection of classes, with possibly too many weapons - all boasting entertaining backstories that can be found within the comical aspect of it. Another brilliant thing that team fortress shows off is its persona as one of the silliest games ever made for a theme that it follows. For example, you have the over-exaggerated characters, in silly situations AND you have to give them silly gear. Yet, if this doesn't suit you enough then fear not! In team fortress 2, you can make your own server, and you can mod it. Yes from you-tubers to community supporters you can have your own private servers for your fans. And the variety of mos available for these servers is extreme. A good example, for those of you who wish for one, some servers contain randomisers, these enable a scout, for instance, to use a sniper rifle (used by the sniper); or a soldier to use a wrench (used by the engineer) enabling a great deal of diversity.

This game is one of the most unique FPS games I have ever played. If you ever wanted a FPS that's always active, has different playstyles, and has a lot of hats? This one's the game!
Now without any hesitation, here's how the game works:
There are 9 classes that you are able to choose.
3 are set into 3 groups: Offense, Defence, and Support.
OFFENSE
Scout: Quick as lighting, mainly used for close-range attacks. It's pretty easy to make a simple slip-up with this character, so you have to pay attention to where you're going.
Soldier: The Soldier is quite an amazing character. Using his rocket, he is able to do a huge leap into the air, which is known as a Rocket Jump. Also, he's not a real Soldier.
Pyro: The Pyro is very... unique in certain ways. Underneath this Pyromaniac is someone who just wants to have fun. With his flamethrower, shotgun, and Fireaxe, Pyro can make you burst into flames in mere seconds.
DEFENCE
Demoman: Almost ALWAYS drunk, even within battle, he can be very easy to use. Kinda like the Soldier, Demoman is able to place down his stickybombs, and detonate them at his own feet, launchin' him into the air. But, don't mess with him when he has a sword ;)
Heavy: The one who will mow down ANYONE! Slowest class, yet has a powerful Minigun. It costs $400,000 dollars to fire said weapon. If you want to mess with this guy within a fist fight, though... You better run!
Engineer: A person from Texas, who uses his Sentry-gun to shoot you with ease. Sure, it may seem hard to build a Sentry, but this Engineer has metal, which he can use to create or upgrade his buildings. "Sometimes, you just need a little less gun"
SUPPORT
Medic: As the name may suggest, he's the one who is able to heal the team. With the use of his medi-gun (Medical Gun), he can heal a teammate. As he heals a teammate, he builds up what's known as an übercharge. Once the übercharge is full, he can make his teammate and him invincible, have more power within there weapon, or more defence from attacks.
"Dummkopfs!"
Sniper: This New Zealander was raised in Australia. If you see one, make sure he doesn't hit you with his sniper rifle! It can do a headshot, and if you have played other games, that means a bad time for the person being headshot. He also carries an SMG and a kukri knife.
Spy: The sneaky one of all the characters. He is able to perform a lethal backstab with his Butterfly Knife. He wields a revolver, knife, and what's known as a sapper, which is used to disable the Engineer's buildings. But the sapper isn't that overpowered, because the sapper can be easily removed with the wrench, or the Pyro's Homewrecker. You gotta be sneaky and careful with this class. He can also disguise as one of the enemies teammates, so if you notice something unusual about a teammate, it may be a Spy.
Well, that explains the characters. The gameplay is as simple as I have explained it. But many people like to be greedy, because the game is F2P, and if you're not a P2P player, you can't trade your items. To become the said P2P player, you have to buy something from the Mann Co. Store, or buy the game when it was a paid game. You can also get P2P by buying the computer version of the Orange Box. The game is also a game FILLED with cosmetics. They're not part of the game, and are used to make your character look nicer. If you're still not convinced, there's also a friendly side to the game. If you don't want to be part of the friendly side, that's fine with me. There are many taunts you can do, such as a High Five or Conga.
tl;dr. If you want a good game, you can get it for... $60? $30? $5? No! It's the price of FREE!

There was once a time where I found enjoyment out of hopping into a random server and playing a few rounds with friends or randoms just for kicks. I've never really been skillful as an offensive, front lines class in TF2 or any other FPS game ( Medic main ftw :D ), but it was great nonetheless to work as part of a team to capture an objective. Sadly, that enjoyment has died with the "Pubocalypse," where the vast majority of servers are full of others who seem to lack a similar sentiment for teamwork. I've literally lost count of the number of times that I've been on the team getting steamrolled because of the severe lack of coordination, or when I've dropped a charge so tantalizingly close to 100% because your patient leads you straight into a pack of ravenous pyros, soldiers and demomen whilst refusing to fire a single shot (don't even get me started on the ones that run AWAY from battle when you give them invulns or crits). The game has gone from a fun way to pass the time to a test of your patience (which usually ends in a ragequit if you're like me) and sanity. Granted, the game is still a lot of fun if you have friends to play with and can schedule a time to wreak havoc on pubs or play MvM, but without friends this game is more apt to raise your blood pressure unless you can singlehandedly carry your team to victory with little to no issue (or unless you get lucky and end up on a server where players are knowledgeable in the long-lost art of teamwork).
As much as it pains me to say this due to the amount of time I've spent in this game (more close to 6-700 hours; I often left the game open when I first started playing it, and yes, I reset my stats once I hit 1K hours), I cannot recommend Team Fortress 2 to the proverbial new kid on the block in its current state, especially if you do not have friends that enjoy playing the game with you. The addition of competitive matchmaking may be this game's saving grace, but you're out of luck if you do not care for any of the traditional "6's" classes (unless, of course, highlander becomes a thing in competitive matchmaking too).

Team fortress 2
I would say after spending at least 1k hours on this game, it has an interesting and well desgined set up towards competeive team fights. As well as creating a goofy and entertaining enviorment that is customizable to a certain degree.
The game demands a heavy amount of teamwork towards objectives on maps. However at the same time, value has assesed the true interest of the game. Killing enemy players. This has been provided through arena modes, team competions, and a decent amount of maps that allow the player the simply enjoy themself within the enviroment given.
The game itself provides an exellent way of assisting new players, such as coaching which has an experienced player go out of their way in order to help new players. In doing so, experienced players are rewarded. However, this is what value has done in order to assist new players.
The community can be extremely harsh when it comes to new players. New players are easily identifed via not having any hats, having a hat that is easily accessaible via achievement, or simply inexperience. These players are looked down upon within the community due to their lack of understand towards certain events where players may be trying to do something outside of the common norm within the game and a new player disturbing it. It is also laid out that new players do not understand how to assist a team greatly, even sometimes ruining a game.
In my opinion, I believe that it would be benefical to most of the community that new players were to take some time to figure out classes, look up online tutorials towards how you should play your class, even take some time to face agianst hard bots.
An easy way to not be quickly looked down upon, targeted for pranks, is to simply buy a universal hat. This will give players the idea that you may not be 'free to play' so to speak. Though other than being targeted because of inexperience, the community can be quite...interesting. It all depends towarsd how you go about putting yourself out into the community.
Though this game provides a large variety of assests that protain towards the entiertainment needs of the vast majority of gamers through third party resources such as custom modders, map designers and much more.
In conclusion, I would find that this game is extremely fun, only if you can put together how you can do it well. Where exactly you may fit in with the community itself. If you find the right place to be, you can find yourself playing this game for a long time.

This game is one of the most unique FPS games I have ever played. If you ever wanted a FPS that's always active, has different playstyles, and has a lot of hats? This one's the game!
Now without any hesitation, here's how the game works:
There are 9 classes that you are able to choose.
3 are set into 3 groups: Offense, Defence, and Support.
OFFENSE
Scout: Quick as lighting, mainly used for close-range attacks. It's pretty easy to make a simple slip-up with this character, so you have to pay attention to where you're going.
Soldier: The Soldier is quite an amazing character. Using his rocket, he is able to do a huge leap into the air, which is known as a Rocket Jump. Also, he's not a real Soldier.
Pyro: The Pyro is very... unique in certain ways. Underneath this Pyromaniac is someone who just wants to have fun. With his flamethrower, shotgun, and Fireaxe, Pyro can make you burst into flames in mere seconds.
DEFENCE
Demoman: Almost ALWAYS drunk, even within battle, he can be very easy to use. Kinda like the Soldier, Demoman is able to place down his stickybombs, and detonate them at his own feet, launchin' him into the air. But, don't mess with him when he has a sword ;)
Heavy: The one who will mow down ANYONE! Slowest class, yet has a powerful Minigun. It costs $400,000 dollars to fire said weapon. If you want to mess with this guy within a fist fight, though... You better run!
Engineer: A person from Texas, who uses his Sentry-gun to shoot you with ease. Sure, it may seem hard to build a Sentry, but this Engineer has metal, which he can use to create or upgrade his buildings. "Sometimes, you just need a little less gun"
SUPPORT
Medic: As the name may suggest, he's the one who is able to heal the team. With the use of his medi-gun (Medical Gun), he can heal a teammate. As he heals a teammate, he builds up what's known as an übercharge. Once the übercharge is full, he can make his teammate and him invincible, have more power within there weapon, or more defence from attacks.
"Dummkopfs!"
Sniper: This New Zealander was raised in Australia. If you see one, make sure he doesn't hit you with his sniper rifle! It can do a headshot, and if you have played other games, that means a bad time for the person being headshot. He also carries an SMG and a kukri knife.
Spy: The sneaky one of all the characters. He is able to perform a lethal backstab with his Butterfly Knife. He wields a revolver, knife, and what's known as a sapper, which is used to disable the Engineer's buildings. But the sapper isn't that overpowered, because the sapper can be easily removed with the wrench, or the Pyro's Homewrecker. You gotta be sneaky and careful with this class. He can also disguise as one of the enemies teammates, so if you notice something unusual about a teammate, it may be a Spy.
Well, that explains the characters. The gameplay is as simple as I have explained it. But many people like to be greedy, because the game is F2P, and if you're not a P2P player, you can't trade your items. To become the said P2P player, you have to buy something from the Mann Co. Store, or buy the game when it was a paid game. You can also get P2P by buying the computer version of the Orange Box. The game is also a game FILLED with cosmetics. They're not part of the game, and are used to make your character look nicer. If you're still not convinced, there's also a friendly side to the game. If you don't want to be part of the friendly side, that's fine with me. There are many taunts you can do, such as a High Five or Conga.
tl;dr. If you want a good game, you can get it for... $60? $30? $5? No! It's the price of FREE!
I recommend this game to anyone who is bored, and wants to play a good FPS.

Ahh, good ol' Team Fortress 2.
The guns, the maps, the hats... mainly the hats.
As usual, this review is going strip down some elements about TF2 and give my personal view about them.
While the game itself doesn't have a story mode (or an actual single-player mode to be exact) the game's story is lead up from
To save us all some time, I'll just go through the event that started Team Fortress 2.
Here we start out with a man named Zepheniah Mann, the owner of Mann & Sons Munition Concerns/Zepheniah Mann & Sons Co. (Mann Co.). Since Zepheniah Mann was a wealthy man, he purchased Gravel Pits and Dustbowls in which I assume he was looking for materials to sell for more money before ultimately realizing that all the land he bought were useless which was unfortunate for Zepheniah since he pretty much sacrificed his life digging those mines. Zepheniah then became over overwhelmed with a lot of illnesses at a old age. His last will and testament made was to give his two sons, Redmond (RED) and Blutarch (BLU), their own halves of the Gravel Pits and Dustbowl which didn't seemed to appeal towards Remond and Blutarch, making them both hire a group of nine mercenaries to assassinate eachother (but not the mercenaries we know today). Both Redmond and Blutarch when through three groups of nine mercenaries, the first ones being Billy the Kid, Stonewall Jackson, Abraham Lincoln, Alfred Nobel, John Henry, Nikola Tesla, Sigund Freud, Davy Crockett, and Fu Manchu, the second group being the mercenaries from Team Fortress Classic, and the mercenaries we all know today in Team Fortress 2.
I didn't get to all of the story in TF2 (and I'm pretty sure I might've messed up a bit in describing the story) but I highly recommend reading the comics for a better understanding. Personally I say the story is pretty straight forward, its certainly not the most interesting story but for a game that everyone calls Hat Simulator 20xx I'd say the story should be the least of anyone's cares (which IMO is pretty upsetting).
After playing the game for a-bit you begin to realize how casual friendly the game really is, the classes are fairly balanced between eachother and just playing on a server for 2 minutes will give you unique guns designed for certain classes. The game also offers you quite a variety of "generic" gametypes to play on such as Capture the Flag, Capture Points, King of the Hill, etc, and unique gametypes such as Territorial Control (unfortunately there aren't many Territoral Control maps), Mann vs Machine (unique in the stance of gameplay), Robot Destruction, etc. There are also modded gametypes you can play from like Saxton Hale/Freak Fortress, Slender Fortress, Jailbreak, Prophunt, etc. Unfortunately the game does get rather boring after a while of playing (give it around 6-12 months) and keeping touch on the game for a while heavily depends on the player, so not much information I can give on that.
Team Fortress 2 holds a very 3D yet cartoonish artstyle whichh, for some players, this could be a real eye sore to them and can really drag them away from enjoying the gameplay since it IS a First Person Shooter game after all, but for other players the artstyle holds charm that can help them enjoy the game much more. The good part about Team Fortress 2 having cartoonish graphic is that even a lot of low specced computers can run it at a good 60 FPS.
: The soundtrack in TF2, to say the least, is pretty left to right for me. There are just some songs that really have a badass feeling to it, a mediocre/more jolly feeling to it, while the other ones just sound dull and way too situational. I guess in some way I can forgive the dullness and situational... ness... of the soundtrack since this is a war game after all, but this game is too mediocre to have a serious feeling to it.
I think I have a thing for reviewing games with pretty crappy communities. Even for how casual this game stands, many players really take this game straight to the heart as if it were some huge sports event. I mean, the TF2 communities isn't ALL that bad, it's common to find gentle-hearted players that are very forgiving and helpful towards your team unlike most First Person Shooters, but it's just as common to find ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s who bash every little thing you do. Also if you're coming to the game as a Free-to-Play (F2P: Player who hasn't bought anything from the Mann. Co shop yet) then it's going to suck since not many people take F2P's lightly (targetting you only, consisstently bashing you, etc.)
So to wrap this up, I say TF2 is a pretty good/interesting game that anyone who's interested into First Person Shooter's or to anyone who recently just started using Steam should really try to get into.
TL;DR
Story: Pretty Good, need to read comics
Gameplay: Casual
Graphics: Cartoonish 3D artstyle
Soundtrack: 50-50
Community: Varies from good to bad

1 cup sour cream
4 eggs
Directions:
For The base:.
If you're using a dark pan, preheat the oven to 350. If you are using a shiny pan, 375.
Combine the crumbs, melted butter and 3 tbsp sugar well and pat onto the bottom of a 9 inch springform pan. I also like to very very lightly butter the sides of the pan so that the cheesecake will not stick later on.
Bake for 10 mins in your preheated oven and remove. Let it cool while you prepare your batter.
For the batter:.
Make sure everything is at room temperature.
Combine sugar, cheese, flour and vanilla in a big bowl and mix on medium speed till well combined. Don't forget to scrape the bowl as you're doing this.
Mix in the sour cream till its incorporated well. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing well after each addition.
Pour the batter into the springform and let it bake for 1 hour and 10 minutes After the baking time, turn off the oven and leave the door ajar. Let the cake cool in there for about 1 1/2 hours.
Remove the cake and let it cool thoroughly. Refrigerate overnight.
Release the sides of the springform.
Eat.

I've decided to make it an agenda of mine to review every game I've spent a significant amount of time on.
Team Fortress 2 is a relatively balanced online FPS game that has been out for many years and has gained a great amount of new content since then. For many reasons, it offers a very, very different and unique experience from other FPS games out there. There are a wide variety of weaposn to choose from, but they are limited to being used by certain classes, of which there are nine.
The Scout, the Soldier, and the Pyro make up the game's Attack category, meant for combat with simple to use yet highly powerful primary weapons. The Scout moves quickly and is highly agile with a double-barreled shotgun, the Soldier wields a rocket launcher in a game where explosive jumping is taken up to eleven and is official and heavily promoted game mechanic, and the Pyro excells in close-combat, carrying a flamethrower that deals damage quickly and sets enemies on fire, dealing damage over time. It also has the ability to use a strong compression blast which can extinguish burning teammates, and can send projectiles like the Soldier's rockets, as well as enemy players themselves, flying backwards.
The Demoman, the Heavy, and the Engineer make up the game's Defense category. The Demo excells in explosives, carrying a grenade launcher and a stickybomb launcher that utilizes explosives that stick to almost any surface and can be detonated at will. Later on, he would go on to become one of the game's most versatile classes with swords and shields. The swords give him longer melee range among other benefits and shields which give him defensive buffs and a charging ability. The Heavy moves slow, but is strong enough to carry around a gatling gun on his own, along with a shotgun, and can kill his foes with just his bare hands! Finally, the Engineer can build devices for defense and support, including a sentry gun that automatically locks onto enemies in it's sight, a dispenser that restores health and ammo to teammates, and teleporters to help teammates get across the battlefield faster. I would argue that the Demo and Heavy in particular, while very proficent as defensive classes, are also very much capable of offensive combat and are important to have in a push. Of course however, you're free to form your own views and opinions on the game's classes.
The Medic, the Sniper and the Spy make up the game's Support category. The Medic uses a device known as the Medigun to heal his teammates on the battlefield, and it comes with a bonus: When the device reaches 100% charge, you can activate the gun's Ubercharge ability to render yourself and your current patient invulnerable for 8 seconds. The Sniper is exactly what it says on the tin, yet even in this crazy game his presence still makes sense. His purpose in eliminating dangerous targetes from a distance is an important task, and a difficult one to carry out. Finally, the Spy, too, is a class that will pick enemies off, but using stealth instead of range and careful aiming. Getting behind his enemies using a device that turns him invisible, he will then be able to literally stab his foes in the back with a knife, killing them instantly. He also comes equipped with a device that can disable and destory Engineer buildings, a disguise kit that can make him look like any player on the opposing team or even his own, and a revolver.
All of these classes have their own purposes to fulfill in this game, but the important thing to remember is that this game requires communication and teamwork. You can't handle every single fight and situation all on your own.
Apart from gameplay, how does this game aesthetically appeal? Imagine a Pixar-world filled with the same kind of clever humor, but with a more adult and dark-tone to it, and loads of guns, gibs and violence, and finally make it an online FPS. That is the most basic way I can describe TF2. The characters themselves? They're not just classes to play, they're loaded with creative and enjoyable personalities. The Scout is a Boston-born baseball fanatic with a snarky attitude, the Soldier is a very likely insane patriot with an obessesion for war, the Pyro is fittingly a pyromaniac, but also one who sees the world entirely differently than how we see it, and always wearing it's mask and suit, it's identiy is a mystery and nobody can tell what it's saying, it's just mumbling. The Demoman is a black, constantly drunk Scottish man with only one eye, the Heavy is a Russian man who, while intelligent, has a bad grasp on English grammar and loves to shout insults and mockery at his enemies as he guns them down, the Engi is a rather polite (for the most part) Texan and technical-genius, the Medic is an insane medical scientist, the Sniper is a Australian crack shot who can either be very polite or hilariously rude, and the Spy is a total snake who hails from France, and while not out on a killing spree, is a ladies man. There is one thing however, that all these mercenaries share in common: They enjoy killing.
So these are all factors that contribute to why I personally like this game and how it's managed to become such a huge success and remain so today. This game is unlike any other FPS out there. It provides a truly unique gameplay experience, takes full advantage of character personality. What's NOT to love about it?
So even if you aren't an FPS fan, I would still very much recommend trying this game out. It's free to install and play, so you've got nothing to lose. If you do enjoy it, I recommend going premium at some point. Among some other benefits, you'll be able to customize the  appearance of the classes with aesthetic items and get weapons that track your kills.

But... Hackers. We all know Valve can easily patch up hacks like♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or ones that use literally one text file, converted into a readable form by the game. And this goes for all games using VAC. The games are abandoned, Hammer is abandoned, and Valve is only continuing to get worse at stopping what they can easily stop.
Overall, the game is great. The hackers are decently rare, but easy to come across after a bit of time playing. Plus, with vote kick and admins, they can be rid of (temperarily) easily. Valve itself just needs to step up its game, and start updating games, software, and VAC. I will continue to play the game for a long while, and hope for the best when it comes to Valve.

No, make that 3/4s of the steam community plays tf2, and if you haven't already I suggest you go ahead and play. But be warned, tf2 is not what it used to be. It used to be a game that seldom got updates, but when it did it was JAM PACKED with EVERYTHING! New buyable cosmetics, weapons, maps, EVERYTHING! Even mutated loaves of bread! Then... oh god... gun mettle... This is where it all went wrong. There have been 3 semi large updates since gun mettle, and each and every one did the same stupid thing. I'll go ahead and tell you where it went wrong. They added skins. Not so bad, right? Except to get them, you have to spend money on a ticket. Okay, so you buy the ticket, then you get cool skins, right? Not bad... except it's not. You buy the ticket, so you have a CHANCE to find the crates, then you have to buy the $2.50 keys, then open the crates to have around a 3% chance to get a cool skin, otherwise you get a 12 cent piece of garbage. So let's review: buy ticket, wait for crate drop, buy key to crate, unlock crate with key, get bad skin, rage, repeat. They did this over, and over, and over, for the next 3 updates, right now we're on tough break and still with no new weapons. EDIT: Oh wow, new weapons for pyro. About the classes (What can they do?)

TF2 is awesome, and don't you dare to let anyone tell you otherwise! I love the diversity, the teamwork, the learning to play better, the hats, the sillyness and ofcourse the 9 classes and their voicelines. However, there are a few things which I think are confusing to new players and therefore may cause you to dislike the game.
In TF2 you occasionally find a weapon, and sometimes a hat if you are lucky. This is, in my opinion, a great mechanic. More valuable items however can be found opening crates with keys, which cost real life money. Note that the content of the crates never gives a player an advantage over other players, other than looking dashing or intimidating. There are many types of items in TF2.  If you would like to know more about this, I recommend looking for guides on item types and qualities.
If you never did any in-game purchases, you are considered F2P (Free-to-Play). Some people who have spent money on TF2 (P2P, Pay-to-Play) consider themselves better than people who are F2P. This however is complete nonsense. Having bought something in-game unlocks a larger backpack and crafting (more about that later), but does not give an in-game advantage.
If you find a lot of weapons you don't use, you can craft them into scrap metal (considering you are P2P). 3 scrap can be used to craft a reclaimed metal, and 3 reclaimed can be used to craft refined metal (ref). These sorts of metal can be used to craft other weapons and random cosmetics. To learn more about crafting, consult a TF2 wiki.
In game items (like cosmetics, weapons and keys) can be traded with other players. The trading economy of TF2 is very complex. It is very likely you will trade your items for ones "worth less". An item's "worth" is often expressed in amount of keys or amount of refined metal (ref). To know what your items are worth, there are multiple sites to check. I advise watching youtube videos on the subject of TF2 item trading before getting into it.
I hope this helps you with your first steps into TF2, or with deciding if you even want to play this game at all. TF2 might seem confusing at first, but keep in mind that you don't need fancy cosmetics and all the weapons you can possibly get to enjoy the game. If you are interested in trading and crafting it can be fun, but it is most definatly not required to do.
P.S.: I would appreciate it if you let me know what you think of this review ;)

A very fun Valve game, Team Fortress 2 features diverse classes and an even more diverse player base. A wide variety of items for each of the classes allows for an impressive selection of playstyles. The community as a whole is relativly forgiving towards new players and the game's fairly intutive controls also allow anyone familiar with FPS's to get into the game quickly, although certain classes will require much more time in the game to play competently. The backpack paywall system is unfortunate, but not neccessarily a deal killer. Valve's inattention to certain glitchy gameplay mechanics and frequent server lag can also be frustrating, but since the game and Valve's self-sponsered servers are free to play, there is little room to complain. Overall, Team Fortress 2 is a great game with a strong and thriving community, and with Valve releasing steady updates, this game will likely remain a favourite of many people across the world for awhile.

Really solid game in every way. The core game is fun and well-balanced despite the huge difference throughout the 9 classes. The content is sprawling; so many maps, so many items, and many different modes to play, not to mention surf maps, dodgeball maps, jump maps. The skills development is great; several classes excellent for beginners, many classes excellent to master. The business model is the best there is: microtransactions for vanity items only, free to play otherwise. Absolutely everything that affects the gameplay is available freely, and not behind some obnoxious grind; new weapons just come at a steady pace. Fast enough to not feel like you're being patronised, slow enough to still leave you hanging for something in particular you might have your eye on. Many vanity items can be crafted (which is a grind), while many cannot and require real money to get put into a rares/unboxing system. This is also done well, and it's just a great system all round. And the only reason it works as a business model, despite absolutely everything that involves gameplay being free, is because the game itself is simply that good and popular that people want to put money into hats and strange weapon visuals.
But what I really like most about TF2 is its character. There is *so much* dialog in the game. You'll hear the characters saying funny things pretty much constantly, but it's not in your face, and after 1000 hours I'm still hearing new cracks from the characters. The scout is hilarious, heavy is cute in a massive Russian kind of way (if you've been firing for say 30 seconds without stopping, he'll start singing). The spy might sarcastically ask a solider he just killed "How ever will they replace you?", while the soldier himself is just funny in his low intelligence. Once I have heard him singing about his ex-roommate, which is just so amusing. Wtf are you doing singing, soldier?
Speaking of his ex-roommate, that's Merasmus. So what? Lore. TF2 does *not* take itself seriously, but it has so much lore it's fantastic to see it clicking together as time passes. The Source movies you'll find on Youtube are oozing with history, and their little touches result in updates in the game, like the scar on the Sniper's cheek, the entirety of Pyrovision, bread appearing in teleporters, or the Scout mentioning his bucket of chicken. Even better, the comics. TF2 has comics and damn, they are good. I don't even get into comics, but the ironic humour and characterisation is just so good. I know I'm meant to be writing about the game here, but TF2's comic is seriously one of the best comics out there. Probably. I'm no expert.
Also really good music. Not stuff you'd sit and listen too, but really good for the game's character and well produced.
There's more I could say but the short of it is that TF2 is so commonplace that its easy to understate how good it is. It's just really, really solid. Core gameplay: solid, gameplay variety: huge, content: abundant, character and lore: amazing, business model: perfect. It won't blow you away visually these days, but TF2 is easily one of my most respected games.

: 9 years after release, the game has more bugs than ever. Taunt glitches, spazzing ragdolls, symbols over player's heads that will get you killed (mini crit vulnerability symbol staying over player's heads is an example), buildings that are infinitely sapped, sappers remaining on unsapped buildings, players glitching outside of the map, the list goes on and on.
: Got that expensive rig with i5 processor and GTX970? Well, too bad, because this game runs like the average modern console port (while looking bad). Framerates surf between 40 and 150 with a period of 1-2 seconds. An enemy player that's on fire? Good luck hitting him. He'll lag your game so hard that your damage output for weapons like the minigun is halved.
:
- Directx 8 was obsolete 5 years before the game was even released, but yet it's still included out of sheer laziness.
-The server browser is equally lazy and is completely obnoxious to use.
-Want to use the custom server browser? Good, you only see ping, mapname and the number of people on the server. Valve never figured out that they can put "maptime left" on the list.
-And of course the best part about the game: the hitboxes and the "lag compensation". If you played sniper for a period of time, you'll notice that you don't LEAD the target, but shoot somewhere random behind it.
-Want to play pyro? Good luck with that. They managed to ♥♥♥♥ that up too. The phlog only hits the player from certain angles, even when he's engulfed in flames.
-Want to play heavy? Pray that there's never an enemy hugging you. You literally can't hit him if he's inside of your minigun.
-See that enemy running up the stairs? Don't shoot rockets at him, because they will be absorbed by random clutter, dealing no damage to enemies.
-Want to play demoknight? Good luck with that. You can't damage enemies that are in each other and "ghost hits" (hits where you get the sound of meat getting hit, but do no damage) are everywhere. I even get ghost hits on heavies that are standing perfectly still.
-Communities are free to spam ads or even inject malicious code through people running the game and connecting to their servers.
-The most recent fad: engineers going outside of the map and building sentries that can shoot people, while being protected by the invisible walls around the map. Jolly good fun and still not fixed after more than a month.
-Want to call a vote on that cheater? Enjoy the coinflip, because your team clearly doesn't care enough to press F1 or F2. That is, if the vote window actually shows up of course! Want to know the result? Too bad, you only occasionally get the "yes" or "no" displayed, and you most certainly won't see the actual number of votes for each choice. Excellent design!
-Is there a team that's clearly much worse than the other one? Too bad. Only the players with few points get "funbalanced" to that team. The actual players causing the imbalance stay on the other team.
: GET GOOD GET MEMEBOX (yes they censored the actual word, probably afraid of bad reviews) spam, coming from heavies hitting every bullet while jumping in the air. This is still a thing. A sniper doing 5 headshot kills in 5 seconds. This is also a thing. These are the obvious ones that VAC can't even detect. Then there's the pyros with auto deflect scripts, aim assist snipers, aim assist spies, etc. Of course these are way harder to spot, but they exist. Valve never figured out that they can check Heavy accuracy and flag suspicious players, or snipers by monitoring damage output.
: The recent past has shown several weapon stat changes that are utterly dumb. The phlog user was made invincible, the babyface blaster was rendered worthless, afterburn immunity of the demoknight shields completely void, ... The priorities are clearly on minimum effort and maximum profit. While this is a noble corporate strategy, it is, again, utterly dumb on the long run. Want to make or edit a map? After a 5-month Hiatus, I return to this game.
The release of Matchmaking has brough new life to this once considered to be dying game. Even casual pubs have felt a new breath of life, as teamwork returns to Team Fortress 2. Even in casual, communication has returned from trash-talk to tactical assessments. Sentry around the corner? A teammate will likely have tried to warn you. Enemy has full Uber? Someone will call it out.
Teammates now make active efforts to push and retreat as a group. Teammates protect their medics now. Very few cases emerge now of more than 2-3 of a single class, and with the newfound class diversity in this update, a push made of mostly the same class will usually fail miserably.
The community has restored my faith in it. Now with Matchmaking, many complaints I had about the community have all but died. People work together and cooperate now. People congratulate their teammates and their enemies for good performance. The game's sense of good sportsmanship has been revived like I have never seen before in any online community.
Furthermore, in the recently released Comp update, many performance issues were resolved. Even on my integrated GPU, my framerate rarely dives below 50, and I'm not even using a graphics config. Connection issues, however, cannot be fixed by developers. It's entirely on the ISP package you are using (which coming from a dying town means that I constantly get frustrating scenes of rubber-banding, but that cannot be helped until I move out).
Meet Your Match has revived this game like no update before has, despite what naysayers have claimed. Some say this update was made to compete with Overwatch, some say it was in the works since before OW's announcement. Regardless, this game in its current state is far more appealing to me, and for free, no less.
The balancing between free and premium players is almost unnoticeable. All free players have the same opportunities to obtain weapons and skills that the premium players have. The only real difference between a free to play and a premium is how much money they've sunk into this game. Cosmetic items are about the limitation to the benefits of purchasing items. However, bear in mind that statistically speaking, premium players will have been playing for longer and will likely have considerably more skill than a F2P, but this is merely due to dedication to the game.
This game, simply put, is a must-have for all Steam users, and a whopping $0.00 price tag, who can say no? Whether you find enjoyment or not in it is your choice, but I will be playing this game for months, possibly years to come. And hell, why should I not? It's a damn good game at that.

Team. Fortress. 2. Not only is it one of my favorite games of all time it is my favorite FPS AND it's the 3rd most played game on Steam.
So what do I like about this game? Well it's the first game I ever played on Steam, the gameplay is fantastic, the community is fun, the classes are all loveable and memorable, and besides the purely cosmetic microtransactions, it is 100% Free to Play.
Why am I even talking about how great it is? Go get the game and see for yourself.
But for those who want to know in detail and are sceptical let me fill you in.
Story: While there isn't really a story, there are online comics on the official site that explain the backstory and continuation of the RED and BLU's feud over the Badlands.
Presentation: For a game that came out in 2007, it still holds up today. What I really like is the 60's cartoon style they gave this game, the environments in the game are well done and they fit in with the rest of the game. The Classes are amazing, everyone has a distinct, and likeable personality, from Scout's cockyness, to Soldier's patriotism, to Medic's Insanity.
Gameplay: This is what makes the game hold up with the likes of CS:GO and Dota 2 even today, without going into too much detail I can say this: Every Gamemode and Map feels fun and unique and I still play them(Except for Hydro).  What makes the game not get any old is the fact that Valve keeps updating the game with new weapons, maps, gameplay balances, etc. They keep the game fresh and new so it doesn't get stale. Every single class is fun to play, but you will have a favorite to least favorite list, and of course the one thing everyone wants, hats!
Final Verdict: 9/10
Pros:
- The Art Style is unique
- The game is Free to Play
- There's always something new every time you play it
- The Classes are funny and fun to play with
- The community is fantastic
Cons(Mostly Nitpicks):
- Some classes like Demo and Spy are hard to master
- If your looking for a hat that's unusual, then prepare your wallet to be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
